### Introduction of the Ra'avad, of blessed memory

The path of life leads upward for the wise <note>A quote from Proverbs 15:24</note>, for there is no excuse when you are taken to your border and when you understand your house as if you are inside it, to see the shrouds for the pure and the destruction of the congealed memories of the heathens. Know that for him, there is a birth and the number of your days is great. The knowledge of God is thus found in the generations, and the count of your days is like streams. It is known that you have sustained a portion of the fire; a "portion of the face" <note>An idiom for personal attention or favor</note> in your eyes is like yesterday. If so, these days are seventeen thousand years <note>original: "iz alapim"</note>. All of this is hinted at in the "exalted" letters of the calculation of eighty-two, and the number of your days is two hundred and nine <note>Based on Gematria, the Hebrew system of assigning numerical values to letters</note>. Up to three hundred and sixty, they equal the <term>Gematria<note>The kabbalistic method of interpreting words based on their numerical value.</note></term> of one thousand and twelve—meaning twelve thousand years of the cycles of **Snow** <note>original: "SLG" (Sheleg). In this mystical context, snow represents the cooling or crystallization of divine energy.</note> to make known that even in the **Attribute of Mercy** <note>original: "Midat HaChesed" — the divine quality of benevolence</note> there is a mixture of **Judgment** <note>original: "Din" — the divine quality of severity and law</note>, for it has the cycles of **Snow**.

Know that there are sixty types of **Snow**. One of them is the "division of every tree," and we shall remove the burdens and they shall be dismantled... and they were the ascent of the congealed as our kings, and their motion is like congealed milk. There is "lacking snow" which is like the appearance of the points of the sunrise and from the forces of the horn... in the place of lack, and they shall be sanctified. There are some of them that return to establish the "Pered" <note>original: "Pered" (mule/division) — perhaps a reference to the four levels of interpretation: Peshat, Remez, Derash, Sod</note>, and some that return to deviate as **Snow**. All of them rise from the earth to the canopy in the air, covering all the **Mercy** that acts upon them. Outside the Land, the vapors rising from the water and the earth are like the clouds called "Great All," and they themselves are acted upon to be the storehouses of **Snow** and the cycles of **Hail** <note>original: "KLD" (Barad). Hail represents a more severe, solidified form of Judgment than snow.</note>.

With these, the Holy One, blessed be He, takes vengeance upon the wicked, as when He "withholds His covering for the time of distress, for the day of battle and war" <note>A reference to Job 38:23</note>. For with stones of hail <note>original: "Avnei Barad"</note> He took vengeance against Pharaoh, and against the kings of the Land of Israel in the days of Joshua. So too, every single day, there is payment from the wicked, from "Halem" <note>a mystical term</note> to **Snow** and from "Haleg" to "them." Thus, the exchanges shall be cut off and the clouds shall end. They shall return to be as the book of Amos says: "under the soles of the feet" of the congealed <note>foundations</note>. For when their wickedness is upon them, they shall be "ashes under the soles of the feet" of the congealed. For it is reversed, and "the clay becomes as the seal" <note>A reference to Job 38:14</note>.

And the sound of the **Snow** beneath the **Throne of Glory** <note>original: "Kise HaKavod"</note> comes from the powers of the cycles of **Snow** and the cycles of **Hail**. This is the offspring, and later it is written: "this is the translation," and the clay is for the **Mercy** of the world... "He sends forth His snow like wool" <note>original: "kurtolei talga"</note>; "He scatters the frost like ashes" <note>original: "kedra tachmei"</note>. And in His cold, the cycles of **Hail** are the "mortgage" <note>A legal/mystical term for a debt or guarantee</note>, in the language of the wise...

<margin>
This means the congealing stands and we are tested by it and by the frost. For by this scripture, He takes vengeance upon the wicked; when He withholds His covering for the time of distress, for the day of battle and war. And the translation of "He gives snow like wool" is to awaken the cry of their children. And their frost for the day of battle, for Pharaoh and his groups... and it is necessary for all the paths to be in a circle within the **Sephira of Malchut** <note>The final Divine Emanation, representing Sovereignty and the physical world.</note> corresponding to the "fatty parts" <note>original: "Chalvei" — referring to the fats of the sacrifices or the "milky" white light of mercy</note> of the Tabernacle, and there they are... and 17 portions.
</margin>

# Introduction of the Ra'avad, of blessed memory

<warning>There is a brown liquid stain in the upper-middle section of the page, obscuring a few words in the first paragraph.</warning>

Let us return to observing the "Table" <note>The "Table" here refers to the structured arrangement of the physical and spiritual worlds.</note> and its order. As it is said, "the waters shall become wise." This is the explanation of the waters that surround the essences of the firmaments; during their formation, they exist in the ground, and then they return to their previous state through pressure. Out of their coagulation, they are supported and fixed into the shape of the firmaments and the structure of the **Heavenly Host** <term>Pamalia shel Ma'ala<note>The divine "entourage" or assembly of angels that governs the natural order.</note></term>. It is already known that those who "lick" <note>likely an OCR error for "those who walk"</note> in the heart of the sea... and also the letters regarding the "bricks" of ice, as we have learned elsewhere: "He turned them into bricks," <note>original: "shavi l'veinim"</note> which are concepts that will be discussed later. Behold, the waters within the ice are examined and squeezed into existence, and once they depart, the sources are joined to the "inner faces," <note>original: "panim"</note> moving and hardening into possessions. Behold: **the freezer** (a), **the frost** (b), **the snow** (c), **the ice-block** (d), **the rain** (e), and **the hail** (f)—all of these are species <unclear>of them</unclear>. These are the "Ten" <note>Referencing the ten Sephirot or divine emanations</note> which are tested through the pressure of the water. This is the meaning of "Can you bind the chains of the Pleiades <note>original: Kimah</note> or loose the cords of Orion <note>original: Kesil</note>?" <note>A quote from Job 38:31</note>.

Know that **Kimah** <note>The Pleiades constellation</note> is a name for a solid substance formed by the power of binding on the side of the water. Therefore, it possesses great coldness. Because of the moisture of the rainwater found in Kimah, it binds the fruits. Every wise person will understand the word: "chains" <note>original: ma'adanot</note> means a knot or a bond, for it binds all separated things and makes them into a single fluid.

**Kesil** <note>The constellation Orion</note> comes from the side of **Strength** <term>Gevurah<note>The divine attribute of Judgment, Power, and Restriction.</note></term>, and therefore there is great heat within it. Out of the heat of Orion, the fruits are ripened and opened. If so, "the cords of Orion you shall open." And there are "chains of the Pleiades"—meaning, can you stop the fruits associated with Pleiades from resting, or the small ones from being poured out? For in His great kindness, He joins together to restore everything, and from the rain, the fruits and the righteous are benefited. Whereas Orion is specifically designated to ripen the fruits and to purify the changes until they are made... <note>The text here becomes highly elliptical/symbolic</note>. Therefore, out of the accompaniment of all the souls, you can "loosen the cords of Orion," for you are able to untie them. Behold, Pleiades is that which binds all accidental matter, plants, and joints; it is the binder. Orion, however, is that which melts, cuts off, and consumes.

Thus, the "chains" <note>or "delights"</note> are attributed to Pleiades because it provides the "delights of a king." But Orion "draws" its strength and gives things even in judgment and law. This is what you should consider: how far the wisdom of the Founder reached regarding His secret. He placed it in a row and associated Orion with the **Scorpion** <note>The zodiac sign Scorpio</note>. You already know the secret of the twelve essences and the thirty-two constellations. Since Orion's place is in the **Strength** <note>Gevurah</note> of the "Dragon," <term>Teli<note>The "Teli" is a mystical concept in the Sefer Yetzirah, often interpreted as the axis of the universe or the constellation Draco, which directs the movements of the spheres.</note></term> in the path of the "hollow and bitter," gold comes from it... a trust in materiality. Therefore, the distance of the star called Orion is toward the south... and it "kills the camels" if they follow it.

Regarding "the chains of the Pleiades," the **Aramaic Translation** <term>Targum<note>The ancient Aramaic translation of the Bible.</note></term> says: "The knots of the cluster of Pleiades." <note>original: "katrei moleh"</note>... and for "the cords of Orion you shall open," they translate Orion as "the giant" <note>original: "nephila"</note> in the language of the Talmud.

There is also in "the chains of the Pleiades" the weight of the Upper Essences which hover over the path of the **Dragon** <note>Teli</note>... and behold, the one born of matter, his soul follows the paths of the spheres. Therefore, "the cords of Orion you shall open" refers to those supported by the "tail of the Dragon" and the five essences below. For the five essences are the upper ones in form... and in kindness, the world is called out of all judgment. The influence of Pleiades is numbered from the **Supreme Crown** <term>Keter Elyon<note>The highest of the Sephirot, representing the Divine Will.</note></term>... to renew the worlds. It is a "face" <note>Partzuf</note> that participates in it, for it is like a "mother hen" <note>A traditional Jewish identification for the Pleiades cluster</note> that takes the moisture... and all pass through the judgment and law of the Above. This is the meaning of the Targum: "The knots of the cluster."

The Ra'avad links these celestial bodies to the "Teli" (cosmic axis) and the transformative states of water, ice, and snow.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the Ra'avad’s cosmological discourse. While the previous page discussed the soul and the "cycles of snow" as a manifestation of the Attribute of Mercy, this page shifts to a physical and mystical analysis of the elements—specifically how water transforms into ice, snow, and rain through the influence of the divine attributes (Sefirot) and the scriptural descriptions found in the Book of Job.</meta>

# Introduction of the Ra'avad, of blessed memory

He portioned out for good; do not spare the paths he brought up on high. And "who divided paths for the clouds," <note>original: "mi phileg netivot le-ananim"</note> observing the waters in the sounds, and their height toward the bolts of the firmaments and in the depths. And "there is He who divided a channel for the overflowing water" <note>Job 38:25</note>; who divided channels and paths for the flood, which comes from the attribute of **Lovingkindness** <term>Chesed; the divine attribute of expansive benevolence</term>. Some of these paths are drawn toward every living species and every individual detail of the fundamental elements, and some are drawn toward the explanations for the scripture concerning the "striking of waters": for frozen waters, for hot waters, for salty ones, for surplus waters, and for salt-sea waters.

He also divided the paths that are drawn from the attribute of **Severity** <term>Gevurah; the divine attribute of judgment, restraint, and power</term> toward the inner realms. For Severity is like the winter lightning in its freezing clarity, seen in its numerical value as two paths. Some are drawn toward the foundation <note>the element of Yesod</note> and some are drawn toward the transformations. And this is the Aramaic translation of the verse: "Who prepared and leveled the path for the flood to descend from above, and a path for the sound of the thunder's lightning." <note>original Aramaic: "tatar'ges ve-chamar..."</note> Because the waters are influenced by the power of Lovingkindness, while the great saltiness comes from the side of Severity, it is from this interaction that the sound of thunder and lightning is produced. "And who divided a channel for the overflowing water"—as if to say: "I have created many hairs, and each and every hair has its own follicle and is written by itself; for if even two hairs were to draw from a single follicle, they would destroy and darken the eye of a man." <note>This is a famous Talmudic teaching from Bava Batra 16a, where God explains the precision of creation to Job.</note> And regarding "a way for the lightning": "I have created many drops in the thick cloud, and each and every drop has its own perforation and is sent out by itself; for if even two drops were to descend from a single perforation, they would wash away the entire world." Similarly, "I have created many lightnings, and for each and every lightning I created its own path; for if two lightnings were to emerge from one place, they would destroy the entire world." All these were made with Knowledge, Understanding, and Wisdom, so that it might be "on the earth, where no man is; on the wilderness, wherein there is no man" <note>Job 38:26</note>.

Those "windows" and "wildernesses" that were hidden at their creation from human beings—I have protected them <note>The Hebrew root "chasiti" is interpreted here as protection or concealment</note>, meaning the power of the strength for human beings; and for their life, I have blotted out the [harsh] threads for the wise of the "enclosure" <note>original: "machtur"</note> so as to elevate them toward Lovingkindness and toward humanity. And this is its translation: "To bring rain upon the land where there is no man, and the wilderness wherein there is no son of man." "To satisfy the desolate and waste ground; and to cause the bud of the tender herb to spring forth" <note>Job 38:27</note>. It is known that the "desolate and waste" are prepared for the wicked, but the dew of light shall be lost like the perfect, and the wicked shall be removed when it comes. For a moment, their forgiveness is spoken of in a place of glory, a good rule, and do not let it be in trial here, as is the way with "him," and "all of them like a wasteland where no man passed and no man dwelt there." Therefore, He causes it to rain upon all the earth to satisfy the most vigorous of all species and to cause the source of the grasses to sprout; and through them, they shall be elevated from the plant to the living, to the [celestial] spheres, to the angels, and to the constellations. Therefore the Aramaic translation says: "To satisfy the parched and thirsty land, and to make the buds of the grass grow." For satisfying the creatures of the earth is for the purpose of elevating the plants.

"Hath the rain a father?" <note>Job 38:28</note>. The explanation is that the rain which descends comes from the Lovingkindness of the Lord and His Severity. Its substance and the goodness of its spirit—this is water. And all of these are examined from the power of **Wisdom** <term>Chokhmah; the first flash of divine intellect</term> which is in its frozen heights, a sea on the right.

"Or who hath begotten the drops of dew?" <note>Job 38:28</note>. For the rain descends by weight, but the drops of dew are born through the power of **Understanding** <term>Binah; the analytical or maternal aspect of divine intellect</term> that is within Lovingkindness. "And may God give thee from the dew of the heavens." Therefore the Aramaic translates: "Is there a father for the rain? Or who begot the droplets of the dew?"

"Out of whose womb came the ice?" <note>Job 38:29</note> "And the hoary frost of heaven, who hath gendered it?" The explanation is that from the power of the **Crown** <term>Atarah; often referring to the Sefirah of Malchut (Kingship) as it receives from above</term>, in which is the Understanding that is in the clarity of the Lord, the ice comes—like the appearance of a terrible ice-crystal. From it, the firmaments were formed, rising to the level of the "frozen ones." Behold, their secret is the frost, and the secret of "crystal" and "flour" <note>possible reference to the white appearance of frost</note>. The Lovingkindness touches the matter of the dew, but it is not included in the "Back" <note>Gevurah/Severity</note>, for not all of its blessing was congealed. The translation says: "From whose womb did the ice come out? And the frost of the heavens, who gave birth to it?"

<summary>The Ra'avad provides a mystical commentary on Job 38, explaining how rain, dew, ice, and lightning are governed by specific Sefirot (divine attributes). He emphasizes the precision of creation, noting that every hair and raindrop has its own unique path to prevent the destruction of the world.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the Ra'avad’s mystical introduction, moving from the cosmological movements of the heavens to the internal "heavens" of the human soul and body. # Introduction of the Ra'avad, of blessed memory

Regarding the soul, whose beginning is in the firmaments <note>original: "beraqim"—likely a transcription error for "reqi'im" (firmaments)</note>, let them go and learn, for they have understood you. Every bride is perfected and known; how she shall serve and be taught for His love. And "know My Name," for they called My Name "to the Lord," <note>original: "l'Hashem"</note> meaning "God," for he knew My Name in the **Secret of Knowledge** <term>Sod ha-Da'at; the mystical bridge between the upper and lower intellects</term> <gloss>Tiferet</gloss>. 
Observe the glory of my father, and my sigh is with him—the wise of the soul—to solve the arrangement of the firmaments, that they should dwell and watch over you. "Who has put wisdom in the inward parts? Or who has given understanding to the heart?" <note>Job 38:36</note>. The explanation is: "Who has put in the kidneys," which are the covered parts <note>original: "tuchot"</note> and the secret of **Wisdom** <term>Chokhmah; the first spark of divine intellect</term>, for the kidneys provide counsel to a person. "Who has given to the heart" <gloss>Tiferet</gloss> "that which joins with **Understanding**" <term>Binah; the analytical faculty of the divine intellect</term>. For the Lord, we are crowned and prayed to, those who receive from Understanding. 

It is known that the "pocket" <note>likely referring to the vessel or containment</note>, the place for all things, is composed of branches. There, the sensation is greatest, for the Sustainer is not divided from the portion called the "Tree" by way of the paths called "branches." Regarding this secret, it is said: "I will bless the Lord who has given me counsel; my kidneys also instruct me in the night seasons" <note>Psalm 16:7</note>. Because Wisdom requires arrangement in its existence and is related to physical action, therefore all Wisdom and Understanding are "simple intellects," and **Counsel** <note>Etzah</note> is what introduces order into Wisdom and Understanding until it reaches physical action. This is the secret of "With the Lord" <gloss>Binah</gloss> "He took counsel, and He instructed Him" <note>Isaiah 40:14</note>. 

The reason for this is that the intellects are surrounded on every side like salt <note>perhaps referring to preservation or permeation</note> and are sealed within them. Therefore, they are called *Tuchot* (inward parts), which means "covered," from the language of "plastering a house" <note>Hebrew: "tach et ha-bayit"</note>. Regarding this secret, it hinted and said: "Who <note>original: "Mi"—a mystical name for the attribute of Binah</note> has put wisdom in the inward parts?" for the star is called "Who," as it is said, "With whom <note>Mi</note> did He take counsel, that he might instruct Him?" She receives from the sparks of Wisdom and spreads through the "harp" <note>likely a metaphor for the heart or the Sefirah of Yesod</note> toward the inward parts the flow of Wisdom that comes upon it. "Or who gave understanding to the rooster?" <note>Job 38:36</note>, providing fruit to the **Foundation of the World** <term>Yesod; the attribute of generation and connection</term>, and Understanding to the order of the **Kingdom** <term>Malkhut; the final attribute, representing the manifest world</term>. From them, Wisdom exists in the kidneys, and is refined for Understanding <gloss>Atarah/The Crown</gloss>. 

Know that the power of procreation has three centers: the **Brain** for the seed, the **Heart** for the spirit, and the **Liver** for the boundary <note>likely referring to the physical maintenance/nutrients</note>. From there, the liver sends the power of the boundary to the kidneys, and it flows through the kidneys. After the power of the kidneys has been explained to you, and the transformations of the boundary which "cooks" <note>metabolizes or prepares</note> through the action of the "three thirties" <note>a cryptic reference to mystical numerical divisions</note> toward male and female; and because the "cooking" is drawn from **Knowledge** <note>Da'at</note> in the heart, it is therefore said: "And Adam knew Eve his wife" <note>Genesis 4:1</note>. Behold, through their action in the "branch" of the kidneys, in the action of the "Root" which arouses nature and Wisdom, etc. This is because, in the value of the kidneys, they receive from everything that is above them; they are the sources of reception for the **Crown** <note>Atarah/Malkhut</note>, and thus the soul is born, which is included from "Being" <note>Yesh</note>.

There is also one "Who put wisdom in the inward parts (the kidneys)," or "Who gave the rooster <note>original: "sekwi"</note> understanding" to distinguish between day <gloss>Tiferet</gloss> and night <gloss>Atarah</gloss>. Know that just as there are four seasons <note>Tekufot</note> in the year through the movement of the sun, so too there are four seasons in the kidneys and in the movement of the day. Just as the sun is prevented from returning from the four corners... the Will, in its daily movement, when it moves to encompass these four corners, creates a "season." This is the secret: the four corners are between the divisions of the night and the twilight of the day, and in the middle of the night and the middle of the day. Behold, in these four times—and the time of each and every one of these—the **Heavenly Host** <term>Pamalia shel Ma'ala; the celestial retinue of angels</term> returns each to the labor they were made to do. 

Therefore, when the "understanding" of one of these four times reaches the spirit of the rooster—whose root is in the Foundation of the World—it understands the strike of its root. Immediately, it claps its wings like its root and gives strength to the intellect. It stands at the time they are receiving dominion, each one an official over his labor. Therefore, the Masters of the Talmud, when they wished to punish a person, would act at these known times, as is explained in **Tractate Berakhot** <note>a volume of the Talmud dealing with prayers and blessings</note>. 

And behold, I will tell you one story in the Holy Tongue, where the name of the deed is mentioned: a certain heretic <note>original: "min"</note> used to trouble **Rabbi Joshua ben Levi** excessively. The Rabbi set his mind to punish him. He tied a rooster to the leg of his bed and watched it, waiting for the hour of the "oath" <note>the specific moment of divine judgment, when the rooster's comb turns white</note>...

It explains the spiritual significance of the rooster as a creature that perceives cosmic "seasons" or turning points throughout the day, concluding with a Talmudic story about using these spiritual timings.</summary>

# This is the Introduction of the Ra’avad, of blessed memory

This is according to the path of
the Torah, according to the limit of the time of their standing. And it says: "Do you know the laws of the heavens?" Why? Because if you knew

the revealed world on the earth <gloss>The Crown</gloss>. For it is possible that by knowing the decree of the heavens, you will not compare the dominion of the "revolutions" <term>Gilgulim; the cycles of the celestial spheres or the transmigration of souls</term> 
upon the earth <gloss>The Crown</gloss>. For by the way of their revolution, their decree is strengthened and gathered to be high and low,
and the sunken rises, and thus all of them. "Can you lift up your voice to the clouds?" <gloss>The Crown</gloss> <note>Job 38:34</note>. Why is this written at the beginning?
When you lift up your voice <gloss>The Crown</gloss> to the cloud <note>the source of emanation</note>, the flow of water—and they appear to you from Kindness—
by the request for water for the ways of the Crown. And the explanation of "lifting up": when the connection is lifted <gloss>The Crown</gloss> as it is written
<gloss>Beauty</gloss> "behold, a spirit for him" <gloss>Beauty</gloss>. "Lift up your voice to praise," and the flow of water will turn toward you. 
"Will the lightning bolts go" <note>Job 38:35</note> in the firmament from the side of **Strength** <term>Gevurah; the Sefirah of judgment and restriction</term>, and they will go to the place where they are completed. And they shall say to you: "Here we are," ready to do 
your will. From the side of the heavens, for from here they enter the righteous ones. And the secret of the Three is handed over—
the keys to water, the keys to birth. And it is because of this he had the power to inform you: that if a person does not know the laws of 
heaven and earth, who is appointed from the entities over the water, and who is appointed from the entities over the land, and so on 
regarding all the laws of the heavens, he will not be able to guide the power that is over the land. As it is written: "Do you know the laws of 
heavens? Can you establish their dominion on the earth?" Or: "Can you lift up your voice to the clouds?" This is the abundance of water, meaning a multitude of water.

<meta>This page continues the Ra'avad’s mystical introduction, specifically exploring the "Sod Ha-Tinnur" (The Secret of the Oven/Cycle) and how divine justice is mirrored in the natural world through the food chain and the transmigration of souls.</meta>

# Introduction of the Ra’avad, of blessed memory

**Strengthen yourself:** Interpretation of "The World" <gloss>original: Atarah; the Sefirah of Kingship</gloss>. They were created through His thought <gloss>original: Tiferet; the Sefirah of Beauty</gloss>. For just as in the thought of the Writing and the Crown—the General Teacher—the **Greatness** <term>Chesed; Loving-kindness</term> and **Might** <term>Gevurah; Strength</term> are found in potential, in the "Point" <note>likely referring to the Primordial Point or Keter</note> and the **Foundation** <term>Yesod</term>, as they are cleaved there.

Likewise, we find in the chapter of the "Heifer whose neck is broken" <note>Deuteronomy 21, a ritual for an unsolved murder</note>, in the scroll of the *Sotah* <note>the ritual for a woman suspected of adultery</note>, and in the "Salt of the bread of a slain man," that a person's "matter" <note>thought or spiritual essence</note> might be in one place while their body is in another. A person's thought leads the body, like a rope leads the hoof <note>original: Parsas; often used in this text to refer to the boundary of the physical realm or the Sefirah of Kingship</note>, for the primary root of the body is from the "Hoof" <gloss>Atarah</gloss>. Alternatively, the thought leads the "Hoof" to the rest of the body, for its primary root is from the Heart <gloss>Tiferet</gloss>. 

From the "Salt of his choosers" <note>difficult phrase; likely referring to divine selection</note> to test and examine—the translation of "chosen" is "selected"—why did He allow all these elements of "dust" <note>materiality</note> to sustain the "Wise One" <note>the soul</note>? 

Consider this: Just as a mortal king requires "Wise Men of Kindness and Mercy" for the administration of the kingdom's subjects, and also requires "Wise Men of Might," warriors, and merchants for the "Foundation of the Hoof" <note>the infrastructure and defense of the realm</note>, and through this his kingdom is established; **so too in the Upper Order.** The King who guides the world requires the Attribute of **Kindness** and **Mercy** to do good for all those close to Him through the beautiful ways of the Kingdom. Yet He also requires the Attribute of "Merchants" <note>referring to those who manage "exchange" or trade</note> and the Attribute of **Death** and **Punishment** to discipline those who rebel against the King’s decree. 

Just as with a mortal king, some are granted a life of ease and luxury, with their needs provided for from the King's house. Some eat at his table, some from the royal stores, some from the city, some from the village, some from the fields and vineyards—and some are sustained from the "fines" paid by those who transgress the King's law. 

So it is in the place of the **Supreme King** <gloss>Tiferet</gloss>. Therefore, He created human beings and every "Person" <note>likely referring to the 'faces' in Ezekiel's vision</note>: the **Face of the Lion** representing all pure and impure wild beasts; the **Face of the Ox** representing all domestic animals; and the **Face of the Eagle** representing all pure and impure birds. 

Among the birds and beasts, some are sustained by prepared food, and some are sustained by "theft" <note>predation</note>, such as lions, leopards, and wolves. If there were no "fined ones" <note>those being punished</note> among the transgressors of the King's law, His kingdom would not be established. Similarly, if there were no predatory beasts to seize [the transgressors], the Kingdom would not be sustained. 

This is the secret of what our Sages of blessed memory said: *"No wild beast overcomes a man unless he appears to it like a beast"* <note>Babylonian Talmud, Shabbat 151b</note>. This means that when the awe of the Name [God] is removed from him, the "Awe of God" departs from the predators, and he is consequently abandoned to all.

Know that all the Works of Creation follow the "Law of Exchange" <term>Kavvei Halof; a Kabbalistic term for the transmigration of souls or the recycling of energy</term>. Some change through eating and procreation, and some through perfection. Therefore, everything consumed is divided according to this Law of Exchange. This is the **Secret of the Oven** <term>Sod Ha-Tinnur; refers to the "re-firing" or recycling of souls in the afterlife or through reincarnation</term>.

The interpretation of *"He goes about to hunt prey"* <note>cf. Job 38:39</note> is that he [the predator] must pursue it until he brings the prey to the species destined to eat it, according to what is fitting for both the eater and the eaten. "Prey" refers to food, as in *"The young lions roar for their prey"* <note>Psalm 104:21</note>. The food of the lions will be "filled"—meaning it will suffice to provide for them according to the "Law of Exchange" between the eater and the eaten. 

All this is written as truth and justice. Regarding "sustenance," the translation is "scattered" <note>Aramaic: chafzar</note>, for you shall dwell to provide the animal its food and sustenance. *"They crouch in their dens and lie in wait in the thicket"* <note>Job 38:40</note>. They satisfy their high stature in their dwellings—meaning in their dens—where they lie and wait. When they sit in the thicket of the woods and forests, they direct their entire consciousness to destroy their prey. This is translated as: *"They lie in their dwellings to ambush their food."*

For the sake of "shattering the souls," they are enclosed and hidden in these dwellings. This is the "Law of Exchange," where the "Face of Man" is turned to the "Face of Edom" <note>likely referring to a soul falling from a human level to a lower or more animalistic state</note>. Behold, the soul that is now "woven" <note>trapped</note> in the lion’s den longs for the "thicket" <note>the security of its source</note> and for the "house" which it once chose. Its soul is shattered because of its "harlotry" <note>sinful deviations</note>, and therefore it is "caught in the net" to be destroyed. Perhaps there is some benefit in the soul being preyed upon or eaten by animals, for through the act of being eaten, the soul reaches an "elevation." If the eating is done in purity, it achieves a higher level through pure things. If the eating is inferior...

<meta>This page continues the Ra'avad’s mystical introduction. # Introduction of the Ra’avad, of blessed memory

God, for whom the rooster stands on one leg with its comb upon its head—almost like a kind of white thread—and his strength and time <note>The text likely refers to the "Sekhvi," the rooster/heart mentioned in Job 38:36, which in Jewish tradition distinguishes between night and day.</note>. He receives his portion and looks out upon the world and its companions, cleaving without ceasing to holiness. From the action of the **Voice** <gloss>Tiferet</gloss>, he distinguishes between the darkness of time and the time of peace. It is good for him, and he hastens to occupy himself with "matter," yet he hastens to delay his investigation <note>This suggests a tension between spiritual perception and physical constraints.</note>. For the "portion of evil" is not good, and it is written: *Evil shall not dwell with You* <note>Psalm 5:5</note>. Thus it is explained that he sets his mind to gaze upon the hidden treasuries. He flows toward the "Bed" <gloss>the Shekhinah/Atarah</gloss>, for his bed is hidden within the clay to align the "matter" from the four cycles <term>Tekufot; the four seasons</term> of the year. Therefore, all those who possess a natural form require support from the power of the "Master of the Assembly of the Offering," who was before the Lord. Every "Master" is like a blow to his neighbor, and he hastens for the morrow from their power to derive pleasure from the Torah.

And behold, the time appointed for the "Call of the Rooster" <note>Kriat HaGever; the dawn</note> is drawn from the four cycles of the year. This is what is meant by: "He gives from his glory to those who fear Him." He gives his wisdom to him; He gives to the rooster the strength of the dove <note>A mystical comparison between the rooster's alert nature and the dove's loyalty</note> to hasten toward the morning.

"Who can number the clouds by wisdom?" <note>Job 38:37</note>. Who can record? For when the entire **Foundation** <term>Yesod</term> is clarified for the **Crown** <term>Atarah; the 10th Sefirah</term>, He gives wisdom to the flow that provides "Splendor" <gloss>Hod</gloss> to her, for **Understanding** <term>Binah</term> and the Heat. For he who is Understanding and occupies himself with the surrounding **Sefirot** <term>Divine emanations</term>—they allude to **Endurance** <term>Netzach</term> and **Splendor** <term>Hod</term>. The wise ones say: **Wisdom** <term>Chokhmah</term>, the Supernal, is in the Crown. This means that the Name gives them their clarity, and the "Generalities of Heaven" <note>likely a reading of 'Nivlei Shamayim' or 'Bottles of Heaven' from Job 38:37</note> represent the exchanges of the heavens—who shall write and arrange their place? 

This means: who can count and number the lightness of the stars of the heavens? For the heavens are "laws" <note>Original: *Gezarot*</note> corresponding to the **Foundation** <term>Yesod</term>. That which is vacant of them in his world comes from the movers. The "Generalities of Heaven" refers to the matters of the heavens which are nullified before their lights; who shall arrange them? Behold, they shall gush forth, and behold, they shall turn, and they shall pour out their bread in perfection. Therefore, he sings to them and says: He gave the timings of the stars of heaven by His wisdom. The matters of all the seasonal cycles are likened to "precise measurements" given to the wise. For we already know that all existing things are found through the "Eye of the Eye" <note>The Primal Source</note>. Know that Wisdom belongs to the wise, for He taught all existing things and improved them toward the Supernal Wisdom, as it is written: *In Wisdom.*

And behold, the "Place-Makers"—which are the firmaments—who is the "Voice" <gloss>Tiferet</gloss> that can give them a number? He who understands shall answer you under the Supernal Wisdom. "And the Generalities of Heaven—who can record them?" The things joined to the heavens—who shall arrange them? Therefore, he sings and says: He gave the timings of the celestial bodies by His wisdom, and their power is adjacent. 

The interpretation: When the heavens reign, they live and become wise in their place, alluding to the "Appointed Ones." And "The Generalities of Heaven—who can record them?" It is known that everything that emerges from the **First Cause** <note>the Divine Source</note> only lingers and is hidden due to the distance. This is the "Line" <gloss>original: Kav</gloss> in the world of the Sea. Therefore, it was at the ultimate thickness according to what was drawn from them. According to its "Taste" and the "Beauty" <gloss>Tiferet</gloss> of its surroundings, it is drawn from the source of the **Investigation** <gloss>Binah</gloss>. The Beauty <gloss>Tiferet</gloss> merited to gaze upon the power of the Supernal Machine, of blessed memory—which is Binah— and the "Line" was, as it were, uplifted. Therefore, the "Line" was "unformed and void" <note>Tohu va-Vohu; Genesis 1:2</note> and was born and sought the good of its primordial state, looking back to its birth.

Therefore, "And the Generalities of Heaven—who can record them?" The interpretation is: "Who can quiet them?" <note>as in 'to be still'</note>. It is like the cooling of the "Wings of the Dust" <note>original: Kanfei Afar</note> for rest. The interpretation: When it is complete in the mind of the **Crown** <term>Atarah</term>—which is called "Dust"—to rest, it is like water as it was before the Creation, being close to **Understanding** <term>Binah</term>. For the *Spirit of God* <gloss>Binah</gloss> *hovered over the face of the waters.* It entered and was pressed until the Holy One, blessed be He, stirred and attached the indwelling. Just as one might say: *He established the Earth* <gloss>Atarah</gloss> *upon its foundations* <gloss>Binah and the Voice</gloss>, *that it should not collapse forever* <note>Psalm 104:5</note>. This implies that it was in its mind to collapse until He attached the indwelling. This was the "Request of the Dust to Rest" when the Dust was appointed to be in the hand of the works of Heaven, to be gathered like the "Form of the Transition" <note>difficult mystical phrase</note>... and it was entered and pressed...

<meta>This page continues the Ra’avad’s mystical introduction to the Book of Creation. Having established the relationship between the divine "Voice" and physical "matter" on the previous page, he now turns to the mechanics of pregnancy and birth, viewing them as a reflection of the Sefirot (divine emanations). # Introduction of the Ra’avad, of blessed memory

For satisfaction and from the **Understanding** <gloss>Binah</gloss>, the "greenness" within the embroidery <note>Likely referring to the intricate formation of the embryo</note> acts like the opening of her womb, bringing forth below. It is like the "potential matter" <term>Hyle; the primordial substance from which all things are formed</term> that is planted to give birth to the hidden child, waiting for its time to be born until its full capacity arrives. 

We learn that the pain of childbirth is one of the ten curses placed upon Eve, stemming from the aspect of "a hanging grape" <note>A metaphorical description of the embryo's precarious state</note>. In the time of the Garden of Eden, there was a wellspring of "Strong Knowledge," which allowed for eternal life—except for the bird of **Kindness** <gloss>Hesed</gloss> named the *Chul* <note>The Phoenix, which according to legend lives for a thousand years and then regenerates</note>, as it is written: *And I shall multiply my days as the Chul* <note>Job 29:18</note>. Therefore, all living things were cursed because of Eve with the pain of birth and with death. Every species of living creature has its own specific gestation time, as explained in the **Torah** and in **Tractate Bekhorot** <note>The Talmudic volume dealing with the laws of the firstborn and animal gestation</note>. The gestation time of each is the period required for the physical matter to reach its completion.

And behold, when the time of birth arrives, the "Rock of Strength" ascends, and the time of "the end of the forces" begins. This corresponds to the seven types of pure qualities: **Crown** <gloss>Atarah/Malkhut</gloss>, **Foundation** <gloss>Yesod</gloss>, **Victory** <gloss>Netzach</gloss>, **Splendor** <gloss>Hod</gloss>, **Beauty** <gloss>Tiferet</gloss>, **Kindness** <gloss>Hesed</gloss>, and **Strength** <gloss>Gevurah</gloss>. In this mystical system, "Diyon" represents **Beauty** <gloss>Tiferet</gloss>. The exchange of "Diyon" is **Kindness** <gloss>Hesed</gloss>, for there is a distinction between the portion of the children of Jacob and the portion of the children of Esau.

The "greenness" mentioned earlier comes from the power of *Dan shall be a serpent by the way* <note>Genesis 49:17</note>. This represents the completion of the forces that strike through the hand of Dan, who seals the judgment for the child to be born. As our sages said: *Against your will you are formed, against your will you are born, and against your will you live* <note>Pirkei Avot 4:22</note>. This is what is meant by "the child is born through the exchange of forces." 

Behold, birth is through the power of the Lord, for He is the one who "unties the birth-pangs of the mother." We learn that in His greatness, at the moment He sends the child down to be born below, **Wisdom** <gloss>Chokhmah</gloss> is completed from above and departs from the **Kingdom** <gloss>Malkhut</gloss>. This is the power of the "Dream of Kindness," referring to the Lord of Birth. At the time that **Wisdom** <gloss>Chokhmah</gloss> departs, it descends into the "Seventy" <note>The seventy celestial princes or nations</note> and revolves around the "Thirteen" <note>The thirteen attributes of mercy</note>. From there, it receives all the future events destined for the child. 

Therefore, it is proper for you to contemplate this: a person who writes an amulet to speed up a birth before its natural time is effectively killing two forces. Sometimes this causes the child to be born on "evil days" and brings about great misfortunes, one worse than the other. These "destroyers" are the opposite of the "Seed of Jacob." This can be understood through a parable: a fetus is destined to be born on a certain day when the **Moon** <gloss>Atarah</gloss> is favorable. But if one uses "the copper serpent" <note>Magic or forbidden arts</note> to force the birth, they have uprooted the natural decree. By bringing the child out before the Moon has reached its station, they exchange a good destiny for a flawed one. Such a child is born at a time when its life-force is cancelled, often leading to death in a few days. The person who speeds this up "cleanses" the birth by force, but they have stolen the decree of the Creator and killed the living soul by bringing it forth out of its time. They may cause the child to lose certain wealth or a specific destiny. In short, such a person disrupts all the **Orders of Creation**. This is sufficient for anyone who understands the depth of this matter.

Furthermore, one who brings forth wealth <note>original: "Hon"; potentially a metaphor for the soul/seed</note> should do so according to the Torah. One should count the days of pregnancy and know the time of birth. The explanation is: the one who is "planted" to give birth should count the months backward to know at which degree or level the conception began. This is the order of the count:

Know that the time of birth depends on the number of days of pregnancy. There is a count for "conception" and a count for "gestation." The number is 278 days, or sometimes 273 days <note>A common Talmudic calculation for nine months of pregnancy</note>. The sign for this is "lacking a night from conception." Therefore, when the birth begins, you should count back 273 days from the time of birth. If the constellation associated with **Understanding** <gloss>Binah</gloss> is found there, you will know the true time of birth. If she did not immerse <note>in the Mikvah/ritual bath</note> at that time, but rather months before, you count 278 days. If at that time she also did not immerse, count 287 days. This is how you measure according to the "View of Understanding," which acts to "hold back" and "bring near." Therefore, all those who are conceived through the extended blessings of **Understanding** <gloss>Binah</gloss> have the power to "hold the drop" in the womb until it is ready. This is called "Religion/Law" <note>Dath</note> because it constricts and holds and measures.

<meta>This page continues the Ra’avad’s mystical commentary, moving from the general theory of gestation and "potential matter" to specific examples of how the Divine sustains life and the biological-spiritual process of digestion and birth. It links the behavior of animals like lions, ravens, and goats to deeper Kabbalistic structures.</meta>

# Introduction of the Ra’avad, of blessed memory

The path of the ascent. This is the secret of the *young lions roaring for prey, seeking their food from God* <note>Psalm 104:21</note>, meaning their sustenance. After he mentioned the "Face of the Lion" <note>One of the four faces of the Divine Chariot in Ezekiel’s vision</note> and the order of its nourishment through the **Understanding** <gloss>Binah</gloss> appropriate to it, he returned to mention the branches of the "Face of the Eagle," which includes every bird. He says that the nature of the raven is so cruel that it possesses no mercy at all. Therefore, when it gives birth to its young, it sees them as white <note>According to Midrash, raven chicks are born with white feathers, and the parents, thinking they are not theirs, abandon them</note>. It refuses to provide for them or gather them in the snow. What does the Holy One, Blessed be He, do? He prepares little gnats for them, which fly into the mouths of the chicks, and from these they are nourished. This is what is written: *He gives to the beast its food, and to the young ravens which cry* <note>Psalm 147:9</note>.

At that time, the dog—which is a "beast" <term>Behemah; often refers to domestic animals, but here used broadly</term>—is also provided for. Know that creatures do not usually provide for dogs; therefore, the Holy One, Blessed be He, created a special quality for the dog: everything it eats remains in its intestines for three days before it is digested. This reinforces the verse *He gives to the beast its food*. And regarding the raven: *Who provides for the raven its prey, when its young ones cry unto God, and wander for lack of food?* <note>Job 38:41</note>. The translation <note>The Aramaic Targum</note> of this is: "Who prepares for the raven its food when its young cry before God and wander because of the lack of food?"

It is well known that all food transforms according to the one who eats it. Just as the food... <unclear>illegible</unclear>... is appropriate to add to the body, some of it becomes the animal's flesh, and through the mercy of the "fluids" it becomes waste, and from the waste comes energy <note>Literally "strength"</note>. Through mercy, the food is transformed into milk and then returns to be blood. Our labor to break down the food results in it becoming separated into various components—the liver, the blood, and the "residue" in the gallbladder. 

You must discern that every likeness is a "language" and a "speaker"; they all pass through like "children of change" <note>original: "bnei chalof"; a reference to Proverbs 31:8, meaning those who are transient or passing away</note> in their ascent and descent. Everything happens by the "Judgment of the Worker" <note>Divine Law</note>, by the mouth of the Lord they shall rest and by the mouth of the Lord they shall journey. Therefore, it is possible for a pure bird to be strengthened by the "breaking" <note>The breakdown of matter</note>. How so? The bird is born from an egg, and that egg returns to be a pure bird, a living soul in the cycles. 

Specifically, before God, this is **Kindness** <gloss>Hesed</gloss>: that the **Understanding** <gloss>Binah</gloss> transforms the fluid into milk, and it is absorbed into all the 248 limbs and all the sinews. Then it returns to be the guardian of the "form of the sun" <note>A mystical reference to the vital life force or the soul's radiance</note>. Thus, "its children cry out to God" in their specific essence. When does this happen? When it happens to them that the eater is superior to the food. If the food is "consumed" by the eater, it rises. But if the food is dangerous or heavy, those who walk toward it fall. 

If the animal is far from being elevated, it still remains under the "judgment of death," without any ascent to the higher levels. For there, the "Force of the Food" <note>The spiritual essence within physical nourishment</note> performs its work, bringing forth the effort to ascend. This is the secret of why they ate with the "breaking" <note>Perhaps referring to the transition from vegetarianism to eating meat</note>, for it is permitted to eat the meat of the animal. In the **Torah**, it is sometimes permitted to eat meat and sometimes forbidden. If the food is "consumed" by the person, it is thickened and rolled from level to level until it reaches the highest "faraway" level. This is why it says *they wander for lack of food*. For those who are "consumed" wander in their cycles—why? For the "children of food." If they are strengthened, they return to "nothingness" <note>Ayin; the Divine source</note> and do not go toward loss or descent. Therefore, the food wanders according to the law of the "children of change." This is the secret of *its young ones cry unto God*—if the eater is superior to the food—and *they wander for lack of food*.

*Do you know the time when the wild goats of the rock bring forth?* <note>Job 39:1</note>. This "Ya'eleh" <term>Ya'el; Nubian Ibex or Mountain Goat</term> is a male mountain goat, and its name in the language of the **Torah** is *Dishon*. The translation of *Dishon* is "Ya'ela." It is included in the "Faces of the Living Creatures" <note>The Hayot/Angels of the Chariot</note>. It is a known tradition that when the mountain goat is ready to give birth, she is compassionate. God summons a dragon <note>original: "Drakon"; referring to a serpent</note> for her, which bites her womb, and she immediately gives birth. If the dragon were to arrive one moment too early or one moment too late, she would not be able to survive, because her womb is extremely narrow and the offspring cannot emerge...

<summary>The Ra'avad explains how God provides for all creatures—even "cruel" ravens and dogs—through unique biological traits. He then details a mystical view of digestion as a process of spiritual elevation and describes the miraculous birth of the mountain goat involving a "dragon."</summary>

<meta>This page continues the Ra’avad’s mystical commentary on the wild animals described in the Book of Job (chapter 39), moving from the raven and the dog to the "donkey" (Chamur), the "wild ass" (Arod), and the "wild ox" (Re’em). These creatures are treated as allegories for the struggle between the material world, the "Other Side" (Sitra Achra), and the eventual dominion of the Divine Kingship (Malchut).</meta>

# Introduction of the Ra’avad, of blessed memory

### Introduction of the Ra’avad, of blessed memory

The purpose of this "Good Psalm" <note>Referring to the poetic section of Job 39</note> is to instruct man regarding the means through which our books are sent. Regarding the "donkey" <note>original: *chamur*</note>, the Sages of blessed memory spoke of it as "the donkey I built" to be a speaker in its rebellion against civilization and its affairs. Therefore, amidst the rushes of—God forbid—rebellion against civilization and the habituation of the wilderness, there is a "donkey of the desert" <note>An "Arod" or wild ass</note>, characterized as a "trapped and fleeting spirit" <note>original: *kefat shelefat ruach*</note>.

The "bonds of the wild ass" <note>Job 39:5</note> refer to the eight levels of birds that dwell in the hidden paths of the wild ass. The essence of the wild ass is purely of the wilderness—it is "the donkey I built," turning away to become a creature of the desert. Similarly, the Sages of blessed memory distinguished between a "donkey" and a "wild ass" <note>In Jewish law, they are different species</note>. Its nature is to dwell in the deserts, bound by the chains and bonds of the wild ass. Who is it that can open and loosen these bonds of the wild ass to return it to Man? The Aramaic translation says: *Who has set the donkey free, and who has loosened the bonds of the wild ass?* <note>original Aramaic: *man katar mdora bar chorin umosrei aruda hachun sharei*</note>.

*Whose home I have made the wilderness, and the salt land his dwelling* <note>Job 39:6</note>. This explains that the dwelling of the wild ass is "fleeting." My judgments were sent to the wilderness and our drink was set toward the "salt land" <note>barren earth</note> in order to return it to Man. For a "salt land" is not inhabited, and thus it becomes like a lonely shrub in the desert that does not see when good comes. This is also the Aramaic translation: *In the desert, a salt land that is not inhabited.*

This is the secret of the **Kingship** <gloss>Malchut</gloss> being described as *poor and riding on a donkey, and on a colt, the foal of a donkey* <note>Zechariah 9:9</note>. For all those who are "spread out" <note>The external, wild forces</note> will eventually live under its dominion. This is translated as: *I have placed his house in the desert and his dwelling in a land that is not inhabited.*

*He scorns the tumult of the city; he does not hear the shouts of the driver* <note>Job 39:7</note>. Behold, it is in its nature to rebel against the **Kingship** <gloss>Malchut</gloss> and not to listen to the voice of the taskmaster or the voice of the ruler. If so, in what way is "return" written concerning it? Only when it is before Man, until it accepts upon itself the "yoke of the kingdom." As the translation says: *He laughs at the noise of the city, and the shouts of the driver he does not hear.*

*He ranges the mountains for his pasture, and he searches after every green thing* <note>Job 39:8</note>. Behold, the "fleeing one" and the "wild ass" travel by foot to be spies and scouts of the city. This refers to the judgments of **Wisdom** <gloss>Chokhmah</gloss>, **Understanding** <gloss>Binah</gloss>, and **Beauty** <gloss>Tiferet</gloss>. It is all for the sake of praise and debate. This is the secret of "and he smelled her from afar." Thus the donkey is envisioned as a "girded horse."

This is the secret of "taking the prize and riding for the kings of the earth." And *after every green thing he searches*—this refers to the **Green Line** <term>Kav Yarok; a mystical boundary mentioned in the Zohar and Sefer Yetzirah that surrounds the world and from which darkness emanates</term> which surrounds the entire world from every side. As the translation says: *And the girded crown explores the mountains for its pasture, seeking every green herb.*

*Will the wild ox be willing to serve you? Will he spend the night at your manger?* <note>Job 39:9</note>. This means: Know that all domestic animals, wild beasts, and birds are subjugated to Man. Wherever the "spirit" <note>Ruach</note> intends to go, they go, and they do not turn as they go, for they live from the height of Man. Therefore, the fear and dread of Man is upon every living thing. All of this is by divine decree. But the **Wild Ox** <note>original: *Re'em*</note>, because its portion is so great, rebels against Man. This is why it asks: *Will the wild ox be willing to serve you?* This means: will he be willing to pass through the judgment of "transient beings" <note>original: *bnei chalof*</note> to accept a yoke upon his neck, just as a servant serves his master?

Similarly, *will he spend the night at your manger?* For whoever takes from Man, his soul clings to him. Therefore, when he dies, his strength and being are gathered to him. It is written: *May it be rolled by my hand.* The secret here involves the "trapped and fleeting spirit." Through him, the "spirit is drawn out" and rolled. This is the secret of *will he spend the night at your manger?*—to make a covenant with you and to be subjugated according to the law of transient beings. But the wild ox does not desire to work for a human being, nor to turn toward him, so that no benefit shall reach Man from him. As the translation says: *Is the wild ox willing to serve you? Will he spend the night at your stable?*

*Can you bind the wild ox in the furrow with ropes? Or will he harrow the valleys after you?* <note>Job 39:10</note>. This is a difficult matter! Can you truly tie the wild ox in a furrow that has been separated to spread the seed? *With ropes* <note>original: *avoto*</note>—this means by using the strongest of the animals. *Will he harrow the valleys after you?* Meaning: can you use him to plow so that he returns the valleys to Man?

<meta>This page continues the Ra’avad’s mystical commentary on the wild creatures of Job 39. While the previous page focused on the "wild ass" (Arod) as a symbol of the untamed spirit, this page transitions into "mystical embryology," using the gestation of animals and the imagery of Job to explain the development of the human fetus and the descent of the soul through the Sefirot (divine emanations).</meta>

# Introduction of the Ra’avad, of blessed memory

From the expression "his eye was not dim," <note>original: *lo khata eino* (Deuteronomy 34:7)</note> it is explained to mean that his teeth were not wrinkled. <note>The Ra'avad interprets physical vitality through the state of the teeth/jaw, a common medieval physiological theory</note>. Consider how much strength there is in the "extra understanding" <term>Binah: the divine attribute of Understanding and structure</term>. The seed, while it is up to thirty days old, is later governed by the power of Kindness <term>Chesed: the attribute of Mercy and expansion</term> and is revealed; it expels from itself things that are not fit to be rectified below. And the youth, etc., is a spark that awakens the 248 limbs <note>In Jewish tradition, the human body is composed of 248 limbs and 365 sinews</note> and various revelations.

After thirty days, the power of Strength <term>Gevurah: the attribute of Judgment and restriction</term> governs it, etc. Then comes the wrinkling and the "wing-like" movement, etc., and the "natural axis" spreads through all 248 limbs. It nullifies the "will for flesh" until it returns to flesh, and the "will for revelation," and [the will] for grapes to grapes, and for "gamnot" to "gamnot," <note>likely referring to botanical or anatomical structures</note> and so for every single companion [limb].

Afterward, the life of the "desire-power" is removed from it, along with the power of the multitudes and strength, and all their connections are established upon their base until the completion of thirty [more] days. After that, the power of Victory <term>Nezach</term> and the strength of the hearts rule over it for another thirty days. Afterward, the power of Splendor <term>Hod</term> is clarified, and they are tied with a strong and mighty knot and become sanctified. 

Afterward, the Foundation <term>Yesod</term> rules over it, and within it is the power of the Moon. Therefore, if it is born in the eighth month <note>original: *ch"h* - Chodesh HaShemini</note>, it is because the Foundation is the "Living God" <note>original: *El Chai*</note> that breathes life, being the Crown <term>Atarah: the final Sefirah, Malchut</term>. The secret is that "the Righteous One" (Foundation) is exactly opposite the "Crown," and the letter *Kof* <note>The letter Kof represents the "back of the head" or "monkeys," often associated with the transition between holy and unholy</note>—these are what bring forth the "creeping things."

Because the "Walking" <note>The higher soul's movement</note> serves in the Upper World, and the "Palate" <note>The physical senses</note> serves in the Lower World, it desires to cling to Strength and to separate like the Intellectual Soul from the murky body. Therefore, if a woman gives birth in the "eighth attribute" <note>the 8th month</note>, Heaven forbid <note>original: *ch"v*</note>, who will give a soul to this murky body? Therefore, those of the "kingly" power die. But if she gives birth in the "ninth attribute," which is associated with Kindness (*Chesed*), the child shall live, as it is said: "Life and favor You have granted me, and Your providence has preserved my spirit" <note>Job 10:12</note>. 

According to this order, all the days of gestation for every species are spread out, for their gestation days are divided by seven. Therefore, the Sages said: "If you know the time of birth, you know the time of conception; if you know the time of conception, you know the time of birth." This is the wisdom of the "months of the womb" from the Moon, as in: "Do you know the time when the mountain goats give birth?" <note>Job 39:1</note>. This is what the Aramaic translates as: *Will you see the months of those that go forth, and will you know the peace of their birth?* 

"They bow down, they bring forth their young, they cast out their pains" <note>Job 39:3</note>. Know that everyone who departs from the King is like one who flees, yet he bows to the King and takes permission from Him and accepts His decree. So too the soul, at the time it departs from the King, the Lord, with its powers—it bows down, it and all its companions, which are: 
- The Lower Soul <term>Nefesh: associated with the World of Action</term>
- The Spirit <term>Ruach: associated with the attribute of Beauty/Tiferet</term>
- The Higher Soul <term>Neshamah: associated with Understanding/Binah</term>
- The Living Soul <term>Chayah: associated with Wisdom/Chokhmah</term> 
- The Singular Soul <term>Yechidah: associated with the Crown/Keter</term> 

And its powers—at that time, Wisdom bows to give birth. And when the "Supernal Wisdom" <term>Chokhmah</term> cleaves <note>original: *tiflach*</note>, the knots of the "cleavings" are the Crown, Foundation, and Splendor, and they are for all the "Wisdoms of the ones who go forth"—"a joyful mother of children" <note>Psalm 113:9</note>. 

"Behold, they cast out their pains." This means the child is born and they become "mothers" at the time of birth. This is: "they bow down, they bring forth their young, they cleave their pangs, they cast out their pains." This means: "they cleave their young" because the one giving birth breaks through and tears the placenta <note>original: *salya*</note> in which it lies, and immediately "they cast out their pains." This means: the time to give birth arrives, and her labor pains are removed from her. This is what the Aramaic translates: *They are bent like purses, cleaving in their transition, arranged...* 

Just as all these attributes are rectified before the "Pangs" <note>meaning the birth process</note>, so too are they rectified before their "companions"—the Face of the Ox, the Face of the Eagle, and every line and "pen" between them. They go, but "they do not go to them." And when the children become strong and hold onto their King: "Behold, they go and increase." This means they grow and increase like the "secret of gestation." For all their attributes are directed toward Wisdom, for life and life, and upon the face of the "Pangs." Because the "Pang" is the holy level from which it comes. Behold, they are finished with Kindness and strengthened in the Lord and His portions. Their power is from the "harsh sources" that deserve excision <term>Karet: spiritual soul-cutting</term>, but they are crushed in the "rebellious exchanges" and will not turn back to them again.

This is what the Aramaic translates: *They are strengthened in their children, they acquire through their gestation, they go forth and do not return to them.* 

"Who has sent the wild ass free, and the bonds of the wild ass who has loosened?" <note>Job 39:5</note>. It is known that the "wild ass" <note>original: *pere*</note> is a cord/form of Kindness (*Chesed*), which is attributed to the Sea above all, and he will be a "wild man" <note>original: *pere adam* - Gen 16:12</note>. If so, they are prayers in "bloom" <note>a pun on *pere* (wild ass) and *perach* (flower/bloom)</note>; "his hand against everyone and everyone's hand against him," and he is bound in the bond of the Covenant—everything is a bloom.

וכעת <note>Catchword: And now</note>

<meta>This page continues the Ra’avad’s mystical and physiological commentary on the Book of Job. Following the discussion on embryology and the development of the soul's powers, the text now turns to the symbolic descriptions of the ostrich (the "lacking wisdom" bird) and the war horse from Job chapter 39. The Ra’avad uses the Aramaic Targum (an ancient Jewish translation/paraphrase) to deepen the explanation of these creatures' natures.</meta>

# Introduction of the Ra’avad, of blessed memory

...not in vain; he kisses without fear. <note>original: *yishak beli pakhad*. The commentator plays on the word *yis’haq* (laughs) and *yishak* (kisses/touches), suggesting the horse’s bold contact with danger.</note> This represents the boldness of the horse, which does not fear to engage in struggle and use its strength for its own benefit. It does not judge based on who is weak, nor by what is good, nor by force, for its past battles are remembered by it. Therefore, for the most part, **it laughs without fear**, without hesitation. This is as the Targum <note>The ancient Aramaic translation of the Bible</note> translates: "that it mocks at the collision, for it does not fear the emptiness of the drawing of the sword."

For God "deprived her of wisdom and did not allot her a share of understanding." <note>Job 39:17, referring to the ostrich</note> The explanation is that the ostrich’s <note>Hebrew: *sevakhat ha-sus*, though likely referring here to the *Renanim* or ostrich mentioned in the biblical context</note> lack of wisdom means she was not given a portion of **Binah** <term>Binah: the divine attribute of structured understanding</term>. Therefore, the rooster is called *Sekhwi* <note>In Jewish liturgy, God gives the *Sekhwi* (rooster/intellect) the ability to distinguish between day and night</note>, and accordingly, there is life in its movement and mercy, as the Targum translates: "the rooster's intellect" to merit its wisdom, "and He did not allot to her" of its understanding. **"When she lifts herself on high, she scorns the horse and its rider"** <note>Job 39:18</note>—the explanation is that she flies and flutters toward the heights, mocking all the chariots that would try to snatch her away, as the Targum translates: "In the time when she flies high in the heavens, she mocks the horse and its riders."

### The War Horse

**"Do you give the horse his might? Do you clothe his neck with a mane?"** <note>Job 39:19</note> The explanation is that the horse possesses all might, and its inheritance comes from the Kingdom, as the Targum translates: "Is it by your permission that you give the horse strength, or do you clothe his neck with power?"

**"Do you make him leap like a locust? His majestic snorting is terrible."** <note>Job 39:20</note> Do you make him flee? Do you move him and frighten him as you would make a locust flee and tremble? **"His majestic snorting is terrible"**—the sneezing of the shadow of his nostrils is a terror, as the Targum translates: "Do you make him tremble like a grasshopper? The sound of the snorting of his nostrils is a terror."

**"He paws in the valley and rejoices in his strength; he goes out to meet the weapons."** <note>Job 39:21</note> The warriors <note>original: *lavakhim*</note> paw in the depth of the plain, perhaps they can capture them for the Kingdom of Heaven. And the horse laughs and rejoices in his strength over the officers <note>original: *saternin*</note> at the awakening of war, amidst the wings of toil and the transformations. **"He goes out to meet the weapons"**—towards the armed men of war, for he desires the magic of the battle-array and what lies beneath. Therefore, he always laughs at war, as the Targum translates: "They dig in the valley and rejoice in their strength, and go out to meet the weapons of war."

**"He mocks at fear and is not dismayed; he does not turn back from the sword."** <note>Job 39:22</note> The explanation is that he scorns every fear of war, and his heart is not shattered because his nature is that of war and might. Therefore, he does not retreat from the sword in battle, as the Targum translates: "He mocks at the struggle and is not broken, and does not return from before the sword."

**"Upon him rattles the quiver, the flashing spear, and the javelin."** <note>Job 39:23</note> **"Upon him is sent the quiver"**—meaning the weapon-case. **"The flashing spear"** is the iron which is on the spear, and the **"javelin"** is a lance, as the Targum translates: "Upon him is cast the weapon, the spear, and the lance."

**"With quaking and rage he swallows the ground; he cannot believe that it is the sound of the shofar."** <note>Job 39:24</note> The explanation is that he moves with agitation and anger, and scatters pits in the earth in order to run from the path of the trenches to fight the enemies. From the great joy the horse has for war, even when he hears the sound of battle, **he cannot believe** that there is a war until he sees the battle with his own eyes. This is the meaning of "he cannot believe that it is the sound of the shofar." And from its strength... why do I need the sound of the shofar? It is to awaken the war, the fighting, the shouting, and the terror from your obligations. And this is what the Targum translates: "In his quaking and rage he makes pits in the earth, and he does not believe any sound of the shofar."

**"At the sound of the shofar he says, 'Aha!' and from afar he smells the battle, the thunder of the captains and the shouting."** <note>Job 39:25</note> The explanation is that whenever he hears the trumpet-blast of war, he prepares himself with joy. From afar he senses the war, the quaking of the captains, and their intoxication with one another. That is to say, even the captains of the walls of the world—he senses the war immediately. This is as the Targum translates: "When the shofar is blown he says, 'I am glad!' and from afar he smells the battle, the shouts of his masters, and the cry of the chargers." The plain meaning of **"from afar he smells the battle"** is that he does not believe the war is happening until he sees it with his own eyes. "Aha!" <note>The Hebrew *He'akh*</note> is interpreted thus.

**"Is it by your wisdom that the hawk soars, spreading its wings toward the south?"** <note>Job 39:26</note> It is hollow like every day when the southern wind and northern wind rest...

<summary>The Ra'avad provides a detailed commentary on the ostrich and the war horse from Job 39, using the Aramaic Targum to emphasize the horse's supernatural bravery and eagerness for battle. The text explores the horse's physical reactions—snorting, pawing, and its inability to "believe" the shofar's call until the fight begins—as a metaphor for strength and divine design.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the Ra’avad’s commentary on Job 39, moving from the horse and the ostrich to a deeper philosophical and mystical exploration of the differences between human intellect and animal nature. It specifically addresses the concept of "Dveikut" (spiritual attachment) and the symbolic meaning of the "Renanim" (ostrich or wild rooster) in Jewish mystical tradition.</meta>

# Introduction of the Ra’avad, of blessed memory

Regarding this explanation, know that just as the Master sends the grace of His wisdom into the soul, it must be spread out and prepared for its fellow companions. So too, the Supernal Wisdom <note>Hebrew: *Chokhmah HaElyonah*, referring to the divine source of all knowledge</note> requires a spreading out and a discourse to mend its paths. Knowledge is required to give the matter its proper portion, and this stands as an overseer in the heart and brain, which represent the partial dominion of man—but not in the animals that oppose man. For even if a man were to show them his way and his paths, they would not learn from him, nor understand, nor listen to him, for they are inherently opposed to man. Therefore, a man cannot bind them to himself even with a rope or with thick cords. And even if he wishes to arrange the "depths," which are the depths of wisdom, and influence them through his hand, they will not listen to him because they are oppositional, as it is said: "He will not arrange the depths for the furrow" <note>A mystical reading of Job 39:10</note>, which the Targum <note>The Aramaic translation</note> renders as: "Is it possible that you could tie the wild ox (*re’em*) in the furrows of the plain with his harness, or will he level the valleys after you?"

The "harnessing" is a hint to Wisdom, which is called an "inheritance," as it is said, "Restrain your eyes" <note>Hebrew: *balmei reḥaz einyekha*</note>. Will you tie the wild ox (*re'em*) with his thick cord? Know that whoever serves a specific group of powers, in the same proportion that the soul of the servant relates to the object of service, so in the future path will be the bond (*kesher*) of the servant's soul to the Master. This is the secret of the verse: **"But you who cleave to the Lord your God are all alive today"** <note>Deuteronomy 4:4. The term for "cleaving" is *Dveikut*, a central concept in Jewish mysticism describing attachment to the Divine.</note>. Therefore, whoever serves the Living God and is bound to Him—even if he dies for the sanctification of His Name—behold, the Living God shall give him His strength and His spirit. 

The distinction for one who serves "other gods" is like the parable of the *re’em* <note>Often translated as a wild ox or oryx; sometimes associated with the unicorn in medieval lore</note>, which is drawn from the foundation of the world, as it is said: **"his horns are the horns of the wild ox"** <note>Deuteronomy 33:17</note>. This was said regarding Joseph the Righteous. And these are the meanings of "Will you tie the wild ox with his cord," which refer to possessions and the secret within them—they are "thick cords." Regarding "Will he level the depths for the furrow?"—do not let it enter your mind that a man can prepare for you the "furrow of life" which you desire from this world. Would you trust him because his strength is great, and leave your labor to him? And is it possible that you would trust him to deliver your handiwork, that you should bring in your harvest to him, from which you have been sustained until now? Only if you recognize the Harvester and the Reaper through the service of love can you trust in Him and leave your labor to His kindness (*Hasdo*); if He wills it, He gives, and if He does not will it, He does not give. As the Targum translates: "Is it possible that you will trust in him because his strength is great, and will you leave your labor to him?" 

If so, is it possible that you can rely on him that everything you have sown will be improved, and that all your harvest will be gathered and strengthened by the power of the *re'em*? For he is the "firstborn of the bull," as it is said: "His glory is like the firstling of his bullock, and his horns are like the horns of a wild ox; with them he shall push the people" <note>Deuteronomy 33:17</note>. This is why the Targum translates: "Is it possible that you will trust in him... and leave your labor..." Speaking now of the "face of the eagle."

**"The wings of the ostrich flap joyfully; are they the pinions and plumage of love?"** <note>Job 39:13</note>. This refers to the name of the "Wild Rooster" <note>original: *Tarnegol HaBar*. In Jewish folklore, this is the legendary *Ziz*, a giant bird.</note> in the Book of Job; it is called *Renanim* (Joyful Songs) because it gives forth songs of praise. In the *Heikhalot* literature <term>Heikhalot: Early Jewish mystical texts describing the "palaces" of heaven and the divine chariot</term>, it is written that the "Holy Living Creatures" (*Chayot HaKodesh*) hint at this from within their wings, as it is said: "And I heard the sound of their wings." 

Behold, in this Wild Rooster, whose strength comes from the "face of the eagle," it rises in full joy. And likewise, regarding "the pinions and plumage of the stork," the Sages of blessed memory explained that it was a representation of the intellect, as the Targum renders: "The wing of the wild rooster which praises and shouts, and the wing of the white stork and its feathers." 

**"For she leaves her eggs on the earth and warms them in the dust."** <note>Job 39:14</note>. Because the "wing of songs" contains all types of upper and lower wings—for it includes all the celestial constellations—when she leaves her eggs on the ground and nests them in the dust, the Understanding (*Binah*) warms them from the air without her even touching them. Just by her looking at them, they are warmed, and chicks are born from them. This is what the Targum means: "For she leaves her eggs on the ground and warms them on the earth." **"And forgets that a foot may crush them, or that a wild beast may trample them."** She is hardened against her young, as if they were not hers...

<summary>The Ra’avad interprets Job 39 as a mystical allegory, contrasting the untameable nature of the wild ox and ostrich with the human capacity for "Dveikut" (divine attachment). He links the "Renanim" bird to the celestial "Wild Rooster" of mystical literature, which is said to hatch its eggs through spiritual focus or sight alone.</summary>
