<meta>Continuity: This page continues the commentary on Chapter 1, Mishnah 4 of Sefer Yetzirah, shifting from the general definition of the ten Sefirot to a technical and philosophical defense of why the number ten is absolute—neither nine nor eleven. It explores the correspondence between the ten Sefirot and the structures of the physical universe (the World), the calendar (the Year), and human consciousness (the Soul).</meta>

# Ra’avad, of blessed memory — Chapter 1, Mishnah 4

And they ascended in number: seven in the upper ones including the tongue, and six in the lower ones <note>original: *v-z"v b'tachtonim*; likely a scribal shorthand for the numerical arrangement of the Sefirot</note>. This means: with the "arousal" <note>The "arousal" or *m'orer* refers to the initial movement of the Divine Will.</note>. Therefore, he sat and said: "ten and not eleven," and this explains "ten and not nine." We know that the Pivot <note>original: *Goral* or *Galgal*; referring to the central axis of a system</note> does not stand alone except through the diagonals, and the pivot of all the "feet" <note>Metaphorical supports or foundations of the emanations.</note> stands only through the diagonals. 

Lest you say that the pivot is not included among the diagonals—for the number of the weeks <note>original: *shavuot*</note> is not this, and the "foot" is only nine—he comes to inform you: ten and not nine. Not nine on the right, but rather ten in the right hand and right foot. "Ten and not nine" in the left hand and left foot. "Ten and not eighteen," so that you do not think the tongue is combined with the diagonals to make seventeen, or the "arousal" is combined with the diagonals to make eighteen. Therefore it is said: "ten and not eighteen." And so too in the number ten: the diagonals are ten, and not eighteen. 

Generally, just as there is a number in the **World**, and just as there is in the **Soul**, so too in the **Year** <note>This refers to the "Olam, Shanah, Nefesh" (World, Year, Soul) triad, a fundamental concept in *Sefer Yetzirah* stating that the same divine patterns repeat in space, time, and biology.</note>. There are those who say these are the ten spheres of the Chariot <note>original: *galgaley ha-merkhavah*</note>, and some say they are the ten simple essences <note>original: *ikhuyot*</note>... diagonals. And regarding the "Year," it was not explained in all the ten because it is divided and prepared. The scholar said that the "Year" is time, and time is a concept within the movement of a specific star, its foundation, and its number. This number is measured according to the movement of the spheres. 

Each one of them has a unique movement; therefore, the Year and time are measured by every sphere and the count of its movement. For example: the Lunar Year is the time it takes for its sphere to complete a circuit, which is twenty-seven days, eight hours, and 434 parts <note>A traditional Jewish measurement of time where an hour is divided into 1080 parts (*halakim*).</note>. The Solar Year is 365 days and six hours. And so it is with every single sphere, and even with the Spheres of the Chariot. Even in this, there is "ten and not nine," so that you do not say that because the movement of the fourth sphere is not perceptible and its movement is unknown, it shouldn't be counted. Lest you say that Heaven forbid <note>original: *chas v'shalom*</note> no number applies to it at all and there are only nine Sefirot in the Year—therefore it says: "ten and not nine." And lest you say that just as the Fourth is not perceptible in number, so too the Cause of Causes <note>The ultimate source of God, the *Ein Sof*.</note> should be included in the count, making them eleven—Heaven forbid—therefore it says: "not eleven."

Regarding Wisdom <note>original: *Hokhmah*</note>, he did not say "explore all the ends of the world," because thought is forbidden from investigating there, whether in the World, the Year, or the Soul. As it is said: "Do not seek what is too wondrous for you." And our Sages, of blessed memory, said: "From one end of the heavens to the other end of the heavens you may ask," but you may not ask what is above <note>The spiritual realms</note>, what is below <note>The abyss</note>, what is before <note>Before creation</note>, or what is behind <note>The end of time</note>.

Similarly, regarding Wisdom, in the matter of the powers of the soul: we already know that the brain is divided into three parts. The front part, closest to the forehead, is the peak of spirituality, where all things are imagined... there the dreams appear. The middle part corresponds to the diagonals... within it is the power of the intellect and the understanding of sciences and all crafts. This is the "Thinking Power." And the part in the back of the head contains the "Power of Memory" and "Preservation." 

The "Soul-Spirit" <note>original: *ruach ha-nafshi*</note> resides between the membranes. There is the "Power of Imagination" and "Thought." Know that this power is the force behind all crafts. In the body, it corresponds to the "Higher Crown" <note>The Sefirah of *Keter*</note>, which contains all the powers... Wisdom, Understanding, Knowledge, Sight, Hearing, Smell, Taste, Touch, and Will. 

Lest you say that because the Will is not perceptible, there are only nine—Heaven forbid—therefore it says "ten and not nine." And lest you say the Intellect is also included in the count, it says "ten and not eleven." 

So it is with Wisdom: he did not say "investigate with the Intellect," because the Intellect is included [within the Sefirot] and no other power from the powers of the soul can be imagined within it. However, all the powers of the soul that are divided in the soul are all built and exist through the "Power of the Dwelling" <note>original: *koach ha-shekhinah*; the Divine Presence as it dwells within the soul.</note> and through Wisdom. All these nine powers are the agents of all crafts within the Power of the Shekhinah, which is the tenth among them, like a queen among them.

# Ra’avad, of blessed memory — Chapter 1, Mishnah 4 — Rambam, of blessed memory
<meta>catchword: ten</meta>

The explanation of “all that you occupy yourself with in Wisdom and Understanding” <note>original: *Chokhmah* and *Binah*; these are the second and third Sefirot, representing the spark of intuition and the analytical development of that intuition.</note> is as follows: it means you must examine, scrutinize, and stand upon the ultimate purpose and the secret of Greatness and Power <note>original: *Gedulah* and *Gevurah*; technical terms for the Sefirot of expansive Love and restrictive Strength.</note> most intensely. The end of action is found in Wisdom and Understanding, for your beloved ones and your pious ones are enslaved to investigate, observe, scrutinize, and clarify through your Wisdom. You have been refined as one refines **silver** (a metaphor) and in the testing-crucibles as one tests **gold**. 

Therefore, it said “such as they are,” meaning with the urgency found in Wisdom and Understanding. Similarly, Greatness and Power shall be enacted through Wisdom and Understanding, for they are the source from which they originate. The explanation: when you have reached the knowledge of the roots of Greatness and Power through Wisdom and Understanding, you are further obligated to investigate from Greatness and Power the kindness you have attained through Wisdom—the very edge of comprehension. This is achieved through the power of Wisdom and Understanding, according to their ability to draw out the forces from the power of Greatness and Power within them. Therefore, it said, “a source *from* them” and did not say “a source *in* them,” just as it said “such as they are.”

**Establish a matter on its clarity.** The explanation: a matter that has been clarified before Him. And for the four-letter Name <note>The Tetragrammaton, the four-letter divine name YHWH.</note>, the word “pure” etc. is used. When it is mentioned thus, the “source” is an expression of glory <note>original: *shitiya*; likely referring to the *Even Shetiya*, the Foundation Stone of the world.</note>, meaning that a matter is told to him in a vision and not as a mere command. When you reach all these levels, you must look into the pens of the Sages <note>The "pens of the Sages" refers to their written traditions and transmissions of wisdom.</note> to know its source and establish it upon its planting-place. This is why it says “foundation,” for the translation of “our planting-place” is “its clarity” <note>original: *boriyu*.</note>. **And return the Creator to His place.** The explanation: Give to Mercy <note>original: *Tiferet*; the Sefirah of Beauty/Mercy.</note>, which is called the “Creator, daughter of Understanding,” His place. These arrive at the foundation, and all these levels are within the powers of Wisdom and Understanding. And concerning the “revolving,” it says “it shall turn as a help and not as a planting.” The explanation: The Greatness is removed from the general refinement because as long as it does not stand in the Law of Kindness, it is diminished from the number **ten**. This is to warn you about the ten wisdoms, that none are missing from the number ten. In the investigation, stand and let it not be removed. This is the teaching of the Sages who clarify and ascend.

---

If you do not find as much of the world in your place, treat it as a sickness. And begin with the "Desire of Souls" and the Eternal Life <note>original: *Chayei HaNetzach*.</note>, which is proven to be refined upon the furnace. You shall establish Him and support Him upon His base. This is the matter: give your understanding to this example. For if the "Grace" <note>original: *Chen*.</note> given to the understanding were a physical body, every body would have an end, but the "Sickness" <note>In this context, likely a metaphor for the longing of the soul.</note> has no end, for its power is loftier than any accident attached to matter. And this is the meaning of "what likeness" <note>Referring to the conceptual or imaginary.</note>—"To what likeness will you compare Him?" <note>A quote from Isaiah 40:18, emphasizing God's incorporeality.</note> For He is alone in His loftiness and His remembrance. 

It is appropriate to speak of "hands" regarding something that has substance, but concerning something that has no substance, his "holiness" proves it, for the **mouth** is more holy, and the force of the **spirit** <note>original: *ruach*; can mean wind, breath, or spirit.</note> is greater. As for what is said regarding the "spirit of life within him," this refers to the formation of the body's vessels that receive the power of the spirit, which are the brain and the heart. This is especially true in the thought of the wise, the contemplative, and the one who troubles himself to think deeply. To every voice of the thinker, [He examines] every heart and all thoughts.

And all this was taught by the Great Rabbi, Rabbi Abraham, before the Academy of Babylon. And Rabbi Bahya, of blessed memory, wrote: This is the meaning of "**Prepare with Wisdom and be wise with Understanding**" in the matter of investigation. This Sefirah of **Understanding** (*Binah*) is the one that follows the Sefirah of **Wisdom** (*Chokhmah*). In the *Great Book*, it says the word "Prepare" (*hachon*) is used because preparation is more significant than existence, for preparation is the act of preparing one thing from within another. Therefore, it is associated with the Sefirah of Wisdom, to say that it was "hewn" from the Supernal Crown <note>original: *Keter Elyon*; the highest Sefirah.</note>, and from that Sefirah, the **thirty-two wondrous paths of Wisdom** branch out. All of existence is included in the great branch of the Sefirah of Wisdom, and this Sefirah is the root of everything, culminating in the thirty-two paths. And "**be wise with Understanding**" refers to the beginning of the Sefirah of Wisdom, for this Sefirah appears in action through the paths of Wisdom. If so, there is no "end of Wisdom" without Understanding; therefore he said, "Prepare with Wisdom." And there is no "end of Understanding" without Wisdom; therefore he said, "be wise with Understanding." This is the conclusion of his words.

# Ra’avad, of blessed memory | Chapter 1, Mishnah 4

**Ten** <note>original: "עשר" (Eser)</note> meaning: you must examine how sight, hearing, smell, taste, touch, and speech—even though they are actions distinct from one another—are all capable of and submissive to the power of **Wisdom** <term>Chochmah; the Sefirah representing the first flash of intellect or the root of consciousness</term>, which is intertwined with them all. These senses themselves derive from a Higher Power, which is a single force; therefore, they all stem from one power. Thus, all these functions appear similar, though they differ in their sensory manifestation through the physical vessel assigned to them, their source, and their secret. 

Meaning: even though each of them uses its specific vessel—such as sight for the eyes and hearing for the ears—and even though there is no "sight" for the ears nor "hearing" for the eyes, you must investigate and know that these divisions do not exist from the perspective of the Simple Power <note>The unified spiritual energy before it is filtered through the body</note>, but rather from the perspective of the vessels <note>The physical organs</note>. Therefore, it is said in several places that their names are interchangeable, one in place of the other, as it is written: "See the smell of my son" <note>Genesis 27:27; where Isaac uses the verb for seeing to describe a scent</note>, and "All the people saw the voices" <note>Exodus 20:18; the Israelites "seeing" the sound of the Shofar at Mount Sinai</note>. 

And "establish the matter clearly" <note>literally "on its clarity/purity"</note> means: every single action among the actions of the soul, you must establish it upon its specific reality as the Higher Power within the soul. And "return the Creator to His place" <note>a phrase from the Mishnah of Sefer Yetzirah suggesting that understanding the creation leads back to the Creator</note> means: from within the soul you can understand how the Creator of all (may He be blessed) acts within all the mechanisms <note>or "structures"</note> and leads each of them according to His vision.

**Ten Sefirot of Nothingness: ten and not nine.** Meaning: behold, there are five corresponding to the parts of the right hand of the soul, and the parts of the spleen of the winged creature <note>a symbolic anatomical reference common in medieval Jewish mysticism</note>; five against five "clenchings" <note>referring to the fingers of the hand</note>. And in the right foot there are ten segments and not nine; rather, the thumb of the hand is attached, its movement stands in the order of the segments of the number. And there are six joints in them, and with the body on the right side it is seven. And the **Covenant of Circumcision** <term>Brit Milah</term> is the decider <note>the balancing point</note>, and the **Voice** is the decider between the upper tongue <note>the mouth</note> and the lower tongue <note>the reproductive organ</note>, and between the five upper fingers and the five lower toes. They are also called "five," as our Rabbis of blessed memory said regarding "five pieces of death" <note>A reference to the laws of ritual slaughter (Shechitah) regarding the lungs</note>. Therefore, it is ten, and not eleven, nor seven, nor fifty, nor twenty. And five for the hand and foot, and the "cutting" <note>the covenant</note> of the hand, and not eighteen or twelve. And there are six joints of the right hand and foot.

->Six joints of the left hand and foot; examine with Wisdom, for<-
->**Understanding** <term>Binah</term> decides between the **Supreme Crown** <term>Keter Elyon</term> and **Wisdom**, for she<-
->receives from both of them. And be wise in **Understanding**, for **Wisdom**<-
->receives everything from the **Supreme Crown** and influences<-
->everything into **Understanding**. So too in the soul,<-
->there are parts that receive, and there are<-
->those that influence,<-

whose relationship to the number is five, meaning to say they are six. And they also wrote regarding the number as corresponding to the "atonement of the fifth" <note>Leviticus 5:16; the requirement to add a fifth to restitution in the Temple</note>, to say for the number seven, and it is also related to the number five. And this is "nine"... all these are to "establish the matter clearly" and "to return the Creator to His place." **Ten.**

## The Ra’avad, of blessed memory <note>Rabbi Abraham ben David of Posquières, a 12th-century legalist and mystic</note>

As part of the whole, and from it they cascade down; for the more the subject rises from level to level, the more the upper level becomes refined and purified compared to that which is below it. Thus they ascend and become more subtle until the Infinite <note>original: *Ein Sof*</note>. And because it [the Sefirah] has risen to the Cause, may He be blessed, and is not distant from any thing, it too is equal within the whole. Therefore, it taught ten [Sefirot] to indicate they have an end. **Depth of Beginning:** The explanation of "beginning" is Wisdom <note>original: *Chokmah*</note>, as it is written: "The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord" (Psalm 111:10), for it is the beginning of all existing things. And it is the "end of thought" <note>A kabbalistic principle: "The end of action was first in thought"</note> like the relationship of matter to the Creator, and like the concept of Reception <note>original: *Kabbalah*</note> which is a "garland of grace" <note>Proverbs 1:9</note>, the level of the beginning of all the letters. And this is the secret of "My heart is first," and it is fitting to call it "first" because it is "something from nothing" <note>original: *yesh me-ayin*</note>. In this way, it is the first of number, for number cannot be grasped as it is understood. And because the accompaniments and the attributes fall within the definition of measurement, it was necessary to tell you: do not say He has a literal measurement; therefore, he said "Depth." **The explanation of Depth:** Every "beginning" has no measurement, and likewise, each and every one of its parts has depths, and nothing is attached to them. For all the depths are drawn from the Upper Thought; from the general depth within it are its hewings, and its quarry has no end, therefore all the depths have no end. And because it mentioned ten, it shows they have an end to say that they correspond to the Chariot <note>original: *Merkavah*, referring to the divine vision in Ezekiel</note> which is within Wisdom. He mentioned corresponding to them "depths" for every land in every sphere, and corresponding to the sphere of death <gloss>the physical world</gloss> to the "height and below" <gloss>the vertical axis</gloss> for depth. And it is known that circles have no beginning, and the measurements from the perspective of the circle are not from the perspective of its physical end. So too are the Separated Intellects <note>Angels or purely spiritual beings</note>; they are to it as matter... like the mixture of wisdom. And that which has no "how much" <note>quantity</note> cannot be said to have a beginning or an end. And this is the secret of the **Depth of Beginning**, to diminish change and a distant ascent, and [to provide] a foundation for all existing things in the way of the hidden <note>the mystical path</note>.

---

## The Ram"b, of blessed memory <note>Likely referring here to the commentary of Moses Botril, who is cited in this column</note>

To know this: Depth of Height, Depth of Below—to know to what extent His reality was, and the place of his prophecy from beneath the earth. **Depth of East and Depth of West:** He mentions East first because it is the "Face" <note>In biblical Hebrew, "East" (*Kedem*) also means "front"</note> and the West is the "Back." **Depth of North:** [He mentions it] first because it is the secret of the inhabited world, while the South is desolate. And this is what Abraham our Father said to the sages of his generation: because one cannot know His dominion, to what extent it reaches, [it is] the **Depth of Good**, the secret of the permissible, for He rules in the East, West, North, and South. But regarding the language of "good," anything outside of Him, He rules over it—meaning, "Depth of Good" teaches us that He, may He be exalted, is "before it," meaning above it, and there is nothing else before Him. And from this you may say of the good that so-and-so's voice rules over all; but of the evil, that so-and-so does not rule over it, for that is the **Depth of Evil**. And if you say this, it is as they said: all of them are ten depths corresponding to the ten Sefirot. **To a Unique Judge:** For He has no "face" <note>no human likeness or front/back distinction</note>, and this is what Solomon said: "And also both of them, do not join" <note>Ecclesiastes 7:18, interpreted here as not mixing the divine essence with these dimensions</note>. **Faithful King:** And His kingdom is for all time, and He rules in all the depths from His holy dwelling place forever and ever. "M" [for] Dwelling Place <note>original: *Ma'on*</note>—a place, as in "Lord, You have been our dwelling place" (Psalm 90:1). And likewise, "You have made the Most High your dwelling place" (Psalm 91:9). Or it means the dwelling of the "Lamp of the Eye" <note>referring to divine providence</note>, as it is explained according to the verse: "You have been a dwelling place for us," meaning the eyes of all mankind are hanging upon Him by way of the "Watcher of the Heavens," for the eye of man is toward the Lord forever. Therefore, one should not think "how much" ... Moses Botril said in *Blumah* <note>Botril's commentary on Sefer Yetzirah</note> that it is the seal of the "Place" <note>a name for God</note>, a good thing, not wisdom. And the great Rabbi, Rabbi Chasdai the Kabbalist <note>Likely Rabbi Chasdai Crescas, 1340–1410</note>, explained this: that the matter is entirely translated... a small endeavor for a great one to do... from the secrets of the one who teaches the wise man from his learning... and thus he said:

# The Commentary of the Ramban, of blessed memory, Chapter 1, Mishnah 6; The Commentary of the Ra’avad, of blessed memory

**The ten Sefirot of nothingness: their appearance is like the flash of lightning, and their end has no limit. His word is in them in running and returning <term>Ratzo v’Shuv - a concept from Ezekiel 1:14 describing the soul's oscillation between divine ecstasy and physical reality</term>, and at His command they pursue like a storm, and before His throne they prostrate themselves.**

(Right Column - The Ra'avad)
The explanation of the Great Rabbi, the Kabbalist, Rabbi Isaac ben [Abraham] <note>original: "Isaac ben Pr'"; this refers to Rabbi Isaac the Blind, a foundational figure in early Kabbalah</note>:
**The ten Sefirot of nothingness: their appearance is like the flash of lightning, and their end has no limit. His word is in them in running and returning, and at His command they pursue like a storm, and before His throne they prostrate themselves.** Look at it this way: this is an example and a secret for a person to apply his mind to them instead of his usual foundation of study, **lest he cut the shoots** <note>A Talmudic metaphor for falling into heresy while studying mystical secrets</note> in the vacuum and fall defeated. Therefore, he chose to speak of the ten Sefirot and the engagement with His word as something that **runs and returns**. This power and spirit from the attribute of the *Chayot* <note>The "Living Creatures" or angels from Ezekiel's vision of the Divine Chariot</note> do what they do through "running and returning," for they are like souls in their stature. So too shall the person who investigates this wonderful secret do: he should seek to investigate this with clear wine <note>A metaphor for pure, refined intellect</note>, for the King cannot be contained. For their end has no limit, but is broad like the nature of the sea. They do the will of their Creator and pursue after Him like a storm. Thus—

<column-break/>

(Left Column - The Ram"b <note>Likely referring here to the "Rabbi of the Binah," a title sometimes associated with the school of Ramban or his disciples</note>)
And from their wings "like the flash of lightning." This refers to the bodies of the perceptions of the Sefirot, bodies that are woven into one another. And the "appearance" there is like the flash of lightning, like the light that emerges from between shards <note>Original: "cherasim." The author compares divine light to light glimpsed through the cracks of broken pottery</note>. And the explanation of this: if you take a sieve that has very fine holes across its entire surface, and you place a shard over it and blow on it slightly until it ignites, and the light passes through the paths of the holes—in every single hole, flames appear as if they are gazing out, in all the colors of the world, descending through the paths of the holes. So too are the wings of the *Chayot* in the paths of those *Chayot* which are above them. For there is a Throne for the Throne and Glory for the Glory. They are in their wings, and in the language of the intermediate [world] it is described as various kinds of properties. Out of the fear of their reach, they are perceived immediately as "running and returning." They are perceived like a flash of lightning, which appears and disappears in the blink of an eye, or like threads that rise and fall in the blink of an eye. From here, the masters of the Secret Name <note>original: "Ba'alei Hashem" - mystics and wonder-workers</note> said: Do not look at anything except that which looks at you. And immediately look back to the ground... and covered thus, and covered—

---

->The Commentary of the Ramban <note>Rabbi Moses ben Nahman, 13th-century scholar</note>, of blessed memory<-

**Their appearance:** The perception itself is its "body" within them. **Like the flash of lightning:** It does not say "it is the appearance" but "like the appearance." Likewise, "and a portion in the eye" <note>likely a reference to visual perception</note> is only for contemplating and looking at a thing to satisfy the researcher's knowledge. **The lightning:** This is like that which is found in the [heavenly] furnace. **And their end:** That which is included in the flash, for it is without end. For their end has no limit; any defined thing that has a measure is said to have an "end," but anything that has no measurable scale is considered "infinite." **His word is in them in running and returning:** The explanation is that the one who delights in them raises his perception to look at their light and their whiteness with longing; but the one who looks at the Exalted and at each one individually and does not stand still in his perception is called "His word" which is above them. He rises to receive the command of the Will in extra-abundant sources, in "running and returning." **And at His command:** For those who receive the teaching of longing also **pursue like a storm.** **And before His throne they prostrate themselves:** This is the turning of the Will toward the Face <note>The inner aspect of the Divine</note>. All their "going out" is the going out of the power sent from above to below. My language here refers to the receiving of the "face" [presence], for their bodies were in it in order to receive His word. And its "life" <note>or vitality</note> is the power sent from the Word to the messenger. It is like the metaphor of a scribe: the words draw the power to the author through the speed of the creation. The Word and the messenger **prostrate before His throne**—which means to behold the Glory—they bow down.

<summary>This page explores the paradoxical nature of perceiving the Sefirot, using the metaphor of a "flash of lightning" to describe how divine light is both revealed and concealed. It warns of the dangers of mystical study while explaining the "running and returning" (oscillation) of the soul and the angels as they pursue the infinite Divine Will.</summary>
<keywords>Sefirot, lightning, running and returning, Isaac the Blind, Ramban, Chayot, divine throne, mystical perception, infinity</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the commentary on the first chapter of Sefer Yetzirah (The Book of Formation). While the previous page focused on the "Running and Returning" of the Sefirot as described by the Ra’avad and Rabbi Isaac the Blind, this page shifts to a philosophical and astronomical interpretation attributed here to the Rambam (Maimonides), though it incorporates diverse sources to explain the spatial dimensions of "North" and "South" mentioned in the text.</meta>

# Chapter 1: The Rambam, of blessed memory, on the Mishnah

One [force] is like the source of existing things and all the causes for the preservation of the species. The other acts in the opposite manner, and their entire intent and aim is to indicate the nature of **privation** <note>original: "גרס המעדר" - a medieval philosophical term referring to the absence of existence or form</note>. If so, [one might think] they existed as two: one perceiver for the Northern side and one perceiver for the Southern side. Therefore, our father Abraham said, in opposition to those [dualist] sages, **"The Depth of North"** and **"The Depth of South."** This means to say: He [God] perceives the North, and He also perceives the South, even though they are opposites. 

For it is known to the **astronomers** <term>chachmei ha-tekunah - scholars of celestial movements and geography</term> that in the South there is no habitation throughout the sixteen degrees, as written by **Ptolemy**, **Al-Battani**, **Al-Farghani**, and **Ibn Ezra**. To us, the sun [provides] ten degrees, which are therefore inhabited in every way because of its expansion there. And these sixteen degrees of whiteness <note>possibly referring to the "white" or illuminated zones of the spheres</note> are included in the calculation of the **seven climates** <term>aklimos - the traditional Greek division of the habitable world into seven latitudinal zones</term> according to the opinion of **Eudoxus** and his division. 

And for the sages of Greece and India, it was difficult [to understand] because the sun moves from the center of the earth toward the Southern side by two degrees; this is the "good temperament" for wisdom, and it brings forth spiritual matters from the side of the brain. As our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said in **Tractate Temurah**: "Why was his name called **Caleb**? Because he was completed with every good <note>A wordplay on 'Caleb' (Kaleb) and 'Kol Lev' (all heart/goodness)</note>." And the "Northern Lamp" brings forth physical matters, and that is the South <note>The text here appears to be contrasting the symbolic directions of the Tabernacle</note>. 

Your sign for this is: **"The Table is in the North, and the Menorah (Lampstand) is in the South."** For the Table hints at physical things <note>sustenance and wealth</note>, and the inhabited world is Northern. The Table signifies "honor," from the expression "and he sent," which we translate [into Aramaic] as *v'yishlach*. This means to say that whoever focuses his involvement on physical things and is a slave to his desires is **stripped** of wisdom; divinity then rests upon "matter stripped of form." 

For when a person is complete, it is proper for his perfection to be in the **intellectual virtues**, as the wise **Plato** said, and also **Aristotle**. An allusion to this was the Menorah being in the South, for wisdom is compared to light, as it is said: "A man's wisdom makes his face shine." **Light** is a "possession" <term>kinyan - an acquired habit or reality</term>, and **darkness** is "privation" <term>he'eder - the absence of existence</term>. In this way, wisdom is a possession and folly is the privation of wisdom. A possession has superiority over privation. 

The Menorah had **seven lamps**, corresponding to the **seven wisdoms** <note>The "Seven Liberal Arts" or branches of knowledge recognized in the Middle Ages</note>. And since the Northern aspect is the opposite of the Southern, the Sages of blessed memory said in the Midrash regarding the verse "And it was evening and it was morning, one day": This means the Holy One, blessed be He, was alone in His world, so that people would not say there are "two authorities," one ruling the North and the other the South. This is why our father Abraham said: **"Depth of North and Depth of South."**

->Single Master, God, Faithful King, Ruler—here are six rings to hint<-
->at the six directions of His holy Tabernacle; He closes upon all existing reality<-
->to negate the view of one who says Providence has ceased in the voids<-
->against these [directions]. Thus far the words of the Rabbi,<-
->Isaac bar Samuel in the book *Ketav Paz*:<-

# The Ra’avad, of blessed memory – Chapter 1, Mishnah 6 [Page 46]

The Sefirot: Kindness <gloss>Chesed</gloss> is included within the Beauty <gloss>Tiferet</gloss> which is called "Speech." Every single Sefirah among them is meant to **run and return** <term>ratzo va-shov — a mystical concept from the vision of Ezekiel describing the movement of divine energy as a constant oscillation between revelation and concealment</term>. The meaning of **running** is Wisdom <gloss>Chokhmah</gloss> and the meaning of **returning** is Understanding <gloss>Binah</gloss>, based on the words "desire" <note>original: ratzon, a wordplay on ratzo/running</note> and "repentance" <note>original: teshuvah, a wordplay on shov/returning</note>. 

Just as ten "depths" were mentioned in the previous Mishnah, so too you must apply ten instances of **running and returning** to the Foundation <gloss>Yesod</gloss> and to everything included within them. Likewise, you must understand the **running and returning** for each and every one of them in the Beauty <gloss>Tiferet</gloss> hidden within the Sefirot. Regarding the concept of **returning**, whenever it is explained in the context of "forever" (Nehemiah 6), its end "they shall pursue," <note>original: yirdefu</note> meaning and for the "Crown" <gloss>Atarah/Malchut</gloss> which is called "The Utterance" <note>original: Ma'amar</note>. 

You must understand that just as there is a **running and returning** within the Crown <gloss>Keter</gloss> and all its details, so too there is a likeness of **running and returning** in all the generalities of the Diadem <gloss>Atarah</gloss> and all its details. In the **running** is their end, and in the **returning** is their descent, as it is said: "In the whirlwind and in the storm is His way" (Nahum 1:3), which refers to a powerful wind. **Running and returning**: and it is said, "In the whirlwind they shall pursue," <note>original: be-sufah yirdefu</note> meaning the Splendor <gloss>Tiferet</gloss> and <gloss>sign</gloss> their descent to achieve more through Mercy <gloss>meaning Binah</gloss>. 

"And before His throne" means the emanations of Kindness <gloss>Chesed</gloss> are the "face" of the throne of Understanding <gloss>Binah</gloss>, for the throne of Understanding is what is called Beauty <gloss>Tiferet</gloss> and the Diadem <gloss>Atarah</gloss>. And the "sons of His throne" are Crown <gloss>Keter</gloss> and Wisdom <gloss>Chokhmah</gloss>. **They prostrate**: meaning the Speech <gloss>Tiferet</gloss> and <gloss>sign</gloss> and the Diadem <gloss>Atarah</gloss> prostrate to the Crown <gloss>Keter</gloss> and Wisdom <gloss>Chokhmah</gloss> to bring down the abundance of flow <term>shefa — divine influence or energy</term> upon all existing things. They "call to Him" because everything came into being from Him, as it says in the Mishnah above: "He rules over them all from His holy dwelling until the end of ends." 

Therefore, "Speak of them in running and returning," meaning when you reflect and finalize your thoughts in the attainment of the Sefirot, you have permission to speak of them. **Wisdom** <note>Chokhmah</note> in **running and returning**: as the investigation prior to Wisdom is better than the Wisdom of Understanding <gloss>Binah</gloss>, and they received it as Wisdom... But do not send your thoughts into the hidden and concealed, for thought is forbidden from reflecting there. 

A wise person should pursue the "Crown of Crown" <gloss>Atarah of Keter</gloss> "in the whirlwind," to attain it and reflect upon it. "And before His throne they prostrate" refers to the inner aspect and all the dominions. **And returning**: he sealed <gloss>Wisdom and Understanding</gloss> with the signet of the heavens <gloss>Binah and Tiferet</gloss> and the earth <gloss>Malchut</gloss> and all Kindness upon it... and the seal of the "Gathering of Water" <note>Mikveh</note> beneath them all. "The heavens prostrate to You" <gloss>meaning Binah prostrates to Wisdom and Crown</gloss>. 

"And their appearance is like a flash of lightning" (Ezekiel 1:14) and "their end has no limit." If you say the rest of the soul in God has no end in investigation, how then can it say "their end has no limit"? One can say that every soul, by virtue of being a soul, must necessarily have a "sending out." In any case, it is the way of the "Dominions" to be an intermediate thing <term>memutza</term> between two opposites. Just as with salt, which "returns" to its source: from its own side it connects to man, but from the side of its moisture it connects to water; and the salt is an intermediary between water and man, which are two opposites. 

So too in the matter of the Intellects <term>Sechalim</term> and the Bodies <term>Gufim</term>, there is an intermediate species that is drawn out, which are intermediaries between the Soul <gloss>Nefesh</gloss> and the Intellect. Do you not see that for intermediate things, we say of every "horse" and "soul" that it is a soul, but what is not a horse and is perishable is not a soul?

# The Ra’avad, of blessed memory – Chapter 1, Mishnah 6 [and] the Ramban, of blessed memory

Thus, Isaac <note>Rabbi Isaac the Blind, a 12th-century mystic and a central figure in the early development of Kabbalah</note> who meditates on this sublime and good light, draws sustenance from all of it, and it returns and strengthens before him like celestial dwellings. It is a clinging finer than anything thin. Any lack or distance regarding those who are upright <note>referring to the righteous or those with focused intent</note> is where the Divine Presence <gloss>Shekhinah</gloss> encompasses him. This is the "branch of the Sefirot." The intention <note>of the mystic</note> does not descend below ten <note>referring to the ten Sefirot, the fundamental divine emanations</note>, God forbid; for if it did, there would not be ten Sefirot. Thus far are the words of the Ra’avad, of blessed memory, the Kabbalist who was the teacher of the Ramban <note>Rabbi Moses ben Nahman, also known as Nahmanides</note>. And Rabbeinu Bahya, of blessed memory, in his book of *Expositions* <note>referring to *Kad ha-Kemach* or perhaps his commentary on the Torah</note>, explains regarding the **Expanse of the End** <term>Merchav HaSof — a technical term describing the vast, yet bounded, realm of the Sefirot</term>:

The change within the **Expanse of the End** is like a flash of lightning, for there is no place for a moment's delay, as all of this is established as "pure kindness." And behold, we find that our Sages of blessed memory said: Rabbi Yehuda says, just as Rabbi Simon said in the name of Rabbi Levi ben Perata: it is like a cup that is sparkling. Or like one who stirs a large sieve, which flares up in appearance and sends up a flame, rising and falling. And "flashing" <note>original: bazak, from Ezekiel 1:14</note> is a term for scattering, as in "they scattered the coals and they moved." And what did the Sages mean by **Running and Returning**? Rabbi Yehuda said: it is like the spark that flies out from the furnace. What is meant by the **Expanse of the End**? Rabbi Yosi bar Hanina said: like the spark that emerges from between the pottery shards. And following the verse "They run to and fro like lightning" (Nahum 2:5), the Sages took the word **Running** <gloss>ratzo</gloss> as an exchange for the word "spark" <gloss>zak</gloss>, for it is a matter of movement, as in "and he ran with him." Thus far his words.

<column-break/>

"And he gazes at the earth"—know that he is in great awe. And if his eyes do not turn away from you, yet his heart gazes at the earth, know that he is directing his heart toward you. In this way, it is said that "the dream shall not be enlarged," and "who can change the vision of the Temple for his dream?" And this is the secret of "in their appearance in the Expanse of the End." Their appearance is not "suspended" <note>meaning arbitrary</note>; rather, it means their perception is within the **Expanse of the End**. And the "End" changes according to the appearance of the dream:

If the dream is of a star, the "End" <note>the perceived limit of the light</note> is a star, and there is a pure white spark. If it is blue, there is a blue spark. If it is as white as snow, there is a snow-white spark. If it is green, there is a green spark. If it is red, there is a red spark. And such is the law for all other shades of colors and mixtures. And this is the simplicity within the **Expanse of the End**, according to its simple meaning. He who is uniquely able to gaze upon these holy lights will know that sometimes they will sparkle toward him until it seems to him as if there is an "End" in the **Expanse of the End**, and immediately they are hidden; and again they sparkle, and again they are hidden.

"And their purpose has no end"—the explanation is that you already know that all these colors—for example, white and black—can be weakened or strengthened by Kindness <gloss>Chesed</gloss>. If the refined color is darkened, the color that becomes clear between the two of them is a mixture of white and black; therefore, it is not truly white nor truly black. Therefore it said: the purpose of the Sefirot has no end, yet it has an "end," for the shade is mixed from both of them.

This means you have seen an "end" to the total number which includes them, which is ten; yet you have seen that there is no "end" to their count <note>original: minyan</note>, for it includes all the particulars and all the generals. And just as we said regarding the "Depths of Thought," that the heart’s thought and the depth have no end from the perspective of the eye—all of it is a power within them. So too, "the secret of your wisdom is from Understanding <gloss>Binah</gloss> unto the world." The "half-end" of their number has a known limit, which is ten. You have seen that the limit to their purpose has no end because all numbers are included within ten, whether they are particulars or generals. And since this is the case in the nature of Wisdom <gloss>Chokhmah</gloss> and Understanding <gloss>Binah</gloss>, they are like one who aims for their purpose. Thus, there is no end, for they extend until the Infinite <gloss>Ein Sof</gloss>. 

The general rule: In the hidden world, from Understanding <gloss>Binah</gloss> and below, there is no end. And there is no distinction or separation between the "Intellector" and the "Intellected" <note>A philosophical concept where the mind, the process of thinking, and the object of thought become one in the divine realm</note> regarding the higher realm. As it was said above, "you have seen an end for them" to hint at the whole; but it is not according to this judgment that it said "they have no end," for this hints at the Infinite. They spoke here in hints, and this is a good explanation of the Sefirot.

# The Ramban, of blessed memory — Chapter 1, Mishnah 7 — The Ra’avad, of blessed memory

At the beginning and as a praise, so that you do not think otherwise: He is a Unique Master and has no second <note>original: "Adon Yachid ve-ein lo sheni." This emphasizes absolute monotheism, asserting that even within the complexity of the ten Sefirot, God remains a singular unity.</note>. The explanation of His existence and how all of His beginning is the "depth of the start" serves to warn you that His end is in His beginning and His beginning is in His end. You should not think of Him as a "end" in the sense of a temporal conclusion, for He existed before His "end" according to His nature and His host, as it is written. Therefore, read the matter as: "His end is in His beginning and His beginning is in His end," for He is one power standing within Himself, and He has no second in His end.

And if you wonder what the depth of the power is that I intend regarding the "Value of the Gate" <note>likely referring to a specific mystical calculation or a level of divine emanation</note>, there is no "afterwards" associated with Him. Thus, the intellect remains in these matters as it was at the beginning, saying: there is no number to His unity, nor plurality, nor change, nor place, nor boundaries. Just as the end is such, so is the beginning; just as the beginning is such, so is the end.

**"Like a flame bound to a coal"** <note>A famous metaphor from Sefer Yetzirah 1:7. It suggests that just as a flame cannot exist without the coal, and the heat of the coal is only manifest through the flame, the Sefirot are inseparable from the Divine Essence.</note>. The judgment is in the heart, for life exists between him and the power he wrote of in the coal; because the Unity is not hidden, the "One" ascends, but the end of His effect is an effect. And since the flame comes and is attached to the coal more and more, the flame is unique; therefore, one must yield to the "Closure of the World" <note>likely referring to the hidden nature of the Infinite (Ein Sof)</note>. This is the secret of "His mouth is like a high place" <note>paraphrasing a mystical reading of a verse</note> within the bond of Unity, and He has no second—meaning, there is no duality associated with Him at all.

In the Midrash on the verse in Ecclesiastes <note>Ecclesiastes 4:8</note>: *"There is one and no second,"* this refers to the Holy One, Blessed be He. <gloss>Wisdom is unique, [within] Understanding</gloss> and He has no <gloss>Understanding</gloss> second <gloss>Yod <note>The letter Yod often represents Wisdom (Chokhmah)</note></gloss>. This is what is meant by: "Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is One." <gloss>Regarding "The Lord"</gloss> for the builder receives the "Coldness of Wisdom" <note>a technical term for a specific stage of emanation where the "heat" of creation is tempered</note> because before "One," what do you count? The first level is Wisdom, like a unique Understanding. And through it, which is called a "pledge," it is unique. And the verse "Hear" has no other explanation; see the "170 levels" <note>unclear reference, possibly a numerical value for a specific divine name</note> second to the "Anointing." For Israel shall dwell with their Master; "One" <term>Echad — the Hebrew word for One</term> is a hint to the Sabbath of His existence in a "simple year" <note>referring to the cosmic cycles or the "World" dimension of Sefer Yetzirah</note>.

In the combination of the secret of the calculation, the first letters [acronym] of "God" <note>El</note>: **"And before one, what do you count?"** For within it are the tablets of Wisdom, because He is the one who bestows number; it does not fall upon something that has independent existence, nor upon something that is nothing, except that He is the Ruler of these seven and these wrappings. And in the combination of the secret of the calculation in the final letters, hinting to His ability; and He is everything, and therefore He is called "One" because of all this. **"And before one, what do you count?"** This follows the secret of the **Fifty Gates of Understanding** <note>The "N' Sha'arei Binah," a classic Kabbalistic concept representing the levels of insight into the divine order</note>.

And Rabbeinu Meir HaLevi <note>Rabbi Meir ben Todros HaLevi Abulafia (c. 1170–1244), a prominent Spanish rabbi</note> wrote: *"The lamp of the Lord is the soul of man"* <note>Proverbs 20:27</note>. And regarding the Wisdom we have mentioned, it is appropriate to say according to this explanation: His word is upon us and shall not be lost. He said this regarding the "World to Come," because it is the promise of reward. The Holy Torah in the Year of Jubilee <note>Yovel — the 50th year when slaves were freed and land returned</note> is "Freedom," and not because of a measure or number that is included in the weeks, but rather as returning "to his ancestral holding." If so, what thing is full of Him? He swore with a complete oath, with witnesses as we have established, to the Levites... regarding his ancestral holding. This is the secret of **World, Soul, and Year** <term>Olam, Nefesh, Shanah — the three dimensions of reality in Sefer Yetzirah</term>. Truly, the words of the Torah regarding the "World to Come" do not refer to a matter of commerce, but to a matter of qualitative contemplation. Therefore, our Sages of blessed memory said: *"All Israel have a portion in the World to Come."* This is all according to the Master of Kabbalah.

And Rabbeinu Hai Gaon <note>The last of the great Babylonian Geonim (939–1038)</note>, of blessed memory, wrote in the *Book of Belief*: "And he likewise wrote... the author of Sefer Yetzirah regarding the matter of 'His beginning is in His end and His end is in His beginning, like a flame bound to a coal.'" There is a difference between "One" <term>Echad</term>, "Unique" <term>Yachid</term>, and "Unified" <term>Miyuchad</term> <note>These three terms denote levels of divine simplicity and singularity in medieval philosophy</note>. The term "Unified" refers to the action of the Agent acting through His power... while "Unique" refers to the Essence... and "One" refers to the source. If you cling to the Indwelling <note>Shekhinah</note>... this is the end which imprints itself back into its source...

# The Ra’avad, of blessed memory — Chapter 1, Mishnah 7 — The Ramban

**Ten Sefirot: their measure is ten which have no end:**
The explanation is that there is no end to their flow of influence <note>original: "hashpa'atan." In Kabbalistic thought, this refers to the divine energy flowing from the infinite source into the created world.</note> and to their depth, for who could compel them? They will never cease.
**Their end is in their beginning.** This means that when you turn the wheel and return to the place from which you departed—as mentioned regarding "the rod" <note>likely a reference to the central axis or staff of the Sefirotic structure</note> which in its circuit is the axis—they are in the hand [of God]. In the place where they went out from and returned to, they are called "their end in their beginning."
And "the end in their beginning" is like the matter of "their end in their beginning," for when you return to the matter of their end, their beginning is like their end. That is to say, when the *Kingship* <note>term: <term>Malchut</term> (Kingship/Kingdom). The final Sefirah, which acts as the interface between the divine and our physical world.</note> rotates and extends until it reaches its limit, and when the wheel reaches its opening, it circles back. Thus, their end will be like the beginning of what follows it, and they will start from another source.
"The end is as the beginning, and the beginning as the end." All of this comes to hint that the Name, may He be exalted, will never be limited, and there is no conclusion or start to Him. That which has no end has no "head" (beginning). Heaven forbid! Rather, He is established and eternal, from this world to the world to come.
And the Master of Kabbalah wrote, of blessed memory: "the matter of the end in the beginning."

<column-break/>

**And the end is like the matter of their end in their beginning:** Its explanation is that when an end is carved out, you will return again when you desire an end. It is said that the end went and circled in the cycle of the "Wheel of Thought" <note>term: <term>Galgal ha-Machshavah</term>. The primordial realm of divine intention where creation first exists in potential.</note> toward the future and the secret. From their thought, one may know the secret. **Ten Sefirot of nothingness: their end is fixed in their beginning**—at the start of thoughts—**like a flame bound to the coal**; they are suspended and their connection is **for the Master is Unique and has no second.**
Everything is minimal **and before One, what do you count?**
All the Wisdoms were established from of old, and the workings of the matter of Wisdom and the beginning of the Sefirot are from bottom to top, which is according to their end—the "End of Days"—from top to bottom.
The secret of the matter is "like a flame," like a piece of coal that produces a flame; for can there be a flame without a coal? The Lord lives to be released from the life-force of Wisdom, and so He lives to be released from the life-force of Understanding <note>original: "Binah." The third Sefirah, representing structural logic and processing.</note>. The "voice" of the Sefirot, which is the matter of the "beginning like a flame bound to a coal," is the construction of heat and for the sake of the sign.
And behold, he showed us in this parable that it is almost an assumption that the effect [is inseparable] from the cause, just as one who thinks the flame can exist without the coal is mistaken.
And he returned etc. also that the Sefirah is compelled to belong, just as the life-force of the coal is necessary for the flame. This is the secret of the sapphire <note>original: "sapir." The word Sefirah is etymologically linked to the sapphire's brilliance.</note> whose sparks are its cause.
Silenced <note>original: "Blum." A reference to "Belimah" (nothingness/restraint), suggesting the mind must stop at this mystery.</note>.

->Interpretation of the Ramban, of blessed memory<-

Regarding the explanation: Even though the ancients divided Wisdom, Understanding, and Knowledge—and Knowledge <note>original: "Da'at." The quasi-Sefirah that mediates between Wisdom and Understanding.</note> is not a Sefirah in its own right—the verse is "bound to their beginning." The body is connected, and the center is included from the eight, and the end of the matter is the "flame and coal." A spark cannot exist without the sapphire; "sparks of fire, a most vehement flame." <note>A reference to Song of Songs 8:6.</note>
That is to say, everything is unified in the One—not as one who unifies different things, but they are all equal in their essence, for each of the "Ones" is a "Unique" entity, etc.
The language is like the matter of "forgetting," or it is a hint to the Infinite <note>original: "Ein Sof." The Boundless Divine before emanation.</note>. "Master" refers to the Unique One, and because He is the end of all and everything begins when His desire arises, the language used is "Unique and has no second," even though in His radiance He has no second, for everything ends in Him.
"And before One, what do you count?" There is a difference between "Unique" <note>original: "Yachid."</note> and "One" <note>original: "Echad."</note>. When He unifies Himself for an action through a single power, He is called "Unique." And when He divides to perform His work, every part of Him is called "Individual" <note>also "Yachid."</note>. But when He is in His completeness as the "Head," He is called "One."
"What do you count?" Since the counting used in the language of the perfect Torah is not a [mere] number, for they would ascend from the number "one" because it contains division.

And behold, there are ten types of movements, each distinct from one another, yet all originate from a single power that builds, as in the matter [of creation]. Therefore, it says "as in the matter," for the end of the movements and their conclusion is set within their beginning. It is from their doubling that a unique movement is necessitated for each of them. However, when He dwells in His unity, wherein there is no end <note>original: "sof." In this context, it implies a limit or a change in state.</note>, there is no change at all. This is like a flame attached to a burning coal: though it contains many colors and occupies a certain space, it exists there like a spirit, moving the flame toward one of the edges. The primary source from which all existence cascades.</note>, of whom it is inappropriate to apply a number as one would count "before one," for the One who is All is the foundation for every number. What can a "one" count? This means you have no power to include Him in any number, however it may be; He returns all praises to Himself.

### The Ra’avad, of blessed memory ### Mishnah 8 ### The Ramban, of blessed memory — Chapter 1

Restrain your mouth from speaking, just as the soul must [restrain itself] regarding the end of the making of these [emanations]. In its beginning, which is the "Thought" <note>original: "Machshavah." In Kabbalah, this refers to the primordial divine plan or the Sefirah of Wisdom (Chokhmah).</note>, etc., as explained in the previous Mishnah. And if you say: "How shall we picture it in our thought?" Bridle your mouth from investigating such things. Is it not simple to Him, like a light from which heat and measure emanate? He is the Cause of Causes, therefore the matter is: "bridle your mouth." This means that when you look at all the details of existence in the soul, at the place of speech, it is closed. For up to this point, permission was written to speak of the "Thought." It seems to me that permission to speak is given only to provide a metaphor, like a coverlet from the [divine] tapestry, for they are "unto you and beneath you" <note>likely referring to the limits of human perception—knowing what is below/near rather than what is above/Infinite.</note>. Restrain and seal your mouth. You are obligated [to do so].

<column-break/>

**Ten Sefirot of nothingness: bridle your mouth from speaking and your heart from meditating, and if your heart runs:**
The explanation of "if your heart runs" toward a thought: when you experience a "breaking" [of focus], remove it from your heart and "return to the Place." This means returning to the unity of the Place <note>term: <term>HaMakom</term>. A traditional Hebrew name for God, implying that He is the "Place" of the world, but the world is not His place.</note> and the awe of Him. In every place where it says **Ten Sefirot of nothingness**, as we have explained, [it means] "from speaking and your heart from meditating." And if your heart runs, return to the "Place," for concerning this it was said "running and returning" <note>original: "Ratzo V'shov." A reference to the vision of the Chariot in Ezekiel 1:14, describing the movement of the angels; here applied to the oscillating motion of the soul in mystical contemplation.</note> and the "everlasting arms" <note>original: "zero'ot olam," from Deuteronomy 33:27.</note>. **A covenant was carved:**
[Through] returning and awe. And if [the heart] leaps in its interruption, as we find regarding the "Holy Hayyot" <note>original: "Kodesh." Likely referring to the Hayyot HaKodesh, the celestial beings carrying the Divine Throne.</note>. When they lack the strength to keep their statures upright, they immediately bend. This is because of the Divine Presence <note>term: <term>Shekhinah</term>. The immanent, feminine aspect of the Divine that dwells within the world.</note>. And this is what is meant by "entering the Chariot" and the blindness of "running and returning." And "returning" <note>original: "v'shov"</note> is an expression of "many," meaning the will to keep their stature upright in order to see the "branch of the Chariot" and then return.

---

### Commentary of the Ramban, of blessed memory

"Bridle" <note>original: "Belom"</note> is like the matter of "nothingness" <note>original: "belimah," from Job 26:7.</note> and as the Sages said: "We do not expound [on the Chariot]." The ultimate reason for the lips [to be silent] is so one can contemplate. Do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin, because it is said: "It is the glory of God to conceal a matter" <note>Proverbs 25:2</note>. And as they said: "Anyone who does not have concern for the honor of their Maker [it were better he had not come into the world]." "And your heart from meditating"—meaning one should not imagine that which is beyond the permitted limits. "And if your heart runs" to imagine—"return to the Place," to the subject of the "Seat" <note>original: "moshav," the Throne of Glory</note> which your heart is permitted to reflect upon. Concerning this matter, a covenant was carved. Therefore, the matter was revealed so that there would be a way to understand it, speak of it, and reflect upon it. And if [one asks] about the "number" of it: because from the power of the thing called "Covenant," which is the unification of praises into one power, one can recognize that in "Understanding" <note>term: <term>Binah</term>. The Sefirah of logical analysis and processed thought.</note> there are nothing but complete utterances.

And we shall begin to settle Him within the unique power that is in Him.

substance, He will refine and cast down to all existence; He is a power

And He was not alone; He did not change from the order
of the numbers, for He precedes all numbers
by nature. And therefore it said, "He was not," for every

it is not appropriate to attribute to the **Cause of Causes** <term>Illat HaIllot</term> either number
or measure. And who can understand the matter of "their end
is in their beginning" <note>A core phrase from Sefer Yetzirah 1:7, suggesting that the ultimate purpose of creation was present in the very first thought of God.</note>, just as we thought about the voice which is
the Thought <note>The transition from silent thought to audible voice is a metaphor for the process of emanation.</note> to be considered? For from the meditation
the Will was awakened, and He acted in His activity through the power of the "No" <note>Original: "lo," likely referring to the "Ayin" or Nothingness from which creation springs.</note>,
until He brought out the substance like a drop in the shape of the letter **Yod** <note>The Yod is the smallest letter, representing the initial point or "seed" of creation (Wisdom/Chokhmah).</note>,
and in it is the Breath of Life, and from it all the parts and their orders were acted upon.
And if you wish to contemplate all His actions,
it was in the power of His wisdom, for it was like the matter of all the details
and their creations within the totality of the Thought that preceded
the action. So too, you are obligated to understand all
the renewals in the activity of the Thought; and just as
the Thought is impossible to be a separate thing from Him,
so it is impossible to see anything above everything
other than the Simple, Supreme Thought.
And from here you must understand how the One acts
all the activities through His power without any change,
for from Him all actors take [their power], and He is the Wisdom
for all the works, and He has no second to Him in terms of the activity.
For regarding the "Cause" mentioned above, no works can be attributed to Him
as being affected by them, just as the Thought has no wisdom
that comes from outside of it. And from here you
must understand how the Unique One has no
limits to His wisdom and knowledge. And "Before one,
what do you count?" <note>A rhetorical question from Sefer Yetzirah 1:7, emphasizing that God precedes the very concept of number.</note> And who can understand the matter of "their end

<meta>This page continues the exploration of the Divine emanations, specifically moving from the concept of the Infinite Creator to the first of the ten Sefirot: the Breath of the Living God. It transitions from the hidden unity discussed on the previous page to the emergence of "Voice, Breath, and Speech" as the foundational tools of creation.</meta>

# The Ramban, of blessed memory # Chapter 1, Mishnah 9 # The Ra'avad, of blessed memory

**One is the breath of the living God** • **Explanation**
An ancient arrangement for the structures of the Sefirot: "Breath of the living God" <note>Hebrew: *Ruach Elohim Chayim*. In the Sefer Yetzirah, this is the first emanation, representing the primordial atmosphere or spirit from which all else is formed.</note>—this refers to the necessity itself coming from Him and His strength. The spirits—blessed and praised be His name, for His name is Himself.
He called His name "Able," the ten Sefirot and the end of Himself in the blessing: "Breath of the living God."
The secret of the hidden thing: the voice of the name of the "Life of the Worlds," the Unique One. Voice, Breath, and Speech—and this is the **Holy Spirit** <term>Ruach HaKodesh</term> and the Word. Corresponding to the "Breath of the living God." A ladder in the yoke <note>Likely a reference to a balanced scale or structure.</note> corresponding to the balance, and this is the Holy Spirit, meaning the "finest part" <note>Hebrew: *solet*, literally "fine flour," used here to mean the essence or highest quality.</note> of the Sefirah is the Holiness from among the other Sefirot. It is called the Holy Spirit because of its loftiness, for there is no loftiness like His.
The degree of the Holy Spirit is at the level of conquering three stages: and this is the secret of **Voice**, **Breath**, and **Speech**.
The Great Rabbi Aaron, of blessed memory, wrote: "Voice" corresponds to "The voice of the living God." "Breath" corresponds to "By the breath of His mouth all their host." "Speech" <note>original: "דבור" (Dibbur)</note> corresponds to "By the word of the Lord the heavens were made." <note>Citing Psalm 33:6.</note> And no Voice is found without Breath and Speech. This is the end of his words.
Closed.

<column-break/>

"The Assembly of the Kingdom" <term>Knesset HaMalchut</term> etc. to explain to you the laws of every single Sefirah, for He teaches the wisdom of the revealed, because from the revealed you will understand the hidden according to our order—the likeness of all things. Do not learn from the Sefirot alone.
Ten Sefirot of nothingness (*Belimah*): one is the incense of the tongue to speak.
"Breath of the living God, blessed and praised"—is it not even like the body of the name of the "Life of the Worlds"? Voice, his ladder, and the heat of the incense, Breath and Speech—and this is the Holy Spirit. Every language is thus built from spiritual vessels.
A name for the "seal" <note>The creative "sealing" of the directions of space mentioned later in the text.</note> which would be lacking without its seal.
A parable for this is the mirror: regarding the power that reaches man, it is "Breath" <term>Ruach</term>. This Name's primary preparation is for the Breath which is drawn forth as power from the goodness of the Spirit; his spirit shall be improved and its likeness. It is worthy to be the returning laws of those moved by the Spirit that He intended for it.
The proof for this is that if these were at rest after movement until the Breath that moves them was taken away, and if afterwards one were to choose all sorts of "apples" <note>original: "תפוחים" (*tappuchim*). In medieval medical-philosophical Hebrew, this often refers to the lungs or the air-sacs that expand and contract.</note> and it was filled as a handful from the foundational breath that remains from the residue, he would not live and would not move. "Living" is stated first to say that his soul is moved so that he may move.

---

## Commentary of the Ramban, of blessed memory

Regarding the Ancient One <term>Atik</term>, to bless Him as a supreme quality in His "blowing," in His strength, and in His hiddenness. The Ancient One is a literal detail. "One is the Breath"—he did not mention the height of the level until the point of birthing the colors, the beginning of the "Yod-Tav" <note>Likely a reference to the alphabetic creative process.</note> to create from it a voice in the total unity. Breath came through her staff, speaking to speech until a moving voice becomes the number five. "Breath" <term>Ruach</term> is **Wisdom** <term>Chokhmah</term>, the "Beginning," the "Breath of God," and it is the receiving of life, as it is written: "Wisdom gives life to those who possess it." <note>Ecclesiastes 7:12.</note> And since everything comes from Wisdom, as it is written: "You made them all with Wisdom," he mentions here and says: "Blessed and praised be the name of the Life of the Worlds."
"Blessed" <term>Barukh</term> comes from the power of Breath, and "Praised" <term>Mevorakh</term> from the power of five <note>Possibly referring to the five phonetic families of letters.</note>, and this is because they are the nature of blessing and existence. He is called "Life of the Worlds" <term>Chai HaOlamim</term> because He is the "Who" (*Mi*) and has the power to enliven the worlds. Through the supernal things which are from the power of the world, they created Him as "Worlds."
Voice, Breath, and Speech: He said that the first Sefirah that rests as Breath, since its law is Breath, contains three voices: the sound which is called "Voice" <term>Kol</term>; that which moves it, expanding and going forth, which is called "Breath" <term>Ruach</term>; and that which is divided into letters, which is called "Speech" <term>Dibbur</term>. And even the completion of Speech is Breath, as he explains, and this is the **Holy Spirit**.
"The Holy" <term>HaKodesh</term> is the power of the Spirit prepared to receive from the "End of Ends," and from it, the Spirit which is holy is called the "Holy Spirit." Its meaning is: the Holy Letters and the Holy Tongue.

# The Ra'avad, of blessed memory # Chapter 1, Mishnah 5 # The Ramban, of blessed memory

Also, to remove and to withdraw the channels of meditation from Knowledge <term>Da'at: the third mental Sefirah, representing the integration of wisdom and understanding</term> toward thought—all the constrictions of contemplation. And for this, he warns: If one judges thus, to liken the Hidden to Knowledge, it is better for the Place <note>Hebrew: *Maqom*, a common rabbinic euphemism for God.</note>. Explanation: Enter into your understanding, and from what is lacking, descend to the place which is Knowledge, for there His dwelling is pleasing—for the mouth to speak and for the heart to meditate. For your strength is like clay. According to the measure of the past and the standing of its spirit, it must agree to rise from Understanding to Knowledge. And regarding this matter, a covenant was made. For when we engrave for ourselves the throne of light that flows from the Throne <note>The Throne of Glory (*Kisse HaKavod*).</note>, the foundation of the world among all the upper beings, it is in order to gaze upon them and upon it as a world of Knowledge. For the focus should not sour <note>Hebrew: *yitchametz*, meaning to spoil or go astray.</note> toward the Source concerning that which the Knowledge does not have the power to attain. Let him not cause his intellect to go beyond what is written. Except for the specific boundaries of what was in his power to ascend, for if he tests it, he will stumble and will not prevail. 

**The parable of this:** If the intellect had the power to carry **two loaves** and no more, let him not be over-ambitious. If he seeks to add half a loaf to his burden, he will stumble and will not be able to carry even the two loaves that he originally had the strength to carry.

->Stand<-

<column-break/>

This returns to the material <note>Hebrew: *Chomer*, which also punningly refers to a donkey (*Chamor*), symbolizing the physical body or raw matter.</note>, and this is what the Sages, of blessed memory, meant: for the dream will not expand, and of the addition of the Kingdom of the Ministry we do not know. If this is so, it is a *Kal V'Chomer* <term>a logical "how much more so" argument</term> regarding the dream, which is prepared within houses of clay whose foundation is in the dust, which is not his source in the secret of my praise. For "the hidden things belong to the Lord our God, but the revealed things are for us and our children" <note>Deuteronomy 29:28.</note>. And this is the secret of the vision of the **child** <note>A reference to a story in the Talmud (Chagigah 13a) where a young student investigating the mysteries of Ezekiel’s vision was consumed by Divine fire.</note> who was investigating the glory of the *Chashmal* <term>the celestial "electrum" or gleaming fire seen in Ezekiel's vision</term> and was consumed and swept away. And "Good, much good, and the best of good" <note>An emphasis on the goodness of staying within bounds.</note> he wrote, and these are his words: **"Silence your mouth from speaking."** This means: limit your mouth from speaking after these boundaries. Rather, imagine within yourself to maintain the manner of concentration by way of separation—it shall not be separated and it shall not be attached, for He is One and there is no end to the investigation similar to Him. Therefore, it is inscribed: "Blessed be the glory from His place." The word "Blessed" (*Baruch*) is an adjective and a praise... for He does not receive any desire from another. And if you are judged thus, to meditate, and your mouth to speak, and you cannot restrain your spirit, it is "Good for the Place" <note>Meaning it is better to return your focus to God's sovereignty.</note>, for thus it was sealed regarding the **Living Creatures** <term>Chayot: the high-ranking angels supporting the Divine Throne</term>: **"Running and returning."** For the Living Creatures, who are in the inner sanctum of the Glory, run to see the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah</term> and return immediately. And regarding this matter, a covenant was made that you shall not meditate [beyond the limit]. And the Rabbi, my teacher, of blessed memory, explained "Silence your mouth from speaking": He spoke of "speech" regarding the mouth and "meditation" regarding the heart. And if you are judged thus, meaning to meditate—

---

It is better to return to the Place; rather, speak with your mouth that which you have meditated in your heart, for even though you were "stricken" by the meditation <note>Meaning even if you were overwhelmed by the mystical thought.</note>, there is still hope that the speech will return to its place. And so it is said of the Living Creatures, that they have a will to see the Divine Presence, but they return and recognize that they do not act by their own will, and they return immediately. Regarding this, a covenant was made that you shall not meditate [forbidden thoughts], and if you have meditated, do not speak, do not speak in the covenant of the oath, until [the end].
