### Commentary of the Ramban, of blessed memory
"He formed reality from Chaos (*Tohu*) as a literal substance" — using the seal, He formed actual existences from it. "And He made His non-existence into His existence" — and He hewed the columns of the *Sefirot* above. How? In the beginning, that which was "non-existence" in its entirety is actually within Him, a branch of Him that is now "existence." And these are: the columns that support the upper realms, for everything stands and is supported by them. They are called "great columns" because they come from the power of Greatness (*Gedulah*), from the "air" which is the inner essence of Voice and Spirit, which cannot be grasped. Within man, there is "air" that is emptied from it, like a second interior, and these are within it, so that one cannot bring "spirit" into it, as it is written: "And Moses was able..." <note>A reference to Exodus 40:35, where Moses could not enter the Tent of Meeting because of the Divine Cloud</note>.

"He gazes" — from the beginning to the end. This means: it is fitting for this to be so, and who is fitting for which end? "And He speaks" — this refers to that which shall be at the head becoming the end, and that which shall be at the head remaining at the head, in order to equalize the "Blood and the Basin" <note>original: "דם וספל" - likely a reference to the covenant at Sinai; here it symbolizes the balancing of spiritual forces</note> and their surroundings. 

"Making all of creation" — and in this way, he was careful twenty times over regarding the compounded elements. "And all words are one Name" — for there is nothing that does not come from the "Necessary" but rather from the "Compounded," and there is no power in the Compounded that does not come from the Compounded <note>A philosophical argument about the chain of causality in creation</note>. Everything is one root.

"And one Name" — one soul. This is not to say it was not "one Name" at the time of the initial creation; he mentions that it was "one soul." And when he mentions the "Compounded," he mentions "one Name," specifying the name of the "Bride" <note>The *Shekhinah* or Divine Presence</note> in which the Name resides, and she comes from afar.

"A sign for the matter: twenty..." — the "matter" (*Davar*) refers to the fact that the "Word" (*Kalimah*) is the foundation of the many, and things do not come into being from the void. "Twenty-two" — he explains: seventy children, and feet, and hooks <note>A metaphorical description of the alphabet's structure, possibly referencing the Tabernacle's construction</note>, and the "balancing air," which are "one body." He uses a break in the language to simplify, in order to include the "Natural" and the "Sensed" in the word "He leaped" (*Kafatz*) — he rushed, equal to the Name. Therefore, when one is missing, they are all missing.

->The Chapter is Concluded<-

<meta>This page continues the technical and mystical analysis of the Sefer Yetzirah (The Book of Creation). ### The Rambaz, of Blessed Memory: Chapter 2, Mishnah 4

Ten is 17, and nineteen is 18, and in nineteen it is 19, and in twenty it is 20. This is written to explain the measurement surrounding the streets <note>Likely referring to the layout of the Temple courtyards or the "streets" of the heavenly Jerusalem</note> specifically in the "Slaughterhouse" <note>Hebrew: *Mitbach*; the area in the Temple where sacrifices were prepared</note>, because all the permutations are doubled there, and windows are there, in the language of the "Mechanism" <note>Hebrew: *Mekonon*; referring to the *Mekonot*, the bronze wheeled stands in Solomon's Temple described in 1 Kings 7</note>. One who understands the mechanisms of the Temple will understand this explanation.

The principles of music <note>Hebrew: *Musika*; medieval Kabbalists often linked the proportions of the Temple and the Altar to musical intervals and harmony</note> will awaken the secret of this Altar, for the Divine Presence (*Shekhinah*) does not rest except through a matter of joy, as it is said: "But now bring me a musician..." <note>A quote from 2 Kings 3:15. The prophet Elisha required music to achieve a state of prophetic inspiration</note> and so on. We received this explanation from the mouth of our Master, the Father, of blessed memory, the son of Nahshon Yaakov, the pious and ascetic. One who has not delved into the science of music will not understand this.

Regarding what is written in the *Book of Formation* (*Sefer Yetzirah*): **"He carved them"**—this means in every single "gate" <note>A "gate" in this system is a two-letter combination</note>, and from every gate He investigated two letters. This is the "Sorting" (*Miyun*). And in the resting position, one letter transitions with all of them, and so on, with all the letters. All other letters pair with Aleph (א), Bet (ב) pairs with all of them, and Lamed (ל) with all the letters, and all other letters with Bet. This is how He divided them, "carved them," and the "Sorting" to join individual connections.

**"He carved them"** corresponds to the five: Spirit, Life, and Life <note>Representing the upper dimensions of the soul and breath</note>. 
**"The Sorting"** corresponds to the six: "Spirit from Spirit." 
**"He carved and He hewed"** and so on. At first, He took a "Book" and mentioned: **"He carved them, He hewed them."** **"He carved them"** and the **"Sorting"** are imprinted—imprinted to hint at Abraham, "the Father of a Multitude" <note>A play on Abraham’s name and his role as the legendary author of *Sefer Yetzirah*</note>, the head of our Sages of blessed memory. 

He investigated these five: *Ner, Betas, Kafag, Kel* <note>These are likely mystical letter permutations or mnemonics used for meditative purposes</note> which are remembered, and the soul of everything destined to be created. This is the secret of my vineyard, as in the verse "they trembled from the multitude of their worries." 

And this is the secret of the "Inclusion," as in the verse: "Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is One" <note>The *Shema*, the central declaration of Jewish faith</note>. Turn to the Most High, and this is the Crown (*Keter*) of the fifty gates of Understanding (*Binah*). The voice of the "Lamed" <note>The letter Lamed (ל) is the tallest letter, often associated with the heart or reaching upward</note> is as it is written: "The voice of the Lord is in power," for His voice is Kindness (*Chesed*), following the example of "Kindness to the counter" <note>Hebrew: *Mevaser*; perhaps a reference to the herald of good news</note>, and there is no number before Him. He is the foundation of the number; everything is within His investigation, and the Name shall never move from its place. All are in the "Slaughterhouse" and are contained within Him. 

From Him they gaze, and up to nine they are called to "dream in the Orchard" <note>The "Orchard" or *Pardes* is a term for the four levels of Torah interpretation, specifically the mystical realm</note> until they reach the "Merged Ones" and the "Thinker," and "He passes by them," and so on. All of them have one name, and that is **Ten**, because it also presses into **One** by its power. The number is divided into the doubling of tens; when you say "twenty," it is the doubling of two tens. So too until ninety, which are nine tens in the place of the nine individuals in the Orchard. Together with "ten," which is in the place of the "One," they are "five and ten" <note>Numerical value 15, the name of God *Yah* (יה)</note>. 

All of them have one name: Kindness (*Chesed*) and "Material." And "Words" correspond to nine individuals, and with the "Vision," they are "One Thousand Material." So too, nine myriads <note>A myriad is 10,000</note> are in the place of the nine individuals, and with one myriad, they are in one place with ten myriads. And by their power, in the thousand "hidden dreams," and ten myriads in one "baldness" <note>Likely a technical term for a blank or unified space in the celestial spheres</note>. Therefore, David had one "chariot."

Therefore, he attributes Wisdom (*Chokhmah*) to the upper region for the six directions, minus nine myriads and myriads for each side. And there he acquired ten thousand words, because until here is the completion of "Offspring." The Divine Presence did not dwell in Israel until they left Egypt, for there were "sixty myriads of feet" <note>600,000 men; the traditional number of the Israelites in the Exodus</note>. Previously, the Presence did not dwell because there were not "four myriads" <note>40,000</note>. And it is explained in Tractate Ketubot: as her marriage contract is written, so is the virginity of a maidservant; her contract is sixty myriads, and likewise her virginity is sixty myriads. 

In the section of *Kereitot* and in the portions of *Vayishlach* and *Vayishlach* and *Vayikra* <note>Sections of the Torah</note>, regarding the place called *Mahanaim* ("Two Camps"): this teaches that if Israel were missing even one person from the sixty myriads, they would not have been worthy to receive the Torah. This is a great secret in Kabbalah. Therefore, our Sages of blessed memory said: the "Inclusion" is less than sixty myriads. If so, all the "Faces" (*Partzufim*) are included in sixty myriads of thousands of branches. This is the secret of the Torah which says: "Not with you alone do I make this covenant... but with him who is standing here with us today before the Lord our God, and also with him who is not here with us today." <note>Deuteronomy 29:13-14</note>

### The Rambaz, of Blessed Memory: Chapter 2, Mishnah 8

...our iniquities: and "make our heart established" <note>Hebrew: *Yashan*, which usually means "old" or "sleeping," but interpreted here as "established" or "integrated" through divine work</note>: meaning to say a matter that was previously occupied with existence. And the exchange <note>Hebrew: *Chilaf*; possibly referring to the permutation or transformation of divine energies</note> of the great pillars returns from our life like a soul—meaning to say that no man can grasp the Levite <note>original: *ha-Levi*. This likely refers to a specific spiritual degree or perhaps the Leviathan in its mystical sense</note>. Thus far are the words of the Kabbalistic Master, **Rabbi Joseph Gikatilla** <note>original: *Kastaniel*. A major 13th-century Spanish Kabbalist known for his work *Sha'arei Orah*</note>.

And the Rabbi, our teacher **Meir of Rothenburg** <note>The Maharam (c. 1215–1293), a leading German scholar and mystic</note>, explained in the book of Kabbalah called *The Crown of the Name of Life* <note>original: *Keter Shem Chayim*</note>, as follows: The *Book of Formation* (*Sefer Yetzirah*) wrote that in its measure, every foundation and every speech goes forth in one Name, meaning the Holy Spirit—a spirit from the Spirit—which is the Name of Wisdom alone. He formed existence (*Yesh*) from chaos (*Tohu*)—actual chaos and void—and He made and returned that which was "old" <note>or "sleeping"</note> to the state of "Making" <term>Asiyah; the final stage of creation in Kabbalah, representing the physical world</term>. He dug its foundation just as one levels paths. "In the doors I descended, even I made it"—this shows that He preceded "Formation" (*Yetzirah*) over "Making" (*Asiyah*).

Meaning to say: at first, He moved its places from one side to the other, like finding the grace of a dream. And He searched them and moved them and stood them upon the nature of the Foundation. And this "search" I have made—its spheres (*Sefirot*) are in the manner of "Rectification" <term>Tikkun; the process of repairing and perfecting the world</term>, for their existence is not separate. Similarly, because they do not know how to do evil, they do not bring a sacrifice for their sins <note>Referring to the angelic or purely spiritual realms that lack a "yetzer hara" or evil inclination</note>. This is the meaning of "and he made the soul"—this is the wisdom they write for the Temple, for they do not look like a child, and they are like one who is foolish... they do not know how to rectify evil. And similarly, "he did not do his feet" <note>A reference to 2 Samuel 19:25 regarding Mephibosheth, used here to show that "doing" implies grooming or fixing</note> and likewise "to do the Sabbath day." If so, the language of "Making" (*Ma'aseh*) refers to the **rectification of a thing** until it is more perfect than it could otherwise be.

And the exchange of the great pillars returns from our life like a soul. He called the exchange "returning" and called it "like a soul" because it is simpler than all simple things, and a simple thing cannot be grasped. All this is to hint that He is not a body, nor a power within a body. The great pillars and the wise men of the number "return" <note>Hebrew: *Chozer*, possibly a wordplay on "Chazir," the pig, but here used in the context of returning or cycles</note> because all that is received is influenced by His capabilities. And their stature is to speak of all "Desires" and the "Body of Matter."

---

The intention of the author of the *Book of Formation* (*Sefer Yetzirah*) was to create a **sign** for the matter so that it would not be forgotten due to its great depth. A "sign" for a matter is found many times in the wisdom of the Talmud, like this:

He called the **22 letters** "Desires" <note>Hebrew: *Chafetzim*, often translated as "objects," but here implying the divine will embedded in the Hebrew alphabet</note>, as he said in the first chapter: "and a spirit is in each one of them." And the "Body of Matter" of the world stands upon one order, for all the letters in the world stand as general principles in the manner of twenty-two facets, in a measure so that the arrangement—the one arranged by the Unique One—shall not be forgotten. And all of this points to the **perfection of the Arranger**.

---

The chapter is concluded. We have already explained its investigation and its order with His help. This is the aspect of the "Face of Power" in our wisdom.

### The Ra'avad, of Blessed Memory: Chapter 1, Mishnah 10 — The Rambaz, of Blessed Memory

The "Great Ones" and the foundation of the year are called the "Five Pillars." There are seven, and they are those mentioned in the verse: *"Yours, O Lord, is the greatness..."* <note>1 Chronicles 29:11</note>. He called them "Great" so that their primary state would be one of greatness. We have seen much in our grasp explaining the "Attributes of the Lions" <note>original: *Midot ha-Arayot*; a reference to the faces of the Divine Chariot, here linked to the Sefirah of Understanding</note> and "Life" <note>Wisdom</note>. There are in that Name 120 pillars of light, and every single pillar is a pillar and foundation for the world, as it is said: *"The righteous is an everlasting foundation"* <note>Proverbs 10:25</note>. And it is also taught that there are 22 letters; each one of them breathes and gazes into the Supernal Wisdom, which exist and constantly transform their states. There are 22 letters leading up to 231 "Gates" <note>The number of possible two-letter combinations in the Hebrew alphabet</note> for every single species. Through this, He acts at the beginning through the Name, because all the supernal actions were performed in the "Seven Ends" <note>The seven lower Sefirot or directions of space</note> from Greatness <note>Chesed</note> downwards. And the Crown <note>Keter</note>, which is the Name of the Lord, meaning the entirety of Beauty <note>Tiferet</note>, and it was one Name performing every deed and arrangement through these letters. 

And the intent of the matter, may the Name be blessed, is that the Name has 22 "Faces." And there are ten fingers of the hands and ten toes of the feet—behold, there is a "Hand" and a "Foot" in this sense—making 22 within one body <note>Likely counting the ten fingers, ten toes, and the two limbs/units themselves</note>. But the hands are divided, one to the right and one to the left, and so too the feet, one to the right and one to the left. Nevertheless, they all emerge from one body. So it is in the World, so it is in the Chariot, and so it is in the Holy One, blessed be He: all His powers are unified from His simple unity, blessed be He. And there are 22 "Faces" in one body; they are the 22 letters which were woven into one sphere, which is the "Living" <note>Chay; perhaps referring to the Chayah or Living Creature of the Chariot</note>. End of Chapter 2.

<column-break/>

Pillars building pillars... as described in the *Book of Creation* (*Sefer Yetzirah*) in various chapters. And this is the sign of the "Scribe and Transformer." The **Razah** <note>Rabbi Zechariah</note> says this means "One who counts." And he who counts is one who weighs, as it is written: *"Is there a man who counts..."* <note>Likely a paraphrase of Job or Isaiah regarding divine accounting</note>. This corresponds to what was said above regarding the essence of their weight and their exchange. Therefore, he said "Scribe and Transformer"—He makes the mentioned matter. Therefore, "making" is used in its simple sense, as it is said: *"God said: He made you and established you"* <note>Deuteronomy 32:6</note>. And the sages said: *"I made the earth... over all the hosts which I made."* 

And thus, every speech goes forth in His name, like a decree from the mouth of the King. And he says there: "No mouth shall speak," etc. *"Then You spoke in a vision"* <note>Psalm 89:20</note>. *"The spirit of the Lord spoke through me"* <note>2 Samuel 23:2</note>. And this speech is in one Name; for all speech is difficult to divide, because the **Aleph** [א] is the root and foundation of all the letters. And the Aleph itself is seen in the upper world, for the letter Aleph itself is shaped thus: its head is in the shape of a *Yod* [י], its middle line is in the shape of a *Vav* [ו], and its leg is in the shape of a *Yod* [י]. Behold, in this combined arrangement, it equals the Name **Y-H-V-H** <note>In Gematria: Yod (10) + Vav (6) + Yod (10) = 26, the numerical value of the Tetragrammaton</note>. And in this Name is included the secret of the **Explicit Name** <term>Shem HaMephorash; the hidden or fully articulated Name of God</term> which is based on the secret of the calculated combination. For when one combines all the letters together, which are four, it rises in thought to the number 72 <note>This refers to the "Name of 72" derived from the expansion: Y + YH + YHV + YHVH = 72</note>. *Yod* is ten in number, and hidden is the secret of the combination with the 15 <note>the value of Y-H</note>, behold this combination rises to 25. After this, the combination is made from this calculation with the *Vav-He*, rising to the secret of the combination of 72. 

Therefore, the Explicit Name is found in the secret of the *Aleph*, and He is the one who gives wisdom to man to make him wise and understanding. And the sign for the matter is that the thread of life is included in your hand. "22 faces and one body" means that the 22 letters emerge from the faces and the one body, which is the truth of the "Spirit of the Living God." Thus far are the words of the Rabbi, **Rabbi Aaron**, in the book *Pardes*. And the Kabbalist **Rabbi Joseph Ashkenazi** explained in the book called *The Crown of the Torah* (*Keter Torah*), of blessed memory: "It is found that every utterance and every speech is established in one Name." This means that every utterance and every speech goes forth in one Name, through all the combinations he explained. It is nothing but the calculation of the one Name of the Holy One, Blessed be He. Even every other thing alone is the Name; He remembered from its substance reality—meaning a thing that has actual substance, like the calf and all other creatures.

### The Rambaz, of Blessed Memory: Chapter 3, Mishnah 2 — The Ra’avad, of Blessed Memory (Page 69)

"Your iniquities are engraved upon your bones" <note>A reference to Ezekiel 32:27, suggesting that sin leaves a physical or structural mark on the soul's vehicle</note>. 
And behold, a voice—the voice of obligation <gloss>and it was like a cloud</gloss>.
Lacking, mercy and relief have departed from him.
And that "lacking" <note>original: *he-chaser*</note> is related to the sparing <note>original: *chas*</note> of the powers that depend upon it; it rests 
upon him through spiritual excision <term>Karet: "cutting off" the soul from its divine source</term>. And this "sparing" is a lack that strips 
the soul that depends upon it. Thus, the voice of the "Lacking" 
indicates to him a loss of glory. "I will visit upon you" 
as one who thins out the divine flow, like a spreading baldness. And not 
like the "Physician’s illness" where his sicknesses are remembered 
against him; for those who seek the Lord will not gape like those for whom the seven 
heavens live upon them. Yet the "sparing" did not remove the bitterness of death.
The "Tongue of Decree" <note>The *Lashon Chok* is the central balance point in the Sefer Yetzirah’s metaphor of the scales</note> decides the balance, as it is written. Section: Understanding 
and Beauty <note>Binah and Tiferet</note>, like one receiving portions of anger, the pan 
of merit and the pan of guilt. According to the laws of those who move it, 
so there is a pan of merit and a pan of guilt for the princes on high. 
As it is written: *"The Lord will punish the host of the high heaven on high"* <note>Isaiah 24:21</note>, and regarding 
the angels of peace. This is to say 
that he is forgotten by his witnesses and by the power of the meal 
of the kings, etc.

<column-break/>

To return and to lack... bread. You can 
turn the lightness of the tongue to merit and to good, for it 
is the decider. "Sparing" is mentioned in the secret of the three wars 
in difficult questions—Heaven forbid!—to seek through kindness. And "sparing" is to maintain 
the freedom of the plague-mark through salt, until here are his words. And the Rabbi, Rabbi 
Azriel <note>Rabbi Azriel of Gerona, a foundational 13th-century Kabbalist</note>, the holy son of Rabbi Menachem, wrote in the 
"Book of Fillings" <note>Sefer ha-Milu’im</note>, of blessed memory: There are those who use [the Name] 
for merit, and there are those who use [it] for guilt. 
And the "Tongue of Decree" decides, as it is written: "The sun and lightning," 
a single star between the merit 
and the guilt. Let the events upon the tablets not be diminished, 
neither for merit nor for guilt, except because of the division; 
thus the matter comes to a decision. And behold, the 
Rabbi—Heaven forbid—wrote in the book called "Urim and Thummim" 
<note>A reference to the High Priest’s breastplate used for divine divination</note>, 
as follows: In the "Gate of Thirty," God <note>Elohim</note> is called, according to 
the Kabbalists and the Sages of the Talmud, the "Attribute of Justice." 
And this is the intent of the "Perfect Torah" in saying: 
*"Season every grain offering with salt; do not leave the salt of the covenant with your God out of your grain offering; offer salt with all your offerings"* <note>Leviticus 2:13</note>. Salt <note>Melach</note> is found in the secret 
of the combination of *ML* and *M* <note>The word salt, Me-La-Ch, is anagrammatized and linked to Milah (circumcision)</note>. As it is said: *"On the eighth day he shall circumcise [Yimol] 
the flesh of his foreskin"* <note>Leviticus 12:3</note>. Thus five "foreskins" are removed, and 
there is the power of the word *Yimol* [he shall circumcise], which has these letters. And the circumcision hints 
to the attribute of praise, which is called the Attribute of Justice, and it is 
the Sefirah called "Assembly" <note>Knesset Yisrael/Malchut</note>. And the Attribute of Justice is the head; 
for the world would not endure if it were not for the service of 
the Altar, which is the secret of the wondrous transformation of Salt [Melach] 
and Circumcision [Milah] on the eighth day. And there is the foundation of the Attribute of Mercy. 
Behold, here is the pan of merit and the pan of guilt, as it is written: *"On the day 
the Lord God made earth and heaven."* And the "Tongue of Decree" 
decides, as it is written. Until here are the words of the Rabbi, Rabbi Azriel, of blessed memory.

->The Ra’avad, of Blessed Memory — Chapter 3, Mishnah 1 — The Rambaz, of Blessed Memory<-

"Three mothers: their foundation is a scale of merit and a scale of guilt, and the tongue of decree decides between them." As with the seal mentioned above, we spoke of the power <note>original: *koach*</note> to live, but we did not explain the utility of these letters in their proper rectification. Now, in this "Chosen Book" <note>likely referring to a specific commentary or a section of the Sefer Yetzirah</note>, the secret is chosen: to live through the utility of their action.

Their foundation is a scale of merit and a scale of guilt. That which this one lacks, this one draws toward itself, and that one draws toward itself, and the "tongue" <note>The central point of a balance scale</note> decides between them. So it is in the secret of the "Three Living Beings" <term>Chaiyot: the high-ranking angels seen in Ezekiel's vision</term>, for this part is the life-force of the Fire. Fire and Water—the tongue of decree decides between them. So it is in the "Secret of the Sealed Scroll" <note>original: *Sod Sitrei Sefer*</note>, where the portion is the life-force of the Light. If it were not so, the life-force and the water could not cling to one another, for the Fire would decide between them. Thus, the "tongue of decree" decides between them.

So too in a dream: the letter *Shin* represents "sparing" <note>original: *chas*, a wordplay on the sound of the letter</note>, while the water and the Mothers can cling to one another because the Air <note>represented by the letter Aleph</note> decides between them. Thus, the "tongue of decree" decides in the script.

And so did the great Kabbalist Rabbi Aaron explain in the *Book of the Orchard* <note>Sefer HaPardes</note>: The author of the *Book of Creation* <term>Sefer Yetzirah</term> wrote concerning the Living Beings, who are the head of every foundation: "a scale of merit and a scale of guilt, and the tongue of decree decides between them." This means that according to the thoughts of those who intend toward the "tongue of decree," the "lacking tongue" <note>the needle of the scale</note> decides in the writing between the pans of the scale. As an example of this, the foundation is the head to which the Holy One hints...

<column-break/>

And behold, he mentioned in the first chapter "writings, seals, and numbers." In the second chapter, he mentioned the letters and their rotations <note>original: *galgal*, referring to the mystical combinations of the Hebrew alphabet</note>, but he did not wish to mention their values there, because all the preceding chapters speak of Power, Wisdom, and Understanding <term>Keter, Chochmah, and Binah</term>.

Therefore, he began here to speak of their values in the secret of the World, the Year, and the Soul <note>The three dimensions of reality in Yetziratic thought</note. In this chapter, which hints at the "Kindness of the Lord," he began to speak of their relationship to the World, the Year, and the Soul.

He spoke regarding the value of Water in the Upper World: it is the source of life from which life spreads to the seven realms of that world. For "the world is built on kindness" <note>Psalm 89:3</note>, and the foundation of this life is a scale of merit and a scale of guilt, with the tongue of decree deciding between them. This is the secret of the three books that are opened on the New Year <term>Rosh Hashanah</term>: one for the completely righteous <note>the scale of merit</note>, and their seal is for life; one for the wicked <note>the scale of guilt</note>; and one for the intermediates, where the tongue of decree decides between them.

We have received a tradition that the Torah of Wisdom, composed of the holy letters in the order of the commandments, is worthy of the "Seal of Kindness." Who among them truly rules? For they depend upon the small and the great, sent upon the soul in the upper realms. From there, it reaches the soul's portion, established in kindness. Every male who is worthy shall be strengthened to merit through the power of the ruling spirit. Kindness shall pass over him through these commandments... but for those who fail, they are written for the transgression they committed, as it is said: "And your iniquities were [engraved upon your bones]" <note>Jeremiah 17:1 / Ezekiel 32:27</note>.

### Commentary of the Ramban, of Blessed Memory
**Aleph (א):** This refers to the Supreme Crown <term>Keter Elyon</term>. When the counting of the "decree" begins, it rises above the Supreme Crown, for the weight of the *Aleph* is the decree. The "sealing" rises to the beginning, above in Wisdom <term>Chochmah</term>. It is the "tongue" and it is that which decides between the right and the left, and between them. The "Three Living Beings" are weighed for life because they are the foundation for all merit, all guilt, and every decision.

->The Rambaz, of Blessed Memory — Chapter 3, Mishnah 2 — The Ra’avad, of Blessed Memory<-

"...and its consumption is hot and cold; it is the secret of the temperament <term>Mizag: the balancing of the four humors or qualities—hot, cold, wet, dry—in a person</term>, the law of returning all the spirit of life through wisdom."
These are the words of the Rabbi, Rabbi Bahya <note>Likely Rabbi Bahya ben Asher, a 13th-century Spanish commentator known for integrating Kabbalah into his work</note>, of blessed memory. Moshe <note>The author or a later commentator</note> said: Since we have returned to provide the spirit of life for the preservation of its meanings, it has already been clarified for us that the knowledge of the Name *YHV* <note>The three-letter version of the Tetragrammaton: Yod, He, Vav</note> corresponds to the qualities of heat and the sound of water.
From the essence of the matter, and the knowledge of the consequences... as it is written: they change. And therefore, one shall not enter this "Orchard" <term>Pardes: the four levels of Torah interpretation, specifically the mystical/esoteric level</term> without wisdom.
Regarding the philosophers: the wisdom of the philosophers is like a secondary vessel <note>original: *kelim*</note>; it is not fitting to mention the wisdom of philosophy within the wisdom of Kabbalah, just as a flame is to a coal. And today I have seen for the "Children of Zion" <note>Referring to the Jewish community or scholars of the Torah</note> that this wisdom is before us as a sweet portion.

It is hinted at and compared to the people of Zion that they should not investigate the wisdom of philosophy and make the Torah of Moses a forgery <note>original: *palester* - meaning to make the Torah seem false or secondary to logic</note> or a lofty path for their own sake. This is only because our holy Torah is called "The Pure Philosophy." The general philosopher has already investigated in his inquiry this perfection; for them, it is sweet as honey, but to us, it is like a "foreign dog" <note>The text uses a metaphor of dogs to distinguish between secular and holy inquiry</note>.
Therefore, regarding this scholar, he has provided what was written in my heart and my battles. Before him, he solves my existence—the brilliant one whose voice is great. He gives wisdom to my spirit, and the matter will be found to have two general forms. Regarding this aspect of the Torah, the Kabbalistic Rabbi, Rabbi Recanati <note>Rabbi Menachem Recanati, a prominent 13th-14th century Italian Kabbalist</note>, of blessed memory, wrote:
The male is distinguished by heat, meaning he belongs to the latter part of the natural elements, and the bread <note>Likely a metaphor for sustenance or physical nature</note> is distinguished by cold. The male contains more heat than the female, while the female is distinguished by cold because she is in the middle boundary. The middle boundary does not leave its border, and therefore the female is colder than the male. These are his words.
Moshe said: This "Kuzari" <note>Referring to the work of Judah Halevi or the concept of the "Ideal Jew"</note> will agree with the words of the sage who wrote regarding the change of temperaments: that females are colder in temperament. However, the Rabbi, Rabbi Bahya, of blessed memory, gave a great explanation. In the middle, the female is distinguished by heat, and heat is more prevalent in her than in the other two parts.
And regarding the aspect of the distinction... that the female is hotter than the male, he proves this from four ways:
First: The nature of females is toward "redness" <note>original: *edomit*</note>, which is hotter than the male, whose nature is toward "whiteness" <note>original: *levanit*</note>.
Second: The female is more abundant in blood than the male... and blood is naturally hot; therefore, the female is hotter than the male.
Third: The pulse of the female is faster than the pulse of the male, as the "Greatest of Physicians" <note>Typically referring to Maimonides or Galen</note> mentioned in the "Gate of the Pulse"; and since all movement creates heat, if the female’s pulse is faster in movement than the male's, she is hotter than him.
Fourth: Sometimes it happens that the female is formed in the womb because of the heat of the male... <note>The text here navigates complex medieval biological theories regarding gender determination</note>. Thus, "these and those are the words of the Living God" <note>A Talmudic phrase indicating that both opposing views contain truth</note>.
The great Kabbalist, Rabbi Yom Tov <note>Possibly Rabbi Yom Tov Lipman-Muhlhausen or another medieval Kabbalist</note>, of blessed memory, wrote: The *Sefer Yetzirah* is sealed with the name of Nature. Just as the Name *YHV*, which is His Name, may He be blessed, can be permuted into six "wheels" <term>Galgalim: permutations or cycles of letters</term>, so too the letters *AMSh* <note>The Three Mothers: Air, Water, Fire</note> can be permuted into six cycles. If so, the water and the combination are in a state of doubt, divided into male and female. This means these three letters, hinting at Fire, Water, and Air, are placed together as male and female. This was the extent of his words.

->The Ra’avad, of Blessed Memory — Chapter 3, Mishnah 2 — and the Ramban, of Blessed Memory<-

The **Three Mothers, AMSh** <note>The letters Aleph (א), Mem (מ), and Shin (ש), representing the elements Air, Water, and Fire</note> are a secret of three wondrous and hidden things. The explanation is that when we come to investigate outside of its void, surrounding it like an entry into a hidden treasury, it comes from a simple power like a river of knowledge. All of them precede their causes, and therefore it is called "Ah" <note>original: *ah* (א-ה), possibly referring to a shortened form of a Divine Name</note> who created Man (*Adam*).

The text calls this a "secret," meaning the three Mothers—AMSh—are a great secret, wondrous and hidden, and He sealed them with **six rings**. This comes from Greatness and from doubled rings, and from it emerge Fire and Water. "Hidden" means the wisdom of the Mothers (AMSh) is their foundation, and from them were born the Three <note>Referring to the "Three Fathers" or primary elements</note> and their understanding, which are the "masters of the fathers" from which everything was created, out of the six for the sake of transformation.

In the expanse outside... and He **sealed them with six rings**. The explanation of the six rings is that they are the six extremities <term>Qatzvot: the six directions of the physical world—North, South, East, West, Up, and Down</term>. Through their power, they were completed in six forms, which are the permutations of the Name: *YHU, YHU, KYU, HUY*, and so on, as explained in Chapter 1. There, the forms are the sources for the various arrangements of man and the tastes for the moisture of bread.

The term "rings" is used because "in the ring of the King..." <note>A reference to Esther 8:8, implying that a decree sealed with the King's ring cannot be revoked</note>. He wrote them and mastered them according to what He desired to hide; and that which He desired to hide remained hidden. Because every "nature" is lacking, while all "Nature" is connected in its resting places, and all is imprinted in the Ring of His Emptiness—therefore they are also called "rings." He wrote the letter *Yod* from the name *YHU* corresponding to the *He* from above and the lines...

<column-break/>

The **Three Mothers, AMSh**, are a great secret, wondrous and hidden. It is written that the "proximity of the spirit" is like life. He [the author] of blessed memory used the phrase "Book and Limit" <note>original: *Sefer v'Qiras*, likely a variant or corruption of *Sefer v'Sippur*, the "Book and the Story" mentioned in the opening of Sefer Yetzirah</note> as a sign to describe a "great, wondrous, and hidden secret."
This corresponds to the secret of the letters:
- **Great Secret** corresponds to the letter *Mem* <note>Representing Water</note>.
- **Wondrous** corresponds to the letter *Aleph* <note>Representing Air</note>.
- **Hidden** corresponds to the letter *Shin* <note>Representing Fire</note>.

And He **sealed them with six rings**. This is to say that the Spirit <note>original: *Ruach*</note> moves through the six directions in a cycle, as the author of "Book and Limit" explained in the first chapter. This spirit cycles through the six alongside the secret of the Three Mothers, which is open to kindness and open to sight. It turns and cycles down to the lower realms, and from it come life and the secret of blessings. This refers to the secret of the three emanations of the King. It is a cycle, and it is the "Water of the *Mem*," and they are divided into **male and female**.

For the male is the opposite of the female, in the likeness of the **Upper Waters** to the **Lower Waters** <note>A common Kabbalistic metaphor for the flow of divine energy (Upper) and the reception by the physical world (Lower)</note>. The male was created through **Mercy** <term>Rachamim: the balanced attribute of beauty and compassion</term> and the female through **Kindness** <term>Chesed: the attribute of expansive giving</term>. And also regarding the "opening of the pomegranates," it is like the presence of water... the totality of the branches. The *Yod* went... their secret <unclear>...to the power...</unclear>

## Commentary of the Ramban, of Blessed Memory

The "Great Secret" comes from the power of **Understanding** <term>Tevunah: a dimension of divine intellect</term>. "Wondrous" refers to the Wisdom of Understanding, which rises above the **Supreme Crown** <term>Keter Elyon: the highest, most hidden Sephirah</term>. "Hidden" refers to the power of **Greatness** <term>Gedulah: another name for the Sephirah of Chesed/Kindness</term>.

He "sealed them with six rings"—these are the six extremities, which are the six dimensions established by the three letters of the Divine Name. Every letter contains five, as we explained regarding the matter of "He sealed the height with the *Yod*." He established the Three Mothers in His Great Name. These six rings are that in which everything is sealed, within the void that was in the seal of the ring.

From the "prevailing foundation," they are divided. The explanation of "divided" is that they are partitioned into sections, improving as they go. Every male and female requires this "great secret," which is the foundation of the Three Mothers, AMSh, along with the seal of the "Whistling Shin" <note>original: *Shin Shoreket*, referring to the sibilant, fire-like sound of the letter Shin</note> with the voice of a flame, and the *Aleph* which is the "Water" <note>The Ramban here seems to associate Aleph with the air that carries the moisture/water</term> that is the "Beauty" (*Tiferet*) within the body.

The **Three Mothers, AMSh**: from them were created the **Three Fathers**, who emerged and were included. From them, everything was created. The word "to create" <note>original: *levrot*</note> is used in the sense of "selection" <note>original: *berirah*</note>—sorting the good from the bad—rather than "to create" from nothing. This refers to the removal of transgressions.

# Maimonides, of Blessed Memory — Chapter 13, Mishnah 4 — The Ra’avad

Below the three tablets, there is a place for all water to return. This is lacking, as if in a state of rest below. To cover everything within the theory of the **Sefirot** <note>The ten creative powers or attributes in Kabbalah through which the Infinite reveals itself</note> is called "Names," and what is below them is called "Fathers." 

The totality of the Fathers is what constitutes the **Kingdoms** <note>original: *malkhukhot*, likely referring to the Sefirah of Malkhut/Kingship</note>. In the Name below, they are the foundation for all the Sefirot that are found within them. Thus, the Fathers are the fathers and foundations for all existence that comes from them. Behold, there are three names in Mishnah 5: "And He shall be hallowed in the world," for He is hallowed in the world. And when it says "male and female," it is interpreted regarding the **soul**. And when it says "the Queen/Kingdom is great," everything points toward the "Striker" <note>An obscure reference to a creative force</note>.

There are **Three Mothers: AMSh** <note>The letters Aleph (א), Mem (מ), and Shin (ש)</note> in the world: **Air, Water, and Fire**. Heaven was created from Fire, and Earth was created from Water, and Air was created from Spirit <note>original: *ruach*</note> which decides between them.

**Ra’avad:** Heaven is Fire and Water. Furthermore, the **Ra'al** in *Bereshit Rabbah* and the *Book of Illustration* <note>Sefer HaTziyur</note> in the Opening Discourse says: These are fire and water, and the heavens were fashioned from them. And of blessed memory, as the Sages said, they are in the firmament where the "runners" <note>celestial bodies</note> were frozen and created from fire and water, for "water is on His right and fire is on His left." 

Lower down they say: regarding the creation of the heavens, they were created from **Fire**. This refers to the heavens that are in **Power** <term>Gevurah: the Sefirah of Strength or Judgment, associated with Fire</term>. And regarding what is said in the Torah, "Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters," these are the firmaments in the heights. 

And the Earth was created from **Water**, as it is said: "Let the waters under the heaven be gathered together..." (Genesis 1:9). And some say that *Eloah* <note>a Name of God</note> shall be called "Earth." And **Air** was created from Spirit, as it is said: "For behold, He forms the mountains and creates the spirit" (Amos 4:13). Behold, the Air decides between the Fire and the Waters. The Earth and the South are in their branches which are engraved in the **Sphere** <term>Galgal: the celestial sphere or the cycle of the zodiac</term>, for they are the 22 letters. The engraving is in the record for those "rests of heaven" which receive the engraving. And of blessed memory, for He made the first firmaments which received the engravings; they are in the matter of **Power** <note>Gevurah</note>, and they are the "Fathers" unto them.

<meta>catchword: And the place</meta>

<column-break/>

The waters were called "water below." And the Spirit, which is the **Air**, decides between them. If so, the order is this: Fire, Air, Water, Earth. And behold, Aleph (א) is engraved... the quality of the writing says, of blessed memory: **Three Mothers AMSh**. 

Read it as a "book" and the transposition of the secret of the Three in the name of **God** (*El*). Just as a woman holds her son and influences him by her gait, so in this likeness is the secret of the Three Mothers in the creation of the world. 

**Heaven** was created first, and the offspring of the heavens are from Fire, just as one sees in the drawing of fire. If so, the heavens were created first from Fire, and they are the utterance of **AMSh**; thus it was in the heavens. And **Earth** was created from Water, and the Earth "drinks" the heavens. If so, Fire is above and Water—which is its opposite—is below. 

The **Aleph (א)** is the "Judge" above the element [of Water], but it is Fire; and it is poured down from the element of Heaven, which is Fire. The Aleph is **Air**, and Air is Spirit in everything that is said, except for "Spirit." If so, there is here a "strong tongue" <note>A term from Sefer Yetzirah referring to a grammatical or creative balance</note> that decides. This is what is written in the *Book of Formation*: "And Air from Spirit decides between them." 

The Aleph is a portion, thus the "tongue of decree" decides between them. It is divided into three parts... And our Teacher [says]: these Three Mothers, AMSh, through them were created the **Three Fathers**. 

These are the Fathers: **Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob**. And the sign is within the name *Eloah* (א-ל-ו-ה). He "made souls in Haran" (Genesis 12:5), for the generations of the Heaven and Earth are in their creation, as it is said: "These are the generations of the heaven and the earth when they were created" (*be-hibare’am*) <note>A famous wordplay in Hebrew: *be-hibare’am* (when they were created) contains the letters of *be-Abraham* (through Abraham)</note>. 

And the Fathers are the **Chariot** <term>Merkavah: the Divine Throne-Chariot, representing the structure of the spiritual world</term>: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and He is One. And the [letters] *Zayin* and *Tav*... One King in the **Attribute of Justice**. And between them is Abraham, as they have already explained: thirteen words for the work of the Tabernacle. And from there he received the Torah and delivered it to them—Genesis with 23 attributes, and they are the foundation of the thirteen powers. And the Fathers were attached to and influenced by the secret of **AMSh** in the Sphere. And below, everything was created...

<meta>This page continues the exploration of the Three Mother Letters (Aleph, Mem, Shin) from the Sefer Yetzirah, transitioning from the previous discussion on the Sefirot and "Fathers" into the specific linguistic and elemental properties of these letters as taught by the commentators Ha-Ramab, the Ra'avad, and the Ramban.</meta>

### Commentary of Ha-Ramab — Chapter 3, Mishnah 3

The three mothers are **A-M-Sh** <note>original: "AMSh" — the letters Aleph (א), Mem (מ), and Shin (ש)</note>. **Mem** is humming/silent, **Shin** is whistling/hissing, and **Aleph** is the mediating law that balances between them. In its repetition, why is **Mem** called "silent"? Because the mouth is closed, yet one can prove its sound through the compression of the lips, for the source of the letter **Mem** is the mouth and the lips that hold it firm. **Shin** is called "whistling" because a person does not need to open his lips as much as he does for other vowel sounds; rather, he should not close his mouth more than necessary for the sound. **Aleph** is the "deciding law between them"; it is written of it that one should neither fully open nor fully close the mouth. The reason is that the sounds of the letters are drawn from the "Place of the Silent" <note>An anatomical/mystical reference to the mouth's position</note> and are called the "resting of the lips." Therefore, if the lips are joined too tightly, there is no power to demonstrate the sound, and it becomes "silent/mute." 

"Silent" <note>original: *dumamat*</note> is a term related to hearing a voice, meaning a "silence" that contains a voice within it, and a voice without silence. This is the image that I would see before my eyes at the time there was silence; at other times, a form was absent from my sight because it was making a sound heard. And the **Shin** is from the "whistling letters" <note>original: *sharikoni*</note>, and "whistling" comes from the language of "hissing for them" <note>A reference to Zechariah 10:8</note>, and therefore one does not need to open the lips very wide. It is spoken through the closing of the lips. **Aleph** is from the letters that rest in the throat, and therefore it is the "deciding law between them" <note>i.e., it balances the labial 'Mem' and the dental 'Shin'</note>. 

Rabbi Aaron, of blessed memory, wrote: **Mem** is "silent" so that the Kabbalist can make the **Mem** sound begin with the letter **Mem** in a secret way, where the **Mem** comes doubled. One must demonstrate this with the lips to create the pronunciation. Any **Shin** that is adjacent or begins with the letter **Shin** will not perform its action without the voice being heard speaking to him. Concerning this secret, it is said: "The voice of the Lord is in power" <note>Psalm 29:4</note>. The **Aleph** is the "deciding law" because He and His Name are a "double silence," like a standing force, yet also heard in the voice through the way of the **Shin**. This is why it says "Aleph is the mediating law between them." This ends his words.

---

### The Ra’avad, of Blessed Memory
The three mothers, **A-M-Sh**, have their foundations in **Air, Water, and Fire**. For with the carving of the **Aleph**, **Air** <note>original: *avir*</note> was created in the world and in the soul. And with the carving of the **Mem**, and in its snowy consistency, there came to it a source of "living water." Behold, the Spirit of the Almighty, the life-force, hovers over the surface of the **Water**. And with the carving of the **Shin**, **Fire** came forth from the water, as it is said: "Water was consumed by fire." And from them were born the "Fathers" <note>The secondary elements or derivative forces</note> in these three, which correspond to the three existences of the letters **A-M-Sh**.

### Ha-Ramab, of Blessed Memory
The three mothers, **A-M-Sh**, through which three "letters" <note>meaning primary elements</note> were created: namely, **Spirit, Water, Fire**. From them, everything was created, and this is the secret of the Three Mothers. **Aleph** is Air; **Mem** is Water; **Shin** is Fire. Heaven was created first from **Fire**—thus fire is above—and Earth was created from **Water**.

### Commentary of the Ramban, of Blessed Memory
The explanation is that from the "carvings" of the **Water**, snow was made, and from the snow came light for the existence of the earth, as it is written: "For to the snow He says, 'Be earth'" <note>Job 37:6</note>. ### Maimonides, may his memory be a blessing, Chapter 1, Mishnah 4; the Ra’avad, may his memory be a blessing.

And regarding the system of time, one must understand definitively and say that within this "great diameter" <note>likely referring to the celestial equator or the cosmic axis</note> there is a testimony to His unity. The choice of matter changes and varies from one to another because of the physical materials <note>original: *chomarim*, referring to the Aristotelian 'hyle' or primal matter</note>, not because of the Divine Form, may He be blessed. He provides for all forms and enacts the laws of the constellations and their order; He is One, and all powers come to them from His grace and the flow of His blessings. He is exalted and blessed, the God of all. Therefore, our Sages said in the Book of the Earlier Exile <note>an unidentified or mystical source text</note> regarding these matters: At His beginning, He stood by Himself in the ultimate perfection of all completion, a total perfection at the peak of wholeness, elevated and removed from any deficiency. This is why it says "He stood by Himself." Thus far the words of Rabbi Eliezer the Small <note>original: *Ha-Katan*—a common self-effacing title for scholars</note>.

Heat is necessarily a "subject" <note>original: *sovekt*, likely a corruption of the philosophical term for "subject" or "substance"</note>, while cold is necessarily derived from it, for heat is the primary state and cold is its absence. And in this regard, he did not mention the active parts. Moses [the Levite?] <note>original: *Ha-Tuviel*, likely a scribal error for *Ha-Levi*</note> said: It has been chosen for us from all your investigations, for it is already settled in Natural Wisdom <note>Physics</note> that heat is closer to moisture, just as moisture is closer to [dryness] than to the [vacuum]. And regarding the change of the sensible matter <note>original: *chomer*, referring to physical substance</note>, the element is heat, whereas the sensible absence is cold. This is as Alexander <note>likely Alexander of Aphrodisias, a 2nd-century commentator on Aristotle</note> says: that cold is the cause of destruction/entropy, not the cause of existence. The matter <note>original: *chomer*</note> of the element was the cause of existence and conduction, and this matter was high above the [spheres] in the Galaxy <note>original: *Galgal*</note>. And it has a degree, for the degree known to the wise is something that approaches the essence of moisture more than water itself; the moisture of the Air is greater than the moisture of the Water. This is the wisdom: that the Water was once more moist than the Air, to disagree with his lofty response. The action of a simple element is like a compound one, acting by the power of nature on its own, and its power is not from itself. Therefore they agreed...

...a decider between them <note>The letter Aleph represents the Air/Spirit which balances the Fire/Heat and Water/Cold</note>. This is because the Season of Tevet <note>Winter Solstice</note> is cold and [moist?], and it succeeds in its coldness. But when the matter reaches the Season of Nisan <note>Spring Equinox</note>, which is the time of the living Spirit, the cold is finished and diminished little by little, and the Spirit and the [breeze] expand. The day lengthens bit by bit, and the heat increases. This leads to the "death" of the harmful [elements] as they move from the hidden to the revealed.

Therefore, in the Season of Nisan, the earth brings forth grass and herbs, and the walking creatures are praised. However, they are not completely finished until they reach the ultimate heat, which is the time of the Season of Tammuz <note>Summer Solstice</note>. Then the [moisture] is totally nullified until they are ready to be transformed and changed. This is the Season of Tishrei <note>Autumn Equinox</note>, until it returns to the Season of Tevet and the seeds are moistened, and they go once more through the cycle of the wheat.

### The Ra’avad, may his memory be a blessing — Chapter 3

He made the letter *Chet* <note>The eighth letter of the Hebrew alphabet</note> king. From this Supreme Crown, the breath of life reaches the neck, and through the Crown and within it, it reaches the "Life of the Worlds," from which comes the life of the entire world. This corresponds to the attribute of Mercy <term>Chesed; the attribute of loving-kindness</term> within the wheels of the Chariot <term>Merkavah; the divine assembly or vehicle seen in Ezekiel's vision</term>, and among the divine existences, it corresponds to the "Magic of Mercy." And as for the "Spirit in the year," it is the "Voice of the Spirit" returning to the places of judgment from the twelve existences at the end of the week, to see the voice and the spirit of Mercy. And in the body, it is in the *kefesh*. <note>Interpretation: "Kefesh" is an unusual term here, likely a variant of "Nefesh" (soul) or related to a physical covering.</note> Explanation: in the body, this comes from the language of "shield" and "limbs," which implies a small amount; and so is the translation of "the midst" <note>Aramaic: go</note>. ## Commentary of the Ramban, may his memory be a blessing

There is a place in Scripture where "Mercy" is mentioned twice, and in the Sefer Yetzirah, it is divided... a male. And when it departs into the Mercy of the "Radiance" <term>Zohar</term> and the Sephirah of *Binah* (Understanding), there is a voice to separate us. During the time of the "existences," at the moment of birth, the "womb" is weary in the division of the children in the "mother-letters" <note>Aleph, Mem, Shin</note> and at the time of births in Mercy. And Mercy established male and female in the division of the tongue... 10 times: We have ascended to Mercy, the word "Radiance" is male, because they are transformed, receiving from the "Master of the Branches."

# Ramban, of blessed memory, Chapter 3, Mishnah 4

Because the substance of the earth is dense. It is divided into sixty and eight parts <note>Likely referring to a specific medieval calculation of the ratios of the elements or humors</note>. From the power of the bread <note>original: lechem; possibly a metaphor for solid matter or sustenance</note> which is close to being moist and humid by its very essence. And in the water, it is close and humid to the waters, and from the power of the moisture <note>original: luz; here likely meaning a core moisture or essence</note> which is pressed upon the waters and cools by itself. And the pressure cools and covers from the power of the water, drawing near and entering from its own essence. Therefore, those things which are acted upon are to be living, and they enter as is revealed in the nature of the rings and so forth. These are the qualities, and the middle voice is neither hot nor cold. The head, like a sieve, begins the mixing of the mountains <note>likely a metaphor for the lobes of the brain or the higher faculties</note>; its sound is above, like the sound of moisture, and it extends and gives birth to heat. The belly is from water—the lower belly—and water gives birth to cold. And the body is from the spirit <note>original: ruach/air</note> between them, like the fruit of the moisture, and it gives birth to height for the heart; it is settled in the place of the cold, and it is the dwelling place of the soul of the spirit <note>the 'Ruach,' the middle level of the soul associated with breath and emotion</note> to decide between the moist heat and the small cold. And here is the beginning of life: it is the heart, just as the Ramban <note>Rabbi Nachmanides, 13th-century scholar and mystic</note> said. The author of the *Kuzari* <note>Rabbi Judah Halevi, 12th-century philosopher</note> said, based on speculative thought, that the assembly of life must be in the heart. And if a challenger should claim there is another division, specifically that the beginning of life is in the liver—because there is the source of the blood, and as long as the body is nourished it lives, and when the blood is absent it dies—it should be noted that the soul of movement <note>the animating force</note> precedes the state of living in nature. Their eyes were opened to the soul, which is the opposite of what they thought; the beginning of life is the heart, and it exists before the formation of the limbs, and it is the first to be formed to sustain the vitality of the cold. Therefore, the one who challenges this should accept the Ramban's position as correct, for the heart is the beginning of the "standing" <note>existence</note> and the movement given to the embryo in its mother's womb, which moves through the intermediaries of the liver which carries the blood.

### Ramban, of blessed memory

He raised it initially through the power of <term>Binah</term> <note>Understanding; the second higher emanation in Kabbalah</note> and tied the letter *Shin* to the Spirit of the Living God, which is called the <term>Supreme Crown</term> <note>original: K.E. (Keter Elyon)</note>.

in the world. In the concavity <note>original: ka’arurit; referring to the curvature of the celestial spheres</note>

*Shin* of fire, the specific heat will be activated

# The Ra'avad, of blessed memory, on Chapter 3, Mishnah 8

And the soul is placed over the Kingdom <note>original: Malkhut; the tenth and final emanation in Kabbalistic thought, often associated with the physical realm</note>, for in the hand of the King is every living thing. It is also interpreted specifically as the world of the spheres of the Chariot <note>original: Merkavah; referring to the divine Chariot in Ezekiel’s vision</note>, the living beings of the Chariot, and the Levites. The covering <note>original: kaporet; the lid of the Ark of the Covenant</note> surrounds the wings and the living beings of the Chariot, as well as the rotation of the Chariots over their heads, their paths, the timing of their standing and descending, their arrival, and the resting of their existence. Their name is derived from the language of "change" and the "alternation" of the divine utterances within them according to the alignment of the angles. For every existence and every path has a nature known by its movement, and from every heart comes "growth," and from every five "cities of understanding" <note>original: Binah</note>. Their natures change according to their location, or their proximity to that which opposes their nature, or according to the "eight camps" in Grace <note>original: Hesed</note>, as I hinted at above. Since all existences—the silent <note>minerals</note>, the growing <note>plants</note>, the living <note>animals</note>, and the speaking <note>humans</note>—are all included in the primary existences, they are all contained within the World, the Year, and the Soul. Therefore, the individual unit is determined by their influence, as it is said, "and waters they shall remember," though it was not taught in the Name. Furthermore, following this path, whatever is attributed to the World is also attributed to the Soul and the Year.

---

->The Ramban, of blessed memory<-

He made the letter Mem <note>original: M"S; likely a scribal shorthand for the letter Mem, representing water</note> king over water and tied a crown to it, combining them with one another. With it, He sealed the Earth in the world, Coldness in the year, and the Fruit of the Womb in the soul, both male and female.
The explanation of "He made the letter Mem king" is that He placed the Mem at the head. Just as a king serves as the spirit for the entire nation, so He made the letter of Rulership <note>original: Ha-Ma-Sha-L; a play on the word for "rule" and the letter Mem</note> king over every letter Mem at the beginning of the speech... in this section, the speech is divided into parts.
Regarding male and female: There is an "Earth and Coldness" that is the birthright and essence of males, and there is an "Earth and Coldness" that is the birthright and essence of females. Behold, there is a "womb" for both the male and the female; therefore, it must be said to the enlightened one <note>original: maskil; an initiate into mystical secrets</note> that their origin is from Water. This is not the case for the letter Samekh, but rather the letter Mem, whether in the male or the female. The Mem is found at the beginning and the end—representing the Upper Waters and the Lower Waters.

->The Ra'avad, of blessed memory<-

"He made the letter Mem king" — just as they were elevated initially through the power of Understanding <note>original: Binah</note>, and He tied a crown to it. For He tied the letter Mem <note>original: M"T</note> to the Spirit of their Life... the second... the power of the male nature within it. "Earth in the world" — meaning the inner rotation within the ice of the earth, positioned according to its stability toward the sphere above it. And behold... for the understanding of the spheres of the Chariots... from water to the cloud; their hollows are necessarily full... as it says later, this is... that water is full of water. "And Coldness in the year" — the meaning is that aside from the power of the Mem, the nature of coldness through the existences in Grace <note>original: Hesed</note> will arise, and the coldness will be awakened from them through the power of the prayer of the letter Mem, the praise of the Eternal. "And the Fruit of the Womb in the soul" — meaning the power of coldness for Grace in everything; this is the coldness from the power of Living Waters... thus the coldness... the cause of death is remembered here, for it is cold and dry, and afterwards... the life of all that lives.

## Commentary of the Ramban, of blessed memory

"Earth" in the world: through it, water contains "dust" for the male and "viscous moisture" for the female. "Coldness in the year": during which there are fruits and vessels and small things that live by means of the cold. "Fruit of the womb in the soul": meaning the power of the fetus in the body before it is born as male or female.

<meta>This page continues the commentary on Chapter 3 of the *Sefer Yetzirah* (The Book of Formation). While the previous page discussed the elemental foundations of the universe, this page focuses on the astrological and biological correspondences of the letter *Mem* (Water), specifically its relation to the human anatomy (the belly/womb) and the psychological state of "Trust" (Bitachon). It features a significant commentary by Moshe Botril, a 14th-century scholar known for his rationalist and medical approach to Kabbalah.</meta>

### Chapter 3, Mishnah 8

These spirits are meant for the living <note>original: *chayot*; referring to both living creatures and the celestial "Living Beings" of the Divine Chariot</note>, arranged in a spiral <note>original: *chilzon*; literally "snail," here describing the winding or cyclical motion of the heavens</note> according to the twelve signs of the Zodiac. As you already know, the signs are divided into seven males and seven females <note>The text specifies seven and seven, though traditionally the Zodiac is split six and six; this may reflect a specific cosmological variant in the manuscript</note>, and this same law applies to the spirits. Likewise, there are six male and female correspondences according to the stars and the constellations, as well as male and female aspects within the soul. This pattern holds true for the silent <note>minerals</note>, the growing <note>plants</note>, the living <note>animals</note>, and the speaking <note>humans</note>. All of them exist in the name of the Lord; "May the glory of the Lord endure forever; let the Lord rejoice in His works" (Psalm 104:31).

Regarding the soul: this refers to its value within the tens of merits <note>unclear reading in the original</note>. All of this comes to pass because of their internal nature. Our teacher <note>likely Rabbeinu Bahya ibn Paquda, author of *Duties of the Heart*</note> explained that "the belly in the soul" refers to the spirit of **Trust** <note>original: *Bitachon*; a central virtue in Jewish ethics</note>. For trust is the calculation of the pure and the guarded. Trust itself is the "claim" or the essence of this purity. Thus far are the words of our Master Bahya, of blessed memory.

**Moshe Botril says:** Regarding this matter, I must guide you. Secrets have been revealed to me, and intelligence has been granted to me from the heights that does not occur to everyone, to suddenly grasp the number of their glory known to the Sages. I shall tell you how the belly relates to deep Trust, and how it performs the opposite action to Trust <note>referring to the physical manifestation of anxiety</note>. Consider how Trust, when we hope and persist in it, absorbs that which opposes it. The Name <note>God</note> mends the "guarded portion." Therefore, it is said to the "included ones" that Trust is the vessel of Trust. Its physical action draws away the turbidity of the blood, which would otherwise become defiled in the liver and the spleen. When filled with refined Trust, the blood becomes holy and pure, and its turbidity and total foulness are contracted through grace and purity. Otherwise, the "black bile" <note>original: *marah shechorah*; in medieval medicine, this humor was associated with melancholy and depression</note> would spread to the entire body, and the body would be afflicted as if by a plague.

But when Trust is pure and refined, the influence of the black bile is softened, and the "plague" of the blood’s punishment is recognized and removed. That which was spread out is gathered, and a "good heart" <note>good health/disposition</note> crowns the person. Conversely, when the soul is distant from this matter, joy and revelation depart from it. This is why the Levites <note>scholars</note> say that Trust is the vessel of Trust. This is also why our Sages of blessed memory said in the Talmud, in the chapter titled "He who sees" (*Berakhot* 61b): **"The spleen laughs, and the gizzard grinds."** <note>This Talmudic quote links internal organs to emotional and physical functions; here, the spleen is linked to joy/laughter</note>

**Moshe Botril says:** A great secret of the world is placed before us in the Talmud, and I have written it in my heart as a firm and learned principle. I have come to awaken the Sages to these precise, arranged matters: that the living being should be pure and joyful.

Behold, the author of the *Book of Formation* wrote: **"A scale of merit, a scale of guilt, and the tongue of decree deciding between them."** <note>A foundational quote from Sefer Yetzirah regarding the balance of the universe</note> Regarding the "belly" and the "voice," it is a matter of "if you have merit." The belly is the scale of merit <note>original: *kaf zechut*</note> and the scale of guilt <note>original: *kaf chovah*</note>, because within the belly, no creature can stand or endure without balance. All that is said in this chapter is to hint at the secret of the lips and the "doubled secret" <note>referring to the double letters in the Hebrew alphabet</note>. The earthly Temple is aligned directly opposite the Heavenly Temple. His kingdom on earth is like His kingdom in the firmament. This is what the Master of Kabbalah wrote in the *Book of Secrets* <note>original: *Sefer HaRazim*</note>: "World enters within world..." All of this is to demonstrate that they are witnesses to one another, as it is said, "Who is the voice...?"

->The chapter is completed. It is an all-encompassing and powerful explanation.<-

# Ravad <note>Rabbi Abraham ben David of Posquières, a 12th-century legalist and kabbalist</note> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Chapter 3, Mishnah 8 &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Rambam <note>Maimonides, though he did not write a commentary on Sefer Yetzirah, his philosophical views are often contrasted here with kabbalistic thought</note>

And in the Tractate of Fasts <note>original: *Taanit*; a volume of the Talmud dealing with communal fasting and the theology of rain</note>, it is likewise mentioned there that some [rains] are "male" and some are "female" <note>original: *zachar* and *nekevah*. In Jewish thought, "male" rain is strong and saturates the earth, while "female" rain is gentle and allows the earth to receive</note>. There is the upper rain, and there is the "reed-like" <note>likely a scribal variation or error for *nekevah* (female)</note> rain of the downpour. Indeed, we find times where the language of the Bible proves this, and at other times, the language of the "reed" <note>female</note>. It is the same with the wind, and the same with the flow. Water is male, and some [waters] are female. This applies also to the stars and the constellations. There is a female land, and there is a male land. Likewise, there is a male wind and a female wind.

The winds are divided into twelve specific types of winds, and corresponding to them are the twelve [movements] of the sun's wind. These consist of the four "fathers" <note>the four cardinal directions</note> and their eight "offspring" <note>the intermediate directions</note>: (1) Eastern wind, (2) Western wind, (3) Northern wind, (4) Southern wind, (5) North-Eastern, (6) South-Eastern, (7) North-Western, (8) South-Western. Furthermore, there is the High-Eastern and Low-Eastern, High-Western and Low-Western, High-Southern and Low-Southern. These are the four depths, for they descend into the abysses <note>original: *tehomot*</note>.

<column-break/>

Therefore, it is said that the letter *Yod* <note>the first letter of the Tetragrammaton, symbolizing the point of creation</note> brought forth the created being. This is the "Secret of the Sphere" <note>original: *galgal*; referring to the celestial orbs or the cycle of letters</note> made by the Awesome One, blessed be He, whose name is *YHV* <note>a three-letter version of the Divine Name</note> in the permutation of the letter *Heh*. These "Lords" <note>ruling forces</note> are hints that He who rules over all establishes the intention. It is hidden within the Name of the Oath. This concludes the words of the Rabbi of *Le-Hakrin* <note>a potential corruption of a commentator's name, possibly "the Elder" or a specific geographic attribution</note>.

Our teacher Hai <note>Rabbi Hai Gaon, 939–1038, the last of the Babylonian Geonim</note>, of blessed memory, wrote: He who moves the *Aleph* <note>the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, associated with air and the divine breath</note> is like the *Aleph* which stands at the head of all "faces" <note>dimensions or facets of reality</note>. So it is in this verse that follows, where the Blessed One intends to permute, as with the letter *Heh*. The Name is with them in the permutation, occurring twice, as we say: "The Merciful One brings His intention into its daughters" <note>a metaphor for divine energy manifesting in the lower worlds</note>. This is the "Crown" <note>original: *Keter*; the highest emanation</note>, the "Knot" <note>original: *kesher*; the connection between the divine and the mundane</note>, allowing the *Aleph* and the *Heh* to be at the beginning, to permute the spirit of man at the start of its formation. He divided with the letters *Mem* and *Samekh* between the letter *Aleph* and the letter *Zayin* to include the male in all the "watering" <note>sustenance</note> through the blessings of the *Heh*. Therefore, he leaned the...
