<meta>This page transitions from the previous discussion on the gendered nature of cosmic forces (male and female rains and winds) to the specific linguistic and kabbalistic mechanics of the "Seven Double Letters." It links the grammatical "hardness" of these letters to the cosmic struggle against Amalek and explores the seven pairs of opposites that define human existence.</meta>

# ->The Rambam <note>likely an attribution to Nachmanides (Ramban), as Maimonides did not write kabbalistic commentaries</note>, Chapter 3, Mishnah 1, the Ravad <note>Rabbi Abraham ben David of Posquières</note><-

Which is called *Dagesh* <note>a dot placed in a letter to indicate a "hard" or doubled pronunciation</note>. And the nature of the "Doubles" <note>the seven letters—Bet, Gimel, Dalet, Kaf, Peh, Resh, Tav—that can take a Dagesh</note> is the power of transformation, the secret of "The war of the Lord against Amalek" <note>Exodus 17:16</note>. Understand this well. Every *Gimel* <note>the letter ג</note> is entirely a *Dagesh*, and before it... <unclear>sidis</unclear>... as the Sages, of blessed memory, said: "His army is like the leaven [of the war of the Dagesh]" because we lean on the thunder... <note>original: *har'emam*</note> the Lord [fights] against Amalek. This implies that the "hard" sound is like a thunderclap, just like the *Dagesh* from the beginning. Therefore, "the war of the Lord against Amalek" teaches us about the struggle between the forces, for it is written: "Because a hand is upon the throne of Yah <note>a name of God</note>, the Lord will have war with Amalek from generation to generation" <note>Exodus 17:16</note>, until the seed of Amalek is blotted out.

Tenderness is opposite of Hardness; Mercy <term>Chesed; the Sefirah of loving-kindness</term> is opposite of Strength <term>Gevurah; the Sefirah of judgment and power</term>; Beauty <term>Tiferet; the Sefirah of harmony</term> is opposite of Ugliness <note>original: *ki hamalkut benekevot*—perhaps "for the kingdom is in the females"</note>. The nature of the Seven Doubles and their foundations are: (1) Life, (2) Peace, (3) Wisdom, (4) [Grace], (5) Wealth, (6) Seed <note>Fertility</note>, and (7) Dominion. The matter of **Life** is drawn from the "Source of Life," and He is the life of all life, the Life of the Worlds. From Him comes the life of the *Sefirot* <note>the ten divine emanations</note> and all that is between them; from Him comes the life of 
<margin>And He is</margin>
the heavens, the animals, and the stone—to the point that even the stone is called "living," for it is the "Land of the Living." From Him comes the life of the plant, the animal, the speaker <note>humanity</note>, and the moving creature, and the living water; everything that has the breath of the spirit of life is directed toward Him. And its opposite is **Death**. From it [the side of judgment] come the Gates of Death and the Gates of Shame. And regarding the memory of Life and Death it is said: "A time to be born and a time to die" <note>Ecclesiastes 3:2</note>, which relates to the concepts of the staffs and the three [forces]. And "A time to kill and a time to heal." For killing is the weakening of the vessel that receives life, while healing is the repair of the vessel that receives life. And the life of every living thing is drawn from the power of the *Shekhinah* <note>the Divine Presence</note>, for He is the secret of life and the King of the Universe.

**Peace**: Our Sages, of blessed memory, said: "His name is Peace," as it is said: "And he called Him 'The Lord is Peace'" <note>Judges 6:24</note>. This is the side of Mercy (*Chesed*), regarding the things upon which the world stands: Justice, Truth, and Peace. Peace is the deciding factor between the Attribute of Mercy and the Attribute of Judgment. When the Holy One, blessed be He, uses strength and weapons as a "Man of War"—such as at the [Red] Sea—it is the side of transformation and "beating" the nations. But in a time of peace, the Holy One uses Peace, as it is said: "May the Lord lift His countenance toward you and give you peace" <note>Numbers 6:26</note>. There is war in the Covenant <note>original: *brit*</note>... like a man who speaks words of war. There is a time to gather in the Law of Peace, and a time to conquer in the Law of War. Know that **Silence** is from the side of Mercy and Peace, while **Speech** <note>here meaning loud or contentious speech</note> is from the side of Judgment and War. Peace is the foundation of the world, for the world stands upon it; Peace is the foundation that balances between Mercy (Right) and Judgment (Left), Front and Back. As it is said: "He makes peace in His heights" <note>Job 25:2</note>.

Thus: "A time to be silent" <note>Ecclesiastes 3:7</note> corresponds to the attribute of **Wisdom**, for its secret is a "still, small voice." "A time to speak" corresponds to **Folly**, for it is found "in a multitude of words." "A time to sew" the torn pieces corresponds to Wisdom, and "a time to tear" corresponds to Folly, as the Sages said: "He who tears [his garments] in his anger..." <note>Talmud Shabbat 105b</note>. Sewing pertains to restoration. So it is with the joints of a person that are disconnected... "A time to tear" comes from all types of folly.

**Wealth**: "A time to gather"—this is to gather wealth and precious things... and because of this, [it can lead to] poverty. "A time to cast away stones"—meaning to cast away my hopes [for material gain]. "A time to seek" the side of wealth and place, and "a time to lose" my eyes [from it]. Wealth comes from the side of *Gevurah* <note>Strength</note>, as it is said: "Out of the North comes gold" <note>Job 37:22</note>. 

From what is said: "A time to embrace" corresponds to the attribute of **Grace** and union, and "a time to refrain from embracing" corresponds to ugliness. "A time to keep" corresponds to the attribute of Beauty (*Tiferet*), regarding the memory of [avoiding] ugliness. "A time to cast away" corresponds to the secret of divorce. 

**Seed** <note>Fertility</note>: "A time to give birth" corresponds to the side of Mercy (*Chesed*)...

The text provides both the primary source material and influential commentaries that explain how these letters govern the dualities of the human experience.</meta>

Seven doubles: seven and not six, seven and not eight. <note>A classic formula from Sefer Yetzirah emphasizing the precision of the divine structure.</note> Their strength is established and their source is fixed, and the masculine stands upon its foundations and its opposite stands upon its base.
In the world of the Sefirot <note>original: "S"M", likely shorthand for Sefirot and Middot/Attributes</note>, they serve to clarify the Crown <term>Atarah</term> <note>The lowest Sefirah, Malchut, often called the Crown</note> from the category of the seven doubles.
Seven and not eight: this is a scale used to include Understanding <term>Binah</term> within the general rule of the doubles, for Grace <term>Chen</term> is the permutation <note>The word "Chen" (grace) is an anagram of "Noach" and is used here to describe kabbalistic transformations</note>. The desire of the mouth is the permutation according to the supernal pattern.
The six extremities <note>the six directions: Up, Down, East, West, North, South</note> are lacking a permutation, but not the three upper Sefirot. The Masculine <note>original: "Dechar"</note> (represented by the letter Ayin-Tet) stands on its foundation <term>Yesod</term>, and the Beauty <term>Tiferet</term> <note>original: "Taf"</note> is reversed upon its base with strength and source.
"And He shall give him mercy" <note>referring to the Sefirah of Chesed</note>—this is the permutation of Understanding <term>Binah</term>.
The seven doubles correspond to the atonement <note>A play on the mnemonic "BGD KPRT", where "KPRT" shares a root with "Kapparah" or atonement</note> of the above and the below, right and left, front and back, with the Holy Palace aligned in the center. This explains the totality of every body and every existence.

Seven doubles: B, G, D, K, P, R, T <note>The letters Bet, Gimel, Dalet, Kaf, Peh, Resh, and Tav</note>. No fewer than seven and no more than seven. They correspond to the seven extremities, for the seven doubles are detailed by the Author of the Book <note>the traditional author of Sefer Yetzirah</note>. He who knows the plain meaning <term>Peshat</term> understands the double and its opposite.
And this is the "Quiet World"... the eight quarters of the statutes. The seven doubles (BGD KPRT) correspond to the directions of "Above" and "Under." And if so, there are seven extremities, of which six are the directions: Up and Down, East and West, North and South. And the Holy Palace is aligned in the middle.
The Holy Palace in the center carries them all. <note>In this cosmology, the center point is not just a location but the sustaining force of the three-dimensional world.</note>
The power doubles everything. The Holy Palace is this world standing in the center, which is the secret of the Sabbath <note>original: "Shevui," related to the number seven and the Seventh Day</note>. This is the secret of the Holy Torah dwelling in the midst of this people.
Since the Author of the Book says the Holy Palace is aligned in the center, it implies a pattern from without. The Holy Creatures <term>Chayot HaKodesh</term> sing and say: "Blessed be the glory of the Lord from His place" <note>Ezekiel 3:12</note>.
He is the "Place of the World," but the world is not His place. <note>A famous rabbinic teaching that God encompasses the universe, but the universe does not encompass God.</note> The Holy One, blessed be He, carries everything from above and from below.

### The Ra'avad <note>Rabbi Abraham ben David of Posquières, a 12th-century French commentator</note>, of blessed memory; Chapter 1, Mishnah 10; The Rambam <note>Moses Maimonides, though this specific mystical text is more often associated with the school of the Ramban, Nachmanides</note>, of blessed memory.

(Dead) for it is the Sphere of the Thrones <note>original: "Galgal HaKiseot", referring to a high level of the celestial hierarchy</note>. And "a time to die" <note>Ecclesiastes 3:2</note> out of all joy. And "a time to plant" the wings, for Kindness is the Tree of Righteousness from every wing. And "a time to uproot what is planted" from the window of the palms from all joy. 
Dominion: "a time to dance" <note>Ecclesiastes 3:4</note> out of all dominion. And "a time to mourn" out of all servitude. And "a time to weep" out of all servitude. And "a time to laugh" out of all dominion, as we explained above.

And regarding the nature of the mixed opposites <term>Temurot</term> <note>The concept that every quality has a polar opposite, such as Wisdom and Folly</note>, as it is said: "Six things the Lord hates, and seven are an abomination to His soul: haughty eyes, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood; a heart that devises wicked schemes, feet that are quick to rush into evil, a false witness who breathes out lies, and one who stirs up conflict among brothers" <note>Proverbs 6:16-19</note>. 
Know that by the sign of the tongue, the heat of the "Holy, Holy, Holy" <note>original: "KDS", referring to the Trisagion</note> is a "lying tongue" in the opposites. Therefore, "the remnant of Israel will do no wrong; they will tell no lies, nor will a deceitful tongue be found in their mouths" <note>Zephaniah 3:13</note>. 
"Haughty eyes" correspond to the pattern of Wisdom, and within it, the goal includes all eyes and angers, which is the attribute of the "window." However, there is a counterpart for good, for the purpose and the doubled power, and it is in the "wheel" <note>original: "Ba-Akalah"</note>, its name is Tree. 
"Hands that shed [blood]" is the opposite of the right hand; the handle of his hand is supported with him. 
"A heart that devises wicked schemes" is the opposite of the body of Jacob, and the strength of Esau is the opposite of Beauty <term>Tiferet</term> <note>The central Sefirah, representing balance or the heart</note>. 
"Feet that are quick to rush into evil"—these are the opposites of Victory <term>Netzach</term> and Splendor <term>Hod</term> <note>The two Sefirot associated with the legs or supports of the divine chariot</note>. 
"A false witness who breathes out lies" is the opposite of Foundation <term>Yesod</term> <note>The Sefirah associated with truth and procreation</note>, which is a witness to the heat (of the fallen). 
"One who stirs up conflict among brothers" is the opposite of peace between the hot <note>possibly referring to the biblical Ham</note> and the brothers.

And these are the names of the opposites: Strangers, cruel, by my necessity, a man in trembling. A man of iniquity, a seed that merits [or "zodiac"], humming. One who dwells in wickedness. A throne for the simpleton. Lacking heart. The opposite of "the crown of the poor." As it is written: "A slack hand makes poor, but the hand of the diligent makes rich" <note>Proverbs 10:4</note>. So too, Foundation is bound and "a father rejoices," and so "a foolish son is the grief of his mother." 
The opposite of Wisdom is folly and madness. So "one who brings in" <note>original: "mevis"</note> is the opposite of Foundation. The opposite of a throne <note>original: "karkas"</note> is violence. "The wise in heart will receive commandments" <note>Proverbs 10:8</note>—meaning from Beauty <term>Tiferet</term>—and to where it is [directed], the opposite of the wise is "prating lips shall fall," meaning folly and perversion. 
The opposite of the crown of the poor: "The wealth of the rich is their fortified city, but poverty is the ruin of the poor" <note>Proverbs 10:15</note>. Deceitful lodgings are an abomination to the Lord, but the grace of Solomon is His will. 
The opposite of pride is disgrace. To the righteous man belong wealth and honor. Heat <note>or "haughtiness"</note> is the opposite of the righteous. "A man of kindness does good to his own soul" <note>Proverbs 11:17</note>—meaning that he is destined to be reincarnated according to the law of the "exchange vessel" during the withering of all; in the world, the name there is Kindness. 
The opposite of the belt is the stranger. The "wiping away of iniquity" will be through kindness and truth, as it is written: "Through kindness and truth iniquity is atoned for, and through the fear of the Lord one turns away from evil" <note>Proverbs 16:6</note>. 

The seven doubles correspond to atonement, as a matter of speech and as an opposite. It is known that all the judgments of the Name [God] are through the twelve Existences <term>Havayot</term> <note>The twelve possible permutations of the four-letter Name of God, Y-H-V-H</note> and through seven names, for in their hands are all judgments in the secret of "El, Elohim, and Y[HWH]." 
It is known that the Name was life and existed always from above to below—the living—and the Name from below. 
And [one] life was harder to take than that which was appointed for life, behold, for the Existence that was appointed for death. 
The second Existence is that which is appointed over Wealth. [The opposite is] that which was for the second, appointed over Humility <note>or "poverty"</note>. 
The third Existence is appointed over Wisdom. [The opposite is] that which was appointed over Folly. 
The fourth Existence is appointed over Grace <term>Chen</term>. [The opposite is] that which was appointed over Ugliness. 
And these are the opposite Existences: that which is in the Throne is over Fitness, and the sign is over Grace. 
They are appointed over Seed [offspring]; the seventh is appointed over Desolation. 
The sixth Existence is appointed over Dominion, and [its opposite] is appointed over Servitude.

And the philosophers who enter <note>perhaps referring to those who study the "inner" or esoteric sciences</note> are those who have [these] before them, and they say that the tenth Existence is for Dominion and the [opposite] for Servitude, and between the Shelters and Grace. 
And everything—Inanimate, Vegetative, Animate, and Speaking <note>The four traditional kingdoms of nature</note>, as well as the zodiac signs, the celestial spheres, the stars, and the high angels—all of them receive powers from the twelve Existences, "each man by his staff and each man by his banner according to their hosts" <note>Numbers 2:2</note>.

<meta>This page continues the discussion of mystical structures, moving from the philosophical "Opposites" to the practical application of divine Wisdom. ### Maimonides, of blessed memory; Chapters of the Mishnah 2

From the house, as it is said, and concerning the reversal of the loan to Pharaoh twice; for Wisdom was far from all beings, like the water that He lent us from the **Secret of the First Chariot** <term>Sod HaMerkavah</term> <note>The "Chariot" refers to the earliest form of Jewish mysticism focused on the vision of the divine throne described in Ezekiel</note> through the process of emanation. In the "Eye of Knowledge," wondrous secrets shall be revealed to him, for he is the **Holy Palace** which is the purpose of all existence. This is the secret of the Glory [Kavod] mentioned by the Great Rabbi, our Master Hai <note>Rabbi Hai Gaon (939–1038 CE), the last of the great Babylonian Geonim and an early authority on mystical matters</note>, of blessed memory. It says in *The Staff of Kotril* <note>original: "Matteh Kotril," likely a reference to a specific mystical treatise or a scribal variant of a known title</note>: The words of our Master Hai, of blessed memory, are founded upon wondrous secrets. In this proper manner, splendor is bestowed upon the spheres to provide insight through the "Eye of Knowledge," upon which the eyes depend, through the power of Him who "rides upon the heavens" <note>Psalm 68:33</note>.

And the scripture, when it distances itself from a snare so that it might prepare the choicest part from it, understands the action as if from blood that is cursed; it gazes into the light of the Intellect that burns over all. Toward Him, one shall be established and "hear the voice," because the hearing of an equal being is a **Separate Intellect** <term>Sekhel Nifrad</term> <note>A term in Medieval philosophy for an angelic or non-material consciousness</note> that guides all beings according to the rank of the upper worlds and the rank of the lower worlds. For this secret of humility, our Sages of blessed memory said in the Tractate of Words <note>likely referring to a midrashic collection</note>: "The soul resembles a flame," and that "man was first created with two faces" <note>original: "Du Partzufim," referring to the midrash that the first human was androgynous, having two faces joined together</note> regarding the part of the Supernal Soul and the part of the vital spirit. And when the Supernal Eye is in its proper form, it gazes with a final gaze into the secret of the **Illuminating Speculation** <note>original: "Speculatia Ha-Me'irah," a Hebrew-Latin hybrid term for a clear prophetic vision, often compared to a polished mirror</note>.

The later Sages of the Kabbalah established the way of this wisdom: **Rectification** <term>Tikkun</term>, **Permutation** <term>Tziruf</term> <note>The practice of re-arranging Hebrew letters to achieve meditative states</note>, and **Unification** [Yichud], as well as using numerical calculations [Gematria] to gain insight into hidden matters. This method, when performed well, illuminates the "Holy Eyes" like the **Urim and Thummim** <note>The oracular stones set in the breastplate of the High Priest used to inquire of God's will</note>. Therefore, by the power of the Great, Mighty, and Awesome God, who is called "Peace" [Shalom], one should write the **Inquiry of Peace** <term>She’elat Shalom</term> <note>A ritual petition, often performed before sleep or in a trance, to receive a divine answer to a specific question</note>.

**The Inquiry of Peace:** One day, a person should assist himself with water [immersion] and purify his heart from every evil thing. He should be upright, so that his "wings" [hands and intentions] are clean. One's thoughts and reflections and all his preparations should be ready; his hand shall take up the pen to write. He must honor the house and cleanse it of all impurity and any bad smell. It is necessary that he does not focus on any other matter except for the matter of his inquiry. He must ensure he does not have a seminal emission that night. After that one day passes, and another day of holiness and purity comes, he shall say on that day this verse three times forward and seven times backward:

*"Lord, all my desire is before You; and my sighing is not hidden from You"* <note>Psalm 38:10; original: "Adonai negdekha kol ta'avati ve-anchati mimmekha lo nistarah"</note>.

He must say it with great intention. After this, he shall say: *"Yahud, Yahud, Yahud <note>A variation of a Divine Name</note>, Who subdues the will of men, may it be Your will that You receive this inquiry of mine."* He shall say this three times. Afterward, he shall pray a prayer with great intention and say the **Ten Attributes** [Middot]. Following this, [he shall count] five, six, and a hundred "spread waters," and the time of holiness, as I have said, is like **Yom Kippur** itself. Indeed, call it "Yom Kippur" for three consecutive days for this investigation.

It is necessary to be mindful all those days that he fasts. Because on Yom Kippur it is forbidden to wash, he must immerse himself three times the day before. That immersion—sometimes replacing the [lack of] immersion on Yom Kippur—must be in the evening. The form of the immersion is as follows: perform three immersions. For on the day before Yom Kippur, he has already performed two immersions: one in the morning and one in the evening. On Yom Kippur, at the time of the **Ne'ilah** <note>The "Closing" service, the final and most solemn part of the Day of Atonement</note> prayer, and while saying the "Multitude of Holiness," he shall say:

"I am Your servant, praying before You, the Judge of all worlds, God of gods, King of kings, that You may fill with mercy the **Angel Appointed over the Inquiry** from Heaven, in whom is Your Name. May he send to me and to other angels who are appointed over every single inquiry: the eight [angels], and Shamriel, for the sake of the Holy God, the God who told me all this wisdom. May my inquiry and request be complete and true at every moment... Yah Yahud, by Your powers, hear me! Almighty God [El Shaddai], receive my prayer! Merciful and Gracious One, attend and hear..."

It cites Rav Hai Gaon and uses philosophical terminology to explain how human intellect can connect with the Divine Chariot.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the exploration of the "Holy Palace" as a mystical center, transitioning from the general emanation of Wisdom to the specific structure of the universe as defined in the Book of Formation (Sefer Yetzirah).</meta>

->### Ra’avad, of blessed memory &emsp; Chapter 4, Mishnah 2 &emsp; Maimonides, of blessed memory<-

"And the Shepherd of the world" <note>original: "Ve-Ro'eh Olam"</note>—that is to say, the power of the Blessed One who uplifts the entire world "underneath His arms" <note>A reference to Deuteronomy 33:27, "underneath are the everlasting arms," implying divine support of the universe</note>. Therefore, we designate their power through the **seven extremities** <term>Sheva Ketzavot</term> <note>In the Sefer Yetzirah, these are the six directions (North, South, East, West, Up, Down) plus the Holy Palace in the center</note> of space. Corresponding to them, this chapter begins with the foundations, lines, and voids; that which cuts, that which stands, and so on, concerning the Dominion. And this corresponds to the **seven double letters** <note>The Hebrew letters Bet, Gimel, Dalet, Kaf, Pe, Resh, Tav, which have two phonetic sounds and correspond to different dimensions in mystical thought</note>.

Our Master Hai <note>Rabbi Hai Gaon (939–1038 CE)</note>, of blessed memory, wrote: "He decided their traits," meaning He established the four directions of the winds, as well as Above and Below. The **Holy Palace** <term>Heichal HaKodesh</term> is the center; it is the "Land" where His glory resides. He is the "Place of the World" <note>A rabbinic idiom: God is not in the world, the world is in God</note>. Regarding the phrase "the whole earth is full of His glory," the masters of "Lines" and "Olives" <note>Likely referring to specific geometric or symbolic schools of interpretation</note> explain that the Glory of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His power and Presence <term>Shekhinah</term>, encompass everything like a conceptual circle. This is never repeated as a mere coincidence, but follows an orderly arrangement in the language of interpretation, proven by the linguistic roots.

<column-break/>

One cannot escape these ten extremities. However, the center of them all is the **Holy Palace**, which is aligned and directed toward everything in the heavens and the earth. It is directed as a dwelling place for the Lord from the Temple above. Our Sages, of blessed memory, said: In the Heavenly Temple, the archangel **Michael** serves as the High Priest and offers the souls of the righteous. The meaning of this is hidden in the verse: "When any man of you brings an offering to the Lord" <note>Leviticus 1:2</note>—meaning, the offering is "from you," from your very self. This Holy Palace is aligned at its source because it supports them all. This Mishnah reflects the tradition of the Sages that there are Above, Below, and the four winds, with the Palace in the middle. The Kabbalists <note>original: "Ha-Mekubalim"</note> said that the "Depths" mentioned here refer to the Sephirah of **Beauty** <term>Tiferet</term>.

<column-break/>

<margin>
The Name of
the Lord, the Lord
is the secret
of the 5 letters:
Y-H-V-H
Y-H-V-H
<unclear>...</unclear>
</margin>

He arranged it according to the connection of birth <note>Refers to the influence of astrology/constellations on human life</note>, where the end and the words of the lip and their surroundings are dependent on the higher realms. As the Sages taught: "There is no blade of grass below that does not have a constellation <term>Mazal</term> above that strikes it and says to it, 'Grow!'" As it is said, "the family of the stars" in their stations, one rank after another.

The **Perfect Man** <term>Ha-Adam Ha-Shalem</term>, through the secret of his internal composition and his great immersion in Wisdom, is capable of predicting the future. Because of his intense contemplation of the Way, he can focus his intent until he reaches the "Attribute of Mercy," searching through supreme secrets. These insights become for him like the **Urim and Thummim** <note>The oracular breastplate worn by the High Priest in the Bible</note>, for he is connected to the secret of the heavenly angels.

The soul clings to the Good, for the most noble of all created things is Man. This is why the form of the **Cherubim** <note>Angelic figures on the Ark of the Covenant</note> was human. Because the soul is higher than the physical, Moses directed his aim to be upright, for the noble part of him was drawn from the source. Man is like a **Microcosm** <term>Olam Katan</term>, and every "Cherub" is a vessel to receive higher power. When the soul is prepared to receive the Glory, and the body is refined, it is not cast away; the Divine guide leads the matter like a vessel of clay within us, for the Glory will receive the Glory.

Regarding the constellation of Israel: "There is no constellation for Israel" <note>A famous Talmudic debate (Shabbat 156a) on whether Jews are subject to astrology</note>, because the Glory of the Lord fills the whole world. Nevertheless, there are places where the power of the Supreme Governor is more visible than others. First, according to the nature of the recipient; second, according to the higher influence that pours sustenance upon the head of the recipient.

This is the secret of the "Doubling" <note>Refers to the 'double letters' mentioned earlier</note>, as our Sages taught: "The Torah preceded the world by two thousand years." According to the Great Secret of this Wisdom, the Torah is Wisdom <term>Chokhmah</term>, and Wisdom is the secret of all "Faces" <term>Partzufim</term>. Wisdom precedes the world of Angels and the lower world. This is the secret of "two thousand years"—meaning two types of celestial precedence: precedence of existence and precedence of rank. This is the secret of: "One: the Spirit of the Living God; Two: Spirit from Spirit" <note>Quotes from Sefer Yetzirah 1:9-10</note>. The word for "Two" <note>Shenayim</note> is related to the word for "teaching" <note>as in "I will teach you wisdom," Job 33:33</note>.

# Maimonides, Chapter 4, Mishnah 3
<meta>catchword: until</meta>

...to my prayer. And accept my supplication, for I have examined my heart before Your glory in the poverty of my soul to seek from You this completion; and may You forgive me, for the completion of knowledge and every illness within it, I have tasted with joy. And this shall be said three times with focused intention <term>kavanah</term> and in a state of repentance; and each time he says it, he shall stand with great fervor <note>original: "hama," literally heat/sun, implying feverish intensity</note>, in humility and in awe.

And every night that he desires to perform his spiritual remedy <term>segulah</term>, he shall write upon clean parchment <term>klaf</term>, according to what was established for the Holy Name and for purity, these Names. And at the time of writing, he shall not contemplate any worldly thing, even as much as writing "the Heavens" or "the Sea." And when you have finished the writing, it is customary [to invoke] three names and tasks from the Holy, Mighty, and Awesome God <note>original: "Kah-el Ha-Nachman Muphal Ke-Khol," a formulaic invocation of God's comforting and wondrous attributes</note>. And afterward, this writing will be in its full strength of the spiritual remedies <term>segulot</term>, and we shall engage the adjuration <term>hashba'ah</term> therein:

"I adjure you, holy and pure names—Kanas and Dor and Kalot—that you shall rest upon me, for I have found grace and have taken hold in this night, without distance of words. Do such and such, and teach it to me as it was written to be found, and it shall not depart from the world; and you shall remember with me all those who speak with their companions."

And this shall be said three times over the mystery of the seven directions. And when one engages the adjuration, sometimes a person might begin to falter and contemplate another matter; let his thoughts instead remain within the secret of this adjuration, and let his clothes be clean. And if he performs this for another person, he must mention the name of the one calling, whether in the Holy Tongue [Hebrew] or in a foreign tongue; in all other languages it does not need to change to perform the remedy. But if the night is burdensome to him, he will need to perform the remedy [again]. Also, he must not have slept with a woman during that entire week; he must wash and purify himself, and then his request will be granted in full. And the remedy <term>te'ulah</term> shall not fail.

Moses Kutiel <note>A likely late medieval or early modern figure associated with practical Kabbalah</note>, son of the Name [Shem], said: This spiritual remedy was like a dream that was subdued. Master Maimonides <term>Rambam</term> acted thus, and Nachmanides <term>Ramban</term> would perform with this, and our Master Saadia [Gaon] and our Master Hai [Gaon] would make use of it. So too did the Rabbi, our Master Yom Tov, and the Rabbi, our Master Jacob, and the Rabbi, our Master Baruch. And I received it from the mouth of our Rabbi, the great scholar who knows the wisdom of the Kabbalah, who corresponds to the one who composed it, and he is called among the Sages "Rabbi Isaac the Spaniard" <note>Rabbi Yitzhak HaSefardi, often identified with the circle of early Kabbalists in Spain</note>. 

And in every wisdom, he held his hand firm. They bequeathed to him the Crown of Torah and lit before him the Pure Menorah. He gave to us deep secrets. In this, I did not rely on confusion, for whoever does not know the secret of this wisdom—the secret of the "Philosophers" <note>original: "Palchusi," a corruption of "Philosophos"</note>—three in its light and the wisdom of the Talmud, it shall be to him a shame and a reproach. And every manner of prayer is nicknamed within the secret of this wisdom, which includes the Secret and the Foundation <term>Sod and Yesod</term>. Therefore, the life of the Kabbalist is above the collective.

And one must be careful and compassionate and diligent and sustained, so that he does not "cut the plantings" <note>A famous Talmudic metaphor for heresy or damaging the divine order through improper mystical practice</note>. For to Israel, it was not given to use [these names] except by way of the "Right Hand" <note>The side of Mercy and Holiness</note> whenever one seeks. And whoever uses them outside of the way we have stated, in a manner of a borrowed question, he shall be like it: he will go and be cursed. Many have sinned, overstepped, and trespassed against what they knew. Therefore, they were themselves hinted at in the damages, for the conditions of the Kabbalah are those of transmitters. 

Concerning this wisdom, it is said: *It is the glory of God to conceal a matter.* <note>Proverbs 25:2</note> For the things said in this wisdom are the "hidden things of the Merciful One" <note>original: "kivshei d'rachmana"</note>, and they shall be for him a foundation and a departure for the soul that guarded that which preceded and passed. And behold, the great Rabbi and Kabbalist, Rabbi Moses son of Nachman [Nachmanides], was very faithful in the study of this wisdom. And for the explanation he made in the *Book of the Pomegranate* <note>original: "Sefer HaRimon," a classic work of Kabbalah by Moses de Leon</note>, he gave this "Bell" <note>likely a metaphor for a resonant or clarifying insight</note>. And these are his words: 

"In a handful, so that you do not forget the intention of our Rabbis: Be careful, you student, when you prepare to make use of the glory of the Names, so that you do not fall to the ground—which is one of the foundations of the strength of understanding—and do not recoil. For against this, you will not be focused, and you will not be established in your intentions like a charging horse."

And this is [the meaning of] being appointed over slaves through the astrology of the stars. # The Ravad <note>Rabbi Abraham ben David, a 12th-century French commentator</note>, of blessed memory, Chapter 4, Mishnah 3 / The Ramban <note>Nachmanides, a 13th-century Spanish scholar and mystic</note>

And from there, the seven wandering stars <term>planets; original: kochevei lechet</term> receive [influence], and from them comes the power of strength and wealth throughout the seven days. From them, we receive the seven "gates" <note>referring to the seven openings in the human head</note> that are divided. How so? He made the letter *Beth* king over [the attribute of] Wisdom, and He tied a crown to it, and with it He formed **Saturn** <note>original: Shabbetai</note> in the universe, **Sunday** <note>original: Yom Rishon</note> in the week, and the **right eye** in the soul <note>meaning the person/body</note>. This means He elevated the powers to be expansive within the "Daughter of All" <note>a mystical term for a receptive divine sphere</note> and placed within it the power of Wisdom. He placed the planet Saturn beneath it to serve as its vessel, acting as a crown from the power of Wisdom to set it apart. While Saturn is a planet at the center of the zodiacal path, the power of Wisdom is [embedded] within it.

The reason Saturn is appointed over "destruction" is that it does not desire any matters of the physical body. Therefore, it brings things closer [to their end]; it is not provoked by anger or smallness, but rather focuses only on the pure intellects, the attainment of the Name (may He be blessed), and the comprehension of essential problems. From it comes the power that reaches the "circular princes" <note>likely referring to celestial intelligences or spheres</note>, and they mention the "protection" like wings. 

[Regarding] the "dregs of knowledge" <note>original: shimrei ha-da’at; refers to mundane or lower-level wisdom</note>: How can it be appointed over Wisdom and yet from it come these "dregs"? 
**Explanation:** The "dregs of knowledge" regarding worldly matters are lower in the soul. As our Sages (may their memory be a blessing) said: "Since the day the Temple was destroyed, prophecy was taken from the prophets and given to fools and children" <note>original: "minah she-charav beit ha-mikdash..." a reference to the Talmud, Tractate Bava Batra 12b</note>. This is why it is appointed over rest, life, burial grounds, praises, shame, and the ruins of this world, as well as every delay. Because Wisdom is in it, it is appointed over travels and hidden things, for its power is joined with the "Name of Life" which indicates the fullness of the zodiac. Because it acts in secret, it indicates all hidden things like lands and buried treasures. And because it is the seventh, following all other stars, it indicates the end of all things and the elderly. Because it is appointed over wisdoms and thoughts, it is appointed over the "Foundation" <term>Yesod; the ninth Sephirah or divine emanation</term>, and therefore it was placed in the creation of the foundation of the world.
<meta>catchword: And because</meta>

<column-break/>

And there, in the "twenty-two" <note>the 22 letters of the Hebrew alphabet</note>, they were divided regarding worldly matters. He placed the planets to perform His work in this lower world through seven gates in the year <note>referring to time/cycles</note>, six for the days of the week, and everything is fixed by the zodiac. 

There are seven "gates" in the soul <note>the human being</note>: the three upper ones and the others—two eyes, two ears, two nostrils, and a mouth. It is said in the Midrash: The attribute of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is not like the attribute of flesh and blood. If a human makes a vessel and pierces it, whether for water or wine, and checks it, everything will leak out. But the Holy One, Blessed be He, is not so. He created man with many orifices and holes, yet what is inside is preserved. Even though the body is pierced, the life remains within. Thus, it says: "He who acts wondrously" <note>original: Maphli La'asot; part of the Asher Yatzar blessing recited after using the bathroom, thanking God for the biological function of the body</note>.

Regarding the nature of lands: The sage Ptolemy <note>original: Talmai</note> divided the inhabited world into seven climates <term>aklimim; geographical zones</term>. In every climate, the air changes. The Land of Israel is the "Gate of the Climates," and Jerusalem is in the fourth climate <note>the central, most balanced zone</note>. Of it, it is said: "Beautiful in elevation, the joy of the entire earth" <note>Psalm 48:3</note>, meaning Jerusalem is the "beautiful elevation" <term>Nof; can mean view, elevation, or province</term>. "Nof," "Aklim," "Pelekh," and "Machoz" are all the same thing <note>they all mean region or province</note>. The Creator (blessed be He) divided His world into seven parts called seven provinces, or seven climates, or seven "Nofot." Every province's air differs from the others. Therefore, one who comes from the province of their birth and enters another province will fall ill, for this is a change from all the qualities of the air to which their nature was tempered. 

Jerusalem is the most praised "Nof" in language, for it was the most beautiful of provinces. Therefore, anyone who comes there from other climates will be enticed by the change in its spirit. This is why our Sages (may their memory be a blessing) said: "The air of the Land of Israel makes one wise" <note>original: Avira d'Eretz Yisrael Machkim; a famous Talmudic adage from Bava Batra 158b</note>. That is to say, the air of the Land of Israel is purer than all other air for the hearts, as it is located in the center of the inhabited world. Therefore, one who dwells in this place is naturally prepared for the power of spiritual perfection. And one who is prepared in such a way of perfection...

### The Ravad <note>Rabbi Abraham ben David, a 12th-century legalist and mystic</note>, of blessed memory, Chapter 4, Mishnah 3

And these—the Crown and the blue pigments <note>possibly referring to cosmetic or ritual dyes</note> etc. — relate to dreams. Its sicknesses will heat up those who suffer from madness through the power of the "conjunction of knowledge." To it belongs the "double" <note>referring to the "double" letters of the Hebrew alphabet</note> from a high place, and it governs the heart, fruitfulness, the madness of the thread <note>unclear; possibly a medical or weaving metaphor</note>, and the place and the grinding of the tooth—therefore their reading is like unripe fruit <note>original: *pagi*; referring to a specific phonetic quality</note>. To it belong violence and robbery, the lion, the scorpion, wild beasts, and a medicinal mixture [described as] dogs crying as they go, and garments for learning. To it belong the cooling places.

**He made the letter *Beth* king**, and He tied a crown to it, and with it He formed the **Sun** <note>original: *Hamah*</note> in the universe, the **fourth day** of the week, and the **spleen** in the soul. To it belong (in the Prayer) <note>abbreviated as *Taf*</note> Glory, and (in the Crown) Sovereignty and the Unity of the Name, inscribed in writing and in vocalization. It indicates the hidden Torah and the service of kings, for the Sun serves the [Divine] Throne. It governs the recognition of those who possess loving-kindness and piety—and this is hidden. It also indicates natural wisdom, inscribed from another [source], for it is an acquisition of Loving-kindness. It indicates wealth from the "right side"—silver, and from his compassion, gold, and success; every kindness he shares, the Lord makes it prosper in his hand. To it belongs the booth <note>or covering</note> from the side of Strength <term>Gevurah</term>, and many helpers from the side of Unity. Its "sickness" is that all the surplus of silver and gold will reach them, and all that he inherited from their ancestors, etc. Every person of stature, such as the wise men of the Council of Justice and the scholars of the Ephod <note>priestly vestment</note>. And because he receives from Strength, he will rejoice over harm, and [troubles] will reach the humble, though they are not from the princes. Because he "clothes" between Loving-kindness and Mercy, he therefore tells of peace from the side of good and cut-off things. And the Sun is a good star from another [perspective]. One should know that for anyone who has water, it is bad <note>an astrological warning regarding the Sun's heat and water</note>, for all the creatures of the earth (in the Prayer) have no existence without water alone. He humbles the sinners through the power of Strength; his hand is on the neck of his enemies and those who plan his harm. He awakens the sending of servants to search for the secret of the Sabbatical year <term>Shemitah</term>, and regarding the rest of the missing [person] from the house of the Caesar, just like an exchange. So too those who sit in the furnace will be remembered from their labor, for the shield of the Lord is a protection over them, and the secret of [Divine] will is with mankind, and he shall find grace in the eyes of God and man. He awakens toward rest and generosity etc., and the sick are healed, for he is the mediator between hot and moist, and cold and dry.

**He made the letter *Pe* king**, and He tied a crown to it, and with it He formed **Venus** <note>original: *Nogah*, meaning "Brightness"</note> in the universe, through the power of the firmament, the **fifth day** of the week, and the **right nostril** <note>original: *kehol yamin*</note> in the soul. Therein lies the power of retribution and the "time-pairing" of every belly <note>possibly referring to pregnancy or digestion</note>, and the time of beauty and the danger of the "smallness" as it is written: "and the women will be sought out." And He wrote regarding sins: "in your days... with strength." Peace is in the chamber from the power of Harmony <term>Tiferet</term>, the power of his exchange. He has helpers from the side of Loving-kindness and those who seize from the side of Harmony, and those who seek his good. To him belongs strength among women (in the Crown), and the parts [of the body], and he desires the tools of the flute and the pipes, and the exchanges <note>or "dreams"</note>, and jewelry, and gardens, and orchards, and all kinds of delights. He indicates rest and powers from the side of Loving-kindness toward the Diadem <term>Atarah; another name for the Sephirah of Malchut</term>, and the peace of the "exchanges" <note>or "dreams"</note>, for he is the comforter. He is sweet because he receives from the side of Strength, from the "head of the thread" that is purchased with silver. Therefore, he awakens regarding the [embroidery] work, and silk, and embroidery, and all types of luxury and every pleasure.

# The Ravad, of blessed memory — Chapter 4 — Mishnah 2

And the scribes are like few and like a memory <note>original: "k'dikhur"; the meaning is slightly obscure, possibly referring to the preservation of records</note>. And the Runner <note>original: "Rahiton," a name for the planet Mercury, emphasizing its rapid orbit</note> indicates the planet [Mercury]; it indicates the intellect and every pure thing, as well as the black bile <term>the "melancholy" humor in medieval medicine</term>, and the sages of silence, mathematics, and worldly knowledge, and the signs of excision <term>karet; a spiritual penalty of being "cut off"</term>, and assets, special properties, and much more. It also indicates one who turns to investigate a matter—whose speech is established and grows, who speaks deeply, acts shrewdly, and is both near and far—and evil movements. All of this is according to its path [through the heavens]. Its influence is refined only for the higher intellects, and therefore it indicates the depths of thoughts and wisdoms. And the general rule is: any craft that you think to do in "black" <note>possibly referring to ink/writing or the humor of melancholy</note>, such as writing, sometimes it will proceed, sometimes it will stand still, and sometimes it is better to leave it lacking. So too with movements: sometimes they are hot, and sometimes it is good to investigate and cool down, and similar things; it [Mercury] is appointed over them. And because it is appointed over persistence, therefore, when it reaches its height, it shall never descend, as it is said, "And He placed upon him a spirit of wisdom and understanding" <note>referring to the divine inspiration that stabilizes the mind</note>. And this is the secret of the Anointed of the Lord <note>the Messiah</note>. Its relationship is shared by everyone and for everything, and this is the secret of its acquisition. Therefore, it has two types of actions: when it clings to the higher realms, it improves the destruction below; and when it clings to the lower realms, it causes hardships in diverse matters. Therefore, all the ascent of Israel is only through the commandments that draw down the power of blessing. For this reason, your enemies possess chariots, spears, and weapons of war, for "Not by sword nor by spear does the Lord save" (Understanding). When they [Israel] withdraw from the commandments, the blessing immediately withdraws from them and they descend to the lowest point of descent—and this is the secret of "If you walk in My statutes" and the secret of all the [Biblical] admonitions.

He made the letter **Gimmel** king, and tied a crown to it, and formed with it **Jupiter** <term>Tzedek; literally "Righteousness"</term> in the universe, the **second day** of the week <note>Monday</note>, and the **left eye** in the soul. That is to say, He elevated the letter Gimmel to be a heart for it, as a strength for its depth. And the secret of "For now he shall reign" comes from the power of Loving-kindness <term>Chesed; the divine attribute of expansive benevolence</term>; for this reason, it [Jupiter] rules over kindness, uprightness, justice, humility, good deeds, and a good spirit. It is the master of the fortune of kindness, the sages of the Name, every cantor, and the wisdom of the Torah which is called "Kindness," and the performing of kindness below. It rules over merchants in the law of exchange, buying and selling, giving and lending with all justice and profit, and wealth—for the silver is His—and the good hope of kindness, and the [ethical] qualities, and similar things. It also indicates pregnancy through the power of the fortune of the celestial sphere, and the males who procreate, for they are the procreative entries. It is the secret of peace, tranquility, and security from all fear. It assists with money and with the strengthening of the incoming power and good glass <note>possibly "crystals" or "clarity"</note>. It is written "all," for it is the prayer of the Covenant, the general rules of royalty, and the service of the King of kings of kings, the "Open-Eyed One"—meaning Understanding <term>Binah</term>—and it sends forth grace and kindness, and pleads with uprightness, and leans toward the side of kindness. It opens the windows and the blessing of the land (79) and an abundance of grain, and peace in the city. It oversees partners and peaceful worship, for it is the healer of the sick and the peace of the "sent ones" <note>likely messengers or travelers</note> and the dangers in the law of exchange, and the path of the house of ethics through kindness and good intercessors, and over the kings of life and the righteous judges. In appearance, it is seen as a propitious omen, for it has the appearance of a white sapphire and the leadership of every desire. To it belong the honorable garments, facial perfumes, and the gatherings in synagogues and the seat of the pious, and prayers and supplications, and the honorable Temples for the service of God. It testifies to the essence of youth as well as old age <note>original: "wheat," likely a scribal error for "old age" or "maturity"</note>, and it testifies to the higher parts of the kingdom and its adornments.

He made the letter **Dalet** king, and tied a crown to it, and formed with it **Mars** <term>Ma'adim; literally "The Red One"</term> in the universe, the **third day** of the week <note>Tuesday</note>, and the **right eye** in the soul. It indicates hardness of heart, stiff-neckedness, and cruelty, and over violence, anger, rages, and wars—for such are the judgments of Might <term>Gevurah; the divine attribute of restraint and severity</term>. It rules over the rebellion of rebels and those who shed the blood of every living creature and blood itself. Every craft in which [cutting/blood] occurs is attributed to it, for it is the "Greatness" <note>possibly used ironically or referring to its vast influence over physical force</note>. To it belong the butcher and the surgeons <note>original: "panpim," likely referring to those who perform bloodletting or cupping</note> who strike, and every sharp thing. It is over the cancellation of meetings and the hindering of those who would partner with Understanding. To it belong all types of fear, and it possesses the destruction and the house of capture <note>or prison/confinement</note>. And to it...

# The Ravad, of blessed memory — Chapter 4 — Mishnah 3

And to him belong the crown, the blood, and destruction, and a species of sharpness <note>original: *hidush*; likely referring to a sharp or innovative spirit</note> that awakens from the side of Judgment <term>Din; the divine attribute of severity and justice</term> over strength, the innocent, and the blood of virgins. To him belong slaughter and folly.

And before him is Kindness <term>Hesed</term>; it is the soul, and its temperament is balanced upon Kindness. To him belongs the natural disposition, and he indicates the flyers <note>original: *metisim*; likely birds or spiritual messengers</note> from the side of pleasant aromas, and the spirits of the sun <note>original: *haris*; likely *heres*, a poetic name for the sun</note> and mishaps. To him belong the strings [of the lyre], for they are within his power.

To him belong the sorcery <note>original: *hakos*; likely *hakosem*, the magician</note> and those who deny the law from the side of the columns of smoke. Therefore, their direction is the North, as well as war, the furnace, the oven, the scorpion, and wild beasts. He is the burden of the nursing of barking and wandering dogs, and of dreamt clothes. To him belong drinks made of almonds.

# Yad Avraham, of blessed memory — Chapter 4 — Mishnah 3

...as a type of the few and as the honor. And they shall be a teacher regarding the star; a teacher regarding **Saturn** <note>original: *Shabbetai*</note> and regarding every black thing, and regarding the black bile <term>melancholy; one of the four humors of ancient medicine</term>, and regarding the sages of silence, and darkness, gloom, and thick darkness. And it rules over the master-builders, and over possessions and treasures, and over repentance. It rules over one who tends toward wanting for something yet his life is sustained, and over destruction, the desert, desolation, forests, coldness, and parting, and bad rumors. 

All of this is because he <note>Saturn</note> does not direct his providence except toward the ultimate purpose that is above him. Therefore, he indicates the depths of thoughts and wisdoms. The general rule is: any craft that occasionally returns to "blackness," such as laundering—which sometimes moves and sometimes stands still, and sometimes returns to the blackness <note>soiling</note>—and likewise sewing—which sometimes unstitches and sometimes returns to sewing—and the gravedigger and those similar to these, he is appointed over them. 

And because he is appointed over persistence, therefore when he touches upon a person, he gives him an eternal yoke, as it is said: "And the spirit of wisdom and understanding shall rest upon him" <note>Isaiah 11:2</note>. And being that your reversal is shared by everything, and the joints and the end of the extremities, therefore there are within him types of actions. At the time when he attaches to the upper realms, everything below is destruction; but at the time when he attaches to the name of the extremities, the end of matters is renewed. Therefore, all matters of Israel are only like "blows" <note>trials</note> when drawing down the power of **Understanding** <term>Binah; the third Sephirah, often associated with Saturn in this system</term>. 

Therefore, your vessels are vessels of the sword, the spear, and the weapons of war, for "not by sword nor by spear does He save" <note>1 Samuel 17:47</note>, but by **Understanding** <note>original: *Binah*</note>. And at the time they distance themselves from the "blows," immediately Understanding departs from them and they descend to the lowest depth. This is the secret of "If you walk in my statutes" <note>Leviticus 26:3</note> and the secret of all the Admonitions.

He made the letter **Bet** king, and bound a crown to it, and formed through it **Jupiter** <note>original: *Tzedek*</note> in the world, and the second day of the week <note>Monday</note>, and the left eye in the soul. For the world has three dimensions: breadth, length, and depth. They rule from the power of **Kindness** <term>Hesed; the fourth Sephirah</term>. And he <note>Jupiter</note> is appointed over kindness, integrity, justice, humility, good deeds, a good name, and he is a "Master of Judgment" through kindness. He rules the sages of the Name, and insight, and the wisdom of the Torah, as it is said: "and the Torah of kindness is on her tongue" <note>Proverbs 31:26</note>. 

He rules over commerce with the law of the "children of exchange" <note>merchants</note>, and buying and selling, and giving and taking with all righteousness, and profit and wealth—for "to Him is the silver"—and a good hope of kindness. He indicates profit through the power of the secret of reincarnation <note>original: *gilgul*</note> and the royal gatherings, for they are the gatherings of the messengers. To him belong peace, tranquility, and security from all fear, and he helps through his kindness. He is the author of the merit of the righteous. It is written of him that he is the "beginning of creation" <note>referring to Jupiter's benevolent influence</note> and the vessel of kingship and the service of the King of kings, the Holy One, Blessed be He. For **Insight** and **Kingship** are there, and **Kindness** is most prevalent. He inclines toward the side of kindness and opens powers and the blessing of the land, and the abundance of produce, and peace in the city. 

He cuts off the accusers and is the healer of the sick—for He is the "Healer of the sick"—and the peace of the pious and the small ones. He rules over the "children of exchange" and the writing from the house of the scribe through kindness and good intercessors. He rules over the "Living Kings" <note>referring to the *Chayot*, a high order of angels</note> and the righteous judges in their generation, for he is like the appearance of a sapphire stone, and the leadership of every desire. To him belong the heavy fats <note>in anatomy</note> and the brightness of the face, and the spleen, and the synagogues and the seat of piety, and prayers and supplications, and the houses of thought for the sake of the Name. He rouses the fundamental principle in the choice ones and also in the small, and he testifies to the heights of the Kingdom.

He made the letter **Dalet** king, and bound a crown to it, and formed through it **Mars** <note>original: *Ma'adim*</note> in the world, and the third day of the week <note>Tuesday</note>, and the right ear in the soul. And he indicates the heat of the heart and the stiff-necked, and piety <note>likely used ironically here for zealotry</note>, and violence, anger, shouting, and wars—for such are the judgments of **Strength** <term>Gevurah; the fifth Sephirah, associated with Mars</term>. 

He rules over the fruit of the ground, the shedders of blood—both the blood of beasts and the blood of man—and every craft lacking strength in their sustenance is his, for he is "The Great." To him belong gold and pearls like coals, and every red thing. He rules over the cancellation of desires and the abandoning of those who partner with **Understanding** <note>Binah</note>. To him belong all types of fear, and to him belong dangers, and the latrine <note>representing the waste of the body or the "Other Side"</note>. And to him...

And when you search in the *Makler* <note>original: *Makler*; likely referring to a specific compilation or a corruption of the word *Mikhlol* (Collection)</note> you will find for each and every one verses from the Torah. These are the six "Headings of Wisdom," and they should be constantly before your eyes, for through them every future event is known. Through them, the Creator and my Lord—may He be blessed and exalted—formed [the world].

There are Seven Doubles <term>Hebrew letters that have two pronunciations: Bet, Gimel, Dalet, Kaf, Peh, Resh, Tav</term> corresponding to the mnemonic *K-P-R-T N-D*. Through them are seven heavens, seven stars <note>planets</note>, seven swords <note>original: *charvot*; likely a scribal variant for 'Sabbaths' (*shabbatot*) or 'heavens' (*aravot*)</note>, seven hours, seven days, seven sanctities, seven knives <note>original: *shakin*; possibly meaning 'dwellings'</note>, seven Sabbatical years, the holy Jubilee, and seven gates in the soul: Life, Peace, Wisdom, Grace, Wealth, Progeny, and Dominion. Therefore, He favored the seventh—the Foundation <note>original: *Yesod*, the ninth Sefirah/emanation</note>—under all the heavens.

# Commentary on Sefer Yetzirah | Chapter 4, Mishnah 4

[The text] recounts how the Holy One refined all the letters; they are twenty-two [formed] in a single utterance, something which the tongue cannot speak nor the ear hear. And the Holy One gave a crown to each letter of the seven doubles <note>original: "שבע כפולות"; the letters Bet, Gimel, Dalet, Kaph, Pe, Resh, Tav, which in some traditions each have two distinct pronunciations</note> just as He did with the three names <note>Refers to the three "Mother" letters: Aleph, Mem, and Shin</note>. 

He gave dominion to **Bet**, and likewise to **Gimel**, **Dalet**, **Kaph**, **Pe**, **Resh**, and **Tav**. For these seven are "servants" <note>The seven classical planets</note> that serve throughout the day and night. Each one of them [rules for] one hour, and they rotate in a cycle forever. 

The [ruling planets at the] beginning of the nights follow the mnemonic **B-B-L-H Q-L-H** <note>These letters represent the order of the planets ruling the start of each night of the week</note>. And the beginning of the days follow **B-B-N-H**. 

How so? On the first night <note>Saturday night in the Jewish calendar</note>, the first hour is ruled by **Mercury** <note>original: "כוכב" - Kokhav</note>, the second by the **Moon** <note>original: "לבנה" - Levanah</note>, the third by **Saturn** <note>original: "שבתי" - Shabbatai</note>, the fourth by **Jupiter** <note>original: "צדק" - Tzedek</note>, the fifth by **Mars** <note>original: "מאדים" - Ma’adim</note>, the sixth by the **Sun** <note>original: "חמה" - Hammah</note>, and the seventh by **Venus** <note>original: "נוגה" - Nogah</note>. The eighth hour returns to Mercury, the ninth to the Moon, the tenth to Saturn, the eleventh to Jupiter, and the twelfth to Mars. This entire order is explained in the books of astronomy <term>Hittakhuna: The science of the spheres and calculations of the heavens</term>. 

This was intended to "send" <note>A wordplay on the name of the book or the author's intent</note> a means to bind the lower world to the chain of the upper world, to say that all is one; for the Arranger is the Simple One, in the ultimate sense of simplicity.

And our Rabbi explained, of blessed memory, that the author of *Sefer Yetzirah* wrote: "Two stones build two houses" <note>The text here mirrors the mathematical logic of the Sefer Yetzirah: a "stone" is a single letter, and a "house" is a word/permutation. Two letters can form two distinct words (AB, BA)</note>. He took "stones" as a metaphor, just as it says "The Shepherd, the Stone of Israel" <note>Genesis 49:24</note>, where "Stone" refers to the head of Israel. Similarly, we find "stone" used in the language of greatness, as in "the holy stones are poured out" <note>Lamentations 4:1</note>, referring to the great and small among the seven [planets]. It is also said: "In the midst of the stones of fire you walked" <note>Ezekiel 28:14</note>. 

The other angels are as it is said: "His ministers are a flaming fire" <note>Psalms 104:4</note>. Regarding the "holy stones," as the translation of Jonathan ben Uzziel <note>An ancient Aramaic translation/paraphrase of the Prophets</note> renders it: "the holy people." Israel was given the Torah which was fire, as it is said: "From His right hand a fiery law for them" <note>Deuteronomy 33:2</note>. And the Sages are precious ones, like shining and illuminating pearls. 

The letters are very weighty matters in their form and their writing, as explained in the *Book of the Reed* <term>Sefer ha-Kanah: A 14th-century kabbalistic work on the secrets of the commandments and Hebrew alphabet</term>. "Houses" refers to the matter of wisdom, as in "By wisdom a house is built" <note>Proverbs 24:3</note>. It is also said, "In all my house, he is faithful" <note>Numbers 12:7</note>, and "I have surely built a house of habitation for You" <note>1 Kings 8:13</note>. 

The author of *Sefer Yetzirah* said: "Two stones build two houses." The letters are the "stones" and their structure forms "houses." The secret of "two stones" relates to the secret of the beginning <note>original: "בראשית" - Bereshit</note>, as we say in *Bereshit Rabbah* <term>A collection of ancient homilies (Midrash) on the Book of Genesis</term>: Why does the Torah begin with the letter **Bet** [which has the numerical value of 2]? To inform you that there are two worlds: this world and the World to Come. 

Some say: Why a **Bet**? Because it is the language of "Blessing" <note>original: "ברכה" - Berakhah</note> and not an **Aleph**, which is the language of "Cursed" <note>original: "ארור" - Arur</note>. Others say: Why not an **Aleph**? So as not to give an opening to the heretics to say, "How can the world stand if it was created with the language of cursing?" Rather, the Holy One, blessed be He, said: "I am creating them with the language of blessing; if only it will stand!" 

Others say: Why a **Bet**? Because the **Bet** has two points <note>original: "עוקצין" - thorns or serifs</note>, one pointing upward and one pointing downward (and toward the back). One says to the other: "Who created you?" and it points with its back-serif to the Creator and says, "The Lord is His name!" 

All of this mentioned in *Bereshit Rabbah* contains a great and wondrous secret. Therefore, the *Sefer Yetzirah* wrote: "Two stones" like the name **YH-YH** <note>The letters of the Divine Name</note> which rolls forward and backward. "Three stones build six houses" <note>3! = 3x2x1 = 6 permutations</note>, such as the name **Y-H-V**, which rolls and flips into six houses; and so it is for all of them. 

Everything our Rabbi explained in this chapter was to teach us how the secret of combination <term>Tziruf: The mystical practice of permuting Hebrew letters to achieve meditative states or understand the structure of reality</term> is built within this wisdom. May the Merciful One, may He be blessed, assist us through every distress. This concludes the order, with the help of God, [written in] verse: "His word rose to hang upon it, built up."

->The Chapter is Finished<-

It explains the Kabbalistic reason why the Torah begins with the letter Bet, emphasizing themes of blessing and the connection between the physical and spiritual realms.</summary>

# The Ravad <note>Rabbi Abraham ben David, a 12th-century legalist and kabbalist</note>, of Blessed Memory | Chapter 4, Mishnah 4

The secret of the nesting of the firmaments <note>The seven layers of heaven</note>: four in the void of the seven doubles <note>The seven "double" letters of the Hebrew alphabet</note>, just as it was done with the measure of fifty cubits. So, when the Creator (may He be exalted) desired to create each individual firmament within the cycle of the secret of the seven doubles and also the seven days. All of this is to hint that the world is held in a small knot within the glory of the **Shekhinah** <note>The Divine Presence on earth</note>. 

And this is the verse written by the Master of Kabbalah in the *Sefer ha-Temunah* <note>original: "ספר התמונות" - The Book of the Image, a 13th-century mystical text</note>, and these are his words: "The glory of the Shekhinah," meaning the verse: *In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth* <note>Genesis 1:1</note>. Behold, there are sixteen edges, and the Holy Palace is aligned in their center; all of them are seven firmaments and seven earths. *And God spoke all these words, saying...* <note>Exodus 20:1</note>. 

This is the secret of the sages' statement (of blessed memory): "If not for the Torah, heaven and earth would not endure." For the Torah tells of "spirit from spirit," and by the powers of the Torah, the world was created. If so, it corresponds to **K-P-R-T** <note>The mnemonic for the letters Kaph, Pe, Resh, and Tav, representing the seven double letters</note> against the seven firmaments. Behold, the verse *In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth* contains **Power** <note>original: "כח" (Koach). The word Koach has a numerical value of 28; the first verse of Genesis contains 28 Hebrew letters</note>. 

This is the meaning of: *He has declared to His people the power of His works, in giving them the heritage of the nations* <note>Psalm 111:6</note>. Likewise, in the verse *And God spoke all these words, saying*, there is **Power** <note>This verse also contains 28 letters</note>. Therefore, "Power" (28) and "Power" (28) together [are significant]. This is the secret that returned to the reason of the "Seven Days." The pure soul is placed upon the diagonal, resting with the holy angel named **Sandalphon** <note>An archangel in Jewish mysticism who weaves crowns for God from the prayers of Israel</note>. He ties for [the soul] a knot of **Hesed** <note>Loving-kindness</note>, and it is called a "treasured people," and he oversees the attribute of *And [the heavens and earth] were finished* <note>Genesis 2:1</note>. 

Therefore, our sages said: "It is a night of vigils unto the Lord" <note>Exodus 12:42</note>, a night protected and entirely free from damaging spirits. To hint at this wonderful secret, our sages said: "He who opens these, opens the seven-fold [blessings]." Why did the sages institute seven blessings <note>The Sheva Berachot recited at weddings</note> and the writing of the "summary of the seven" <note>The condensed version of the Amidah prayer</note>? And the secret of the seven circumambulations <note>The practice of walking around the altar or a groom seven times</note>? Even though God gave a portion to the seven [nations] besides Israel—these are the words of the Master of Kabbalah in the *Sefer ha-Temunah*.

All these wonderful powers are within the Holy Torah, meaning *In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth*. All this is to enlighten man, to know the powers of wisdom—the power of the Blessed One—and how the permutation of letters is drawn forth. Therefore, man is called a **microcosm** <note>original: "עולם קטן" - a small world</note> in its image. Through man's knowledge of himself, he knows his Creator and His glory, from the greatest to the smallest of them. Whoever knows how to direct his mind to the secret of "opening the total opening" will be saved from all evil and will be above the celestial constellations. 

Behold, our sages said: "The hidden treasures of the righteous are greater than those who lick the incense." Blessed be the Name of Him who spoke and the world came into being. In six days He formed all His offspring and his ladder. He spread out His world and formed man in His image; He created him in the likeness of the world which He created at first, so that he might be in the lower world to come and to go. With the secret of the matter corresponding to **K-P-R-T** <note>Kaph, Pe, Resh, Tav</note>, He made a covenant. And this was my entire intention: "Establish witnesses as mercy for my unity"—these are the words of the Rabbi, **Isaac of Akko** <note>A 13th-14th century Kabbalist and student of Nahmanides</note>.

And our teacher **Meir of Rothenburg** <note>A major 13th-century German Rabbi (Maharam)</note> wrote as follows: "**Two stones build** [two houses]." A "stone" is a term for a request, as in *And this stone* <note>Genesis 28:22</note>. He used the term "stone" in the way our Teacher said regarding the Torah: *From there, the Shepherd of the Stone of Israel* <note>Genesis 49:24</note>. It refers to all of Israel, just as a stone is a single body. 

The beginning of all the letter permutations are from "two stones." Furthermore, on the day of permutation, he called "two stones" the foundations of the building, for the stone is the foundation of the building. Therefore it says, *From there, the Shepherd of the Stone of Israel*. He called the letter a "stone," and two letters are "two stones." One word is called "two stones," and from this you can [calculate] for three letters and upward—crowns and pathways. May the Merciful One, in His kindness, grant him merit to enter... you can reverse and rotate [the letters] in the *Sefer ha-Gilgul* <note>The Book of Rotation/Cycles</note>. For example: **H-N** (*Chen* - Grace); **N-H** (*Noach* - Rest); **K-H** (*Koach* - Power). Thus all these stones build "houses" for seven or eight words, like the table and the word which is the joined word... as it says, *this is the opening of my mouth*, you can reverse and rotate them at will...

This is not by necessity of his own power, but rather because he is more adapted to it; he is the "Kallah" <note>Bride/Completion</note> of the forces produced from the First Cause. 

In our explanation of our intent, it is explained that the Kabbalists called the Second Sefirah <note>Divine emanation</note> by the name Metatron, who is the Name below, just as the Tetragrammaton is the Name above. We understand from the Midrashic telling that this is Metatron, who called himself "The Prince who appears as a newborn child." He wrote this word in the likeness of a crown... <note>The text here becomes highly elliptical, discussing the mystical associations of the "Youth" (Na'ar), a common title for Metatron</note>. They are not to be understood literally, but only as a metaphor for the Cause of Causes, for they are the measure of these descriptions. # The Ramban <note>Rabbi Moses ben Nahman, 13th-century scholar</note>, of Blessed Memory | Chapter 5, Mishnah 2

It is their way to speak of the "thickened" <note>original: *machmar* - likely referring to a grammatical state or doubling of sounds</note> letters somewhat differently than the simple way; doubled letters which were not created for him in the speech, but in his "dark places" <note>Psalm 88:7</note> at the end. One who understands the workings of the *Book of Grammar* mentioned by the Rabbi, Master Chavivai <note>An early medieval grammarian whose works are mostly lost</note>, of blessed memory, will understand this. And behold, there is a great secret in establishing the ten simple [letters] <note>The text says "ten," but the context of the chapter implies twelve</note> as derived from the Master of the *Book of Commentary*:

Sight—read as "for nothing" <note>original: *keri be-chinam*—a technical grammatical or mnemonic term used by Rabbi Chavivai</note>; Hearing—read as "for nothing"; Smell—read as "for nothing"; Speech—read as "for nothing"; Chewing—read as "for nothing"; Sexual union—read as "for nothing." And so with all of them. "Chewing" is a term for eating, as they said of one who "fed the mallows" <note>A reference to the Talmudic story of King Yannai</note>, and it comes from the expression "Let me swallow" <note>Genesis 25:30</note>, which refers to the manner of eating. "Sexual union" refers to the sensation of the act experienced by a person.

And this is the meaning of the "vision of the breast" <note>original: *hazeh hamfur*—likely a mystical anatomical term</note> mentioned; it increases within a man when he uses it in the way of a rooster <note>A rabbinic metaphor for frequent sexual activity</note>, for without this, it would be impossible to "thicken" it, as "He did not create it to be a waste, but formed it to be inhabited" <note>Isaiah 45:18</note>. So it is with the secret of the entire Twelve. Therefore, the foundation is from the "flesh of distorted things."

And as for "Reading," our Sages of blessed memory said: "Do not read *wasas* but *weses*," <note>An "Al Tikre" wordplay. The OCR here is slightly corrupted, but it refers to the regulation of cycles or measures</note> which relates to the matter of weight and balance. All this is from the Rabbi, Master Chavivai, in the book called *This is the Gate to the Lord*.

"Twelve diagonal boundaries": The entire world has six directions <note>North, South, East, West, Up, and Down</note>. Every corner has two diagonals. Since the world is like a square, it has twelve expanding diagonals that go out to the edge of the world. These diagonals expand the world so it may be bound together and not expand further than is proper for it. These are the "arms of the world" <note>Deuteronomy 33:27</note>.
