# Our Rabbi Saadia Gaon, of blessed memory

The book is for the benefit of the blessings upon the Place <note>original: 'המקום' (HaMakom), a common rabbinic name for God, emphasizing His omnipresence.</note> from Him, and heaven forbid [it is used] for evil from our knowledge, for there is no evil from our knowledge. 

Twenty-two foundation letters, the foundation of the world: He engraved them through the mouth, ten by ten, in the form of their writing. And He wrote them as the <unclear>dwellings</unclear> of letters and gave them reason, as it is found in the chapter "One who brings a jar." He placed their flavor/meaning in them, and their balance, and their <term>notarikon</term> <note>A system of shorthand or acrostics where letters represent whole words.</note>. 

The letters **He (ה)** and **Qof (ק)**: The writing is like a horse to a pit <note>A metaphor for the structure or "gaping" shape of these letters.</note> and its recognition—meaning the *notarikon*—is "the vanity of the divisions of his mouth." His <term>notarikon</term> is "Let the living radiance prove from the mouth." It is made since the top of the upper part is open and the end of the leg of the right side, and its left leg is like a force to the right leg, in the manner of an **N (ן)** like this: **ז**. Therefore, it serves for problems, to recognize... ten in a miracle... and sometimes to recognize grace, as in "you shall do." And likewise the Roman style, and sometimes for the recognition of the Sages. Therefore He made it and wrote it according to the names of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and from the levels which are like a dream... 

The things like "to speak" (L), "from you" (M), "as his strength" (K), "as the time" (K). And likewise, all of them are from the actions, they are like jewelry, such as the letters **Het (ח), Tet (ט), Nun (נ), Ayin (ע), Qof (ק)**. Therefore He made **Tet (ט)** from the actions corresponding to the ten doubles and eight letters... and the bodies corresponding to the seven <term>Sefirot</term> <note>The divine emanations through which the world was created.</note>. He preceded the business of the opening... afterwards all of them with intention... every three letters three times in the count of the fifths as explained in the first chapter. 

He said at the beginning: **Aleph** comes before **Yud**, and after that **Kaf**, and then **Gimel**, as it is found in the count of the Sabbath. The "houses" <note>letter combinations</note> are hairs in strength for the interpretation that the Holy One, Blessed be He, gave to them and took their dust for her. And the master of all that precedes joined all the other letters. And to act with the letters—they are as the Holy One, Blessed be He, made with them two thousand years before they were written.

# Our Rabbi Saadia Gaon, of blessed memory

The pillars [extend] above and below, inward and outward, east and west, north and south.

---

### Chapter Four

**Seven** double letters: *Bet, Gimel, Dalet, Kaph, Pe, Resh, Tav* <note>In the *Sefer Yetzirah*, these seven letters are called "doubles" because they can take a *dagesh* (a dot indicating a hard sound) or remain "weak" (a soft sound). While modern Hebrew usually only recognizes three or six, this ancient system includes the letter *Resh*.</note>. The explanation for why they are called "doubles" is that they are sometimes emphasized and sometimes soft. Because they contain permutations, they are the foundation for things in the world that have opposites. Through their "hard" emphasis, the strong things were created, such as Life, Peace, Wealth, Seed <note>Refers to progeny or fertility.</note>, Grace, Dominion, and Wisdom. Through their "soft" state, their opposites were created: the language of Death, Poverty, and so on. Their transformations occur through the force of the seven active planets: *Shabbatai* (Saturn), *Tzedek* (Jupiter), *Ma’adim* (Mars), *Hammah* (the Sun), *Nogah* (Venus), *Kokhav* (Mercury), and *Levanah* (the Moon) <note>original: "שצ"מ חנכ"ל" (Sh-Tza-M Cha-Na-Ka-L), a traditional Hebrew acronym for the seven classical planets.</note>, which are explained further below. Their sphere is beneath the *Teli* <note>The *Teli* is a mysterious cosmological concept often translated as the "Celestial Dragon" or the "Axis Mundi." It was thought to be the mechanism that suspends the spheres in space.</note>, which is like a scorpion or a "crooked serpent." It is composed of eight "moistures"—moisture, water, and spittle—for the Holy One, blessed be He, made for it a "tongue and a tail." He planted it in the fourth heaven, in the "Abode of the Sun" <note>original: 'מעון השמש' (Me'on HaShemesh).</note>. Its curve is at its center, as we will explain later with God’s help.

The *Teli* rises in the world like a king on his throne. All the stars and zodiac signs are strengthened by it. It is like a permanent king, leading toward both good and evil. It guides those seven planets and moves everything, bringing the zodiac signs from the west and from the west to the east. It is what causes the stars to revolve and return; it is what directs them to walk a straight path. By its hand, the seven planets roll—which are the 365 [degrees] in the sphere. Thus, it is stated below: "Three over seven." Each of the seven planets has a "company" among the stars, and those wise in the stars <note>Astrologers or astronomers.</note> recognize them. The seven planets rule over the twelve zodiac signs. As it is written below: "Seven over twelve."

The seven planets and their spheres wrap around the spheres of the twelve zodiac signs. This is comparable to two wheels: a small wheel with seven "thighs" <note>Likely referring to spokes or supports.</note> and inside it a large wheel with twelve. The sphere of seven overlaps with the sphere of twelve like a horse <note>Possibly a metaphor for how one gear or wheel "rides" or drives another.</note>. This is the path of the twelve zodiac signs. However, as for the seven doubles, their path varies because one star may have greater strength than its fellow. Sometimes the path of a "good" star aligns against a "bad" zodiac sign, and a transformation occurs, resulting in evil. Sometimes the opposite happens: the path is in a good sign, but its orbit moves into a bad sign. A person born under that sign might have a good start but a bad end, or vice versa. If "virtuous" stars are in one group, they balance each other—such as Life against Death—and Peace will prevail. By this, the wise men of the stars know how many times a person will fall ill and when they will die. Yet, even if the zodiac sign is strong, there is a "Faithful King," a Master who rules over them all. He saves [the person] through prayer and repentance, for not everything is dependent on one's zodiac sign. As our Sages of blessed memory said: "Israel has no *mazal*" <note>A famous Talmudic phrase (Shabbat 156a) meaning that the Jewish people are not bound by fixed astrological fate but are subject to direct Divine providence based on their actions.</note>.

**Six** edges in the world: "Six." The explanation corresponds to the six directions: the four winds <note>The cardinal directions: North, South, East, West.</note>, as well as Above and Below, with the Holy Temple in the center. The explanation of "the six in the world are six" refers to the six sides of the six orders <note>Possibly the six orders of the Mishnah or the six spatial dimensions.</note>. These were created "in it and not in it" <note>A paradoxical phrase from the *Sefer Yetzirah* suggesting the directions are part of the divine space but distinct from God's essence.</note> against the six edges, which are six pillars made of water and air that cannot be grasped. These pillars are: two to the east, two to the west, one to the south, and one to the north. Between the pillars are seven "divisions" called orders. In the north and the south, there are pillars called the "Poles of the North" and the "Poles of the South." The order of the sphere is within them, and it revolves within them from east to west forever. Therefore, the six which are the "order" never move, except for the Pole. Thus, the "Wagon" <note>The Big Dipper / Ursa Major.</note> is always seen in the north, and the "Scorpion" <note>The constellation Scorpius.</note> is in the south. However, the seven zodiac signs within them...

While the previous page discussed the "Seven Doubles" (Chapter Four), this page provides the philosophical and cosmological foundation of the "Three Mothers"—the letters Aleph, Mem, and Shin—which represent the primary elements of the universe.</meta>

->Our Rabbi Saadia Gaon, of blessed memory<-

And below it is explained: No—all those who entice, for there they are like the banners, each man by his standard and at his station.

## Chapter Three

**Three names** <note>original: "שמות" (*Shemot*); Saadia often uses "Names" and "Mothers" interchangeably here to refer to the primary letters Aleph, Mem, and Shin.</note> were explained above. For this reason they are called "Names," because they are the essence of all the "generations" (the origins) of the heavens and the earth. The concept was explained above as the language of a thing that is inclusive and intertwined. **Three mothers** are a great and wondrous mystery <note>original: "סוד מופלא" (*Sod Mufla*).</note>. The explanation of this "wondrous mystery" refers to the Name, which is the Great Name of God, etc., and one can use them through their preservation. To walk upon the sea and to stretch out like a natural garment; he explained therein that one [letter] strengthens itself to become the "face" (the primary aspect).

As explained nearby: **Fire and Water** emerge. Explanation: In Chapter Two, it was said that fire is above and its height is upward. And when it is said there that "his likeness is water," it refers to water below, with the **Air of Peace** <term>Air of Peace: The element of Spirit/Air (Ruach) that balances the opposing forces of Fire and Water</term> in between them. Half of it is from the nature of Fire, which is hot, and half of it is from the nature of Water, which is cold. These [letters/elements] are divided into male and female.

He explains that **Fire** is male, rising upward and ascending; its heat is also greater above than below. The matter is "Holy to the Fire." **Water** is female and descends downward. Therefore, when the water is inside the cloud—which is made of fire—and the cloud's nature is to ascend according to the law of Fire, the Water longs to descend according to the nature of the female. It is the **Spirit** (Air), acting as the mediator between them, that maintains the male and female aspects and carries them up to the clouds, like the flash of water high up to the firmament. However, the Spirit is never truly above the clouds. 

On this, he explained that what we hear as lightning and thunder is actually from the "compulsion" of the female [element]. From this comes the movement of the winds to lead the clouds; they make a sound like the sound of a staff striking a copper vessel. This is an inclusive thing. This compulsion only happens when there is a Divine decree; He compels and strikes the earth and has mercy upon it because it [the earth] thirsts for water. Therefore, there is no peace in the rainy season—neither thunders nor lightnings. 

There is a hint here that all things are divided into male and female. He explains that every thing in the world—whether stars, or constellations, or any creature in the world—exists through heat and its likeness; they are all male and female. This is also true in the *Sefirot* <note>The ten creative emanations or spheres in Jewish mysticism.</note> and in Thought.

**Three Mothers** are: **Heavens** were created first from **Fire**. He explains from these that it [the heaven] emerged from the water as explained in the chapter. **Air** <note>original: "אויר" (*Avir*), often used for the atmosphere or the element of Spirit.</note> was created from **Spirit**. From the spirit of the living voids, Spirit was made, which is the Air in between the Fire and the Water. It possesses both their natures, being both hot and humid.

In the **Soul**, the whole was created from Fire <note>Likely referring to the 'Head' or the intellect, often associated with the element of Fire in this system.</note>, to give understanding so that your eyes of thought shall not see Air upon it; it is like a measure that nourishes them, telling you that it has "voids" within. The **Belly** is from Water, and it is the coldness from the food and drink of the body.

**Three Mothers** were explained above as the ten forms of their shape. He engraved them in their preservation and permuted them <note>Permutation (*Tziruf*) is the mystical practice of re-ordering letters to create different spiritual or physical effects.</note>, so that sometimes the *Shin* comes first, sometimes the *Mem*, and sometimes the *Aleph*. He formed through them, by means of permutation and preservation: three in the World, three in the Year, and three in the Soul.

He proceeds to explain: How did He make the *Mem* king, etc., and bind a crown to it? He explains that He gave it dominion and placed it at the head of their word. He permuted them one with another, connecting the letters to each other. Corresponding to the first is **Fire**, and the second is **Air**. Likewise, He made *Mem* and *Aleph* kings, as male and female.

Explanation: Know that there is "Air" in the world that generates and grows males, and there is also that which grows females, whether in fruits or in creatures. There is a saturated beast that gives birth and is fruitful with both males and females. So too in the World: at the end, by the "speech" of the word, if the *Aleph* is not adjacent at its end, it is male. And they are the rings of <meta>catchword: the donkeys (or "the heavy matters")</meta>

# Our Rabbi Saadia Gaon, of blessed memory

...to refine my goodness; and "perform a sign for me for good" <note>original: "עשה עמי אות לטובה" (*Aseh imi ot le-tovah*); a reference to Psalm 86:17.</note> according to the way of my folly. # Our Rabbi Saadia Gaon, of blessed memory

From the North it shone toward the West, and they [the stars/spheres] sparkled within them, revolving forever from East to West. For this reason, the waters within them—corresponding to the expanse of the celestial sphere <term>Sphere: *Galgal* (גלגל), referring to the rotating celestial shells that medieval thinkers believed carried the planets and stars.</term>—are led toward the East. Therefore, all rivers and springs emerge in the East and travel to the West toward the sea, and from there they return to their course. So too is the Deep <term>Deep: *Tehom* (תהום), the primordial or subterranean waters.</term> moved by the sphere and returns. They are kneaded with their dwellings beneath them, surrounding the Deep, for the world is like a dome <note>original: "ככפה" (*ke-kippah*); a common medieval description of the heavens as a protective dome over the Earth.</note> and the revolving sphere [moves] in the path of its embrace. For the world is... <unclear>round and oval</unclear> at the North Pole <note>original: "קוטב צפון" (*kotev tzafon*)</note>, and its praise is revealed to all those in the North forever...

The masters of the constellations <note>original: "חכמי המזלות" (*chachmei ha-mazalot*); the astronomers or astrologers of the era.</note> recognize the Wagon and its height, which encompasses from the North-Eastern corner by way of the world's edge at the pole... until the North-Western side... stretching slightly toward the South until the Eighth Sphere <note>The sphere of the fixed stars in medieval Ptolemaic cosmology.</note>, which is the primary one. Therefore, the sand and the custom... are like the northern regions around [the pole], and from the East... to all its northern parts beneath the world. In the East, it is supported... to every southern coldness, for the world is established like the northern regions.

Therefore, the world is built toward the North, because no creature can withstand the Southern side because of the great heat of its source. <note>Medieval geographers often believed the equatorial or southern regions were "torrid zones" too hot for human habitation.</note> Five waves are open to... as will be said later. By the strength of the world, a northern wind blows, and there is a very deep pit there. Therefore, a great [land] is near it, and it is exceedingly large. During the seasons of Tammuz <note>The summer month (June/July).</note> at noon, when the sun is in the South, no man has any shadow at all... in the pit... and from the northern region to the end of the three... <unclear>distant star</unclear>... and distant sight... until the West.

Two for Spain <note>original: "ספרד" (*Sepharad*).</note>... a second time... the seventh [clime] rises... in the North and at its end. The temple of the corner is inside, leaning toward the West in the direction of Persia <note>original: "פרס" (*Paras*).</note>. It is like a round circle that encompasses the wind of the world's sphere. In its eyes and its orders, it is written in the Deep from every side. But this is not for [human] thought; this is the matter. The spirit is like layers upon layers <term>Layers: *Terafref* (טרפרף); likely referring to "curtains" or atmospheric "flaps" that separate the earthly realm from the divine.</term> up to the top. In its place, He awaits the prayer of His servants... to the lower layer, and in that place, they are like the <unclear>boundary</unclear> of the world to the upper layer... and eyes [raised] to the heights.

<meta>This page continues the exposition of Saadia Gaon's commentary on the *Sefer Yetzirah*. Following the discussion of the "Mother letters" (Aleph, Mem, Shin), this section details the "Double letters" (Bet, Gimel, Dalet, Kaf, Pe, Resh, Tav) and the "Simple letters," explaining how the Creator used them to fashion the cosmos, the calendar, and the human body.</meta>

## Our Rabbi Saadia Gaon, of blessed memory

And he explained in every account and everything within them: He made the letter **Bet** [ב] king, and tied a crown to it, and permuted the letters one with another. He combined them through the "male of loving-kindness" <note>This refers to a Kabbalistic or grammatical categorization where certain letters or qualities are considered masculine/active.</note> and designated them **BGD KPRT** <note>original: "בגד כפרת" - a mnemonic for the seven "double" letters: Bet, Gimel, Dalet, Kaf, Pe, Resh, Tav, which historically had two pronunciations, hard and soft.</note>. He formed with it Saturn in the universe, the Sabbath in the year, the mouth in the soul, and its opposite is life <note>The text suggests "Life" is the quality associated with the letter Bet, and its "opposite" (traditionally Death) is the permutation.</note>. 

He made the letter **Gimel** [ג] king, and tied a crown to it, and permuted the letters one with another. He combined them through the "male of loving-kindness" and designated them **BGD KPRT**. He formed with it Jupiter in the universe, life in the year, and the right eye in the soul; its quality is peace and its opposite is war. 

He made the letter **Dalet** [ד] king, and tied a crown to it, and permuted the letters one with another. He combined them through the "male of loving-kindness" and designated them **BGD KPRT**. He formed with it Mars in the universe, the [unclear] on the Sabbath in the year <note>original: "וכ' בשבת בשנה" - possibly a shorthand for a specific day or cycle.</note>, and the left eye in the soul; its quality is wisdom and its opposite is folly. 

He made the letter **Kaf** [כ] king, and tied a crown to it, etc., and designated them **BGD KPRT**. He formed with it the Sun in the universe, the third day of the week in the year, and the right nostril in the soul; its quality is wealth and its opposite is poverty. 

He made the letter **Pe** [פ] king, etc., and designated them **BGD KPRT**. He formed with it Venus in the universe, the fourth day of the week in the year, and the left nostril in the soul; its quality is seed <note>Meaning offspring or fertility.</note> and its opposite is desolation. 

He made the letter **Resh** [ר] king, etc., and designated them **BGD KPRT**. He formed with it Mercury in the universe, the fifth day of the week in the year, and the ear <note>Likely the right ear, to correspond with the pairs below.</note> in the soul; its quality is grace and its opposite is ugliness. 

He made the letter **Tav** [ת] king, etc., and designated them **BGD KPRT**. He formed with it the Moon in the universe, the seventh day of the week in the year <note>The Sabbath.</note>, and the left ear in the soul; its quality is dominion and its opposite is slavery. 

He set thirty-two paths <note>The 32 Paths of Wisdom consisting of the 10 Sefirot and 22 Hebrew letters.</note>; the world is simple and open, for the end of the thirty is life. Aside from Him, the universe is a thing unto itself, the year is a thing unto itself, and the soul is a thing unto itself. Their testimony witnesses that He is One, there is no second to Him, and there is no end to His kingdom, etc.

## Chapter Five

# Twelve
simple letters He explained. For this reason they are called "simple" and not "double," because in their essence they do not have soft or hard pronunciations <note>Unlike the BGD KPRT letters which change sound with a *dagesh* (dot), these twelve letters have a single sound.</note>. And when they are joined with other letters, they may have hard or soft qualities, and therefore they have opposites like the **BGD KPRT** letters. 

And these are their opposites: 
- The opposite of sight is blindness.
- The opposite of hearing is deafness.
- The opposite of smell is the loss of scent.
- The opposite of speech is muteness.
- The opposite of eating is hunger.
- The opposite of sexual intimacy is eunuchism.
- The opposite of action is affliction.
- The opposite of walking is lameness.
- The opposite of movement is rage.
- The opposite of laughter is anger.
- The opposite of thought is suffering.
- The opposite of sleep is wakefulness.

These letters are: **He** [ה], **Vav** [ו], **Zayin** [ז], **Het** [ח], **Tet** [ט], **Yod** [י], **Lamed** [ל], **Nun** [נ], **Samekh** [ס], **Ayin** [ע], **Tzadi** [צ], **Qof** [ק]. 

He explained them as corresponding to the exiles. The exile of Egypt is according to the twelve Zodiac signs <term>Mazzalot</term> <note>The Hebrew word for the signs of the Zodiac.</note> that were created from the twelve simple letters. 

**He, Vav, Zayin, Het, Tet, Yod, Lamed, Nun, Samekh** — such was the settlement of Egypt. How so? From the Generation of the Dispersion <note>The Generation of the Tower of Babel.</note>... and it is written: "and the memory of sevenfold like an eagle before the advisor of Egypt." And there are those of our Sages who interpreted this in the tractate *Sukkah*: "No verse departs from its plain meaning." The Generation of the Dispersion was upon the districts of Egypt... out of the power of all, there were ten, and afterwards five remained. The settlement of Egypt lasted five years, and therefore the year is the numerical value <term>Gematria</term> of **He, Vav, Zayin, Het, Tet, Yod, Lamed, Nun, Samekh, Ayin, Tzadi, Qof**. 

According to their stations, the Zodiac signs are called by names: 
- **He** [ה]: Aries [The Ram].
- Taurus [The Ox].
- Gemini [The Twins].
- Cancer [The Crab]. 

And just as one gazes at Aries, Taurus, Gemini, and Cancer... **Zayin** [ז]: Jacob, seventy souls and twelve tribes, and all of them through Joseph, and all of them are "soul." And the houses of their sons and daughters and his servants and their mothers. The quality of "sexual intimacy" <note>One of the twelve qualities listed above.</note> corresponds to Jacob, who was made weak before Esau, who went down to Egypt. 
**Mem** [מ]: Cancer. The exile of Egypt is associated with Cancer.

## Our Rabbi Saadia Gaon, of blessed memory

...to the spleen. And the temperament of the kidneys arouses the desire for intercourse <note>Medieval physiology often linked the kidneys and the "lower" organs to reproductive drive.</note> which is constricted; one must soften those who are constricted. And the [unclear] house is suspended, one head of it hanging to the womb of the cycle. And Cancer [is formed] in the kidneys. The spleen is cold <note>In the humoral system, the spleen was the seat of "Black Bile," which is cold and dry.</note> and the teacher <note>possibly a corruption of "nature" or "bitterness"</note> of the bile is cold and dry. When the spleen is attached to the "servant" <note>original: "המשמש" — likely referring to the stomach or the digestive heat</note>, the heat of the food is tempered slightly lest it be burned by the heat of the Yellow Bile, which is hot and dry. And from the moisture, the liver acts to bring down [fluids] to the stomach and the small intestines, and to soften the strength of the rectum. The spleen is like a small lyre <note>original: "כנבל קטרה" — likely comparing the anatomical shape of the spleen to a kithara or harp</note> under the ribs of the urinary tract. The liver is entirely closed except for the expectation of urine <note>unclear; likely referring to the gallbladder or urinary ducts</note>, and the spleen is stretched and nourished by everything through the channel of the waters that exit from it, flowing with the secret of the Natures. Therefore, when the masters of the Natures [are balanced]:
- **Blood** is hot and moist.
- **Yellow Bile** is hot and dry.
- **Phlegm** <note>original: "ליחה"</note> is cold and moist.
- **Black Bile** is cold and dry.

Therefore, when a person is composed of these four elements, he is in good health. The urine flows; the dream is clear <note>original: "חלום סחור" — possibly meaning "circulating" or "clear/white"</note>; from phlegm comes water. The temperament changes based on the power of one humor riding over its fellow; and he is blessed who gives him something to diminish it <note>i.e., medicinal balance</note>. There is a prayer between the urine and the pure state, resulting from the composition of the four natures. And just as one examines the causes of illnesses, know that there arise in the body and are revealed through it the four seasons. Through them, the illnesses are manifest, and the seasons change according to the four natures:

- **The Spring Season** [Nisan] is hot and moist, and in it the Blood shall rule forever over everything, and its dominion is over the three signs <note>Aries, Taurus, and Gemini</note>.
- **The Summer Season** [Tammuz] is hot and dry, and in it the Yellow Bile shall rule forever over everything, and its dominion is over its companions <note>Cancer, Leo, and Virgo</note>.
- **The Winter Season** is cold and moist, and in it Phlegm shall rule to overcome its companions. 

The temperaments and their compositions will follow their nature during sunny days and rainy days, according to their law and judgment. Also, from the point of the body's nature, they will be found according to their nature. If the times of the year are not balanced—for instance, if the heat of the Summer season is drawn into the Period of Nisan <note>The spring equinox</note>—then Phlegm will increase and the Blood will not be strengthened in its power. And if the Summer Period is soft in heat and dry... then Phlegm will grow and be cold like it, and the power of Phlegm will be diminished and mixed. Through the power of the hidden essence of moisture, the nature of man is lightened from all parts of the body, for it is divided also in the mind, like the consumption of food, and it is separated from its places; for the place of food ceases, and the powers are established on their dregs. It is like a wick that flickers when the oil is finished from the lamp. Then the humor of Black Bile mixes with Phlegm to ascend to the head and is remembered in the vessels of the mind.

And if the temperament and its law are in cold and dryness, then the Black Bile of its kind will grow in the [unclear] and the blood will fall, and the Phlegm will help to diminish it, and dreams will be mixed with dryness. And if the Period of Nisan <note>Spring</note> increases in its temperament, then the Blood will increase, and it is proper to let blood <note>Bloodletting was a common medical practice to reduce "excess" blood during the spring.</note> lest it become heavy upon the secret of the foundations to stir the natures.

Behold, I have spread out these things for you in the languages of Rome <note>Latin</note>, Persia, and [unclear] <note>original: "וחצ"פ" — perhaps a shorthand for Arabic or another language</note>. The Period of Nisan <note>The Spring Equinox</note> is the time of moisture for the year; it lasts from the beginning of Nisan for thirty days, nine hours, and 648 parts <note>A *helek* (part) is 1/1080 of an hour in Hebrew timekeeping</note>. And so the one after it follows. Every day is seven and a half hours <note>unclear; likely referring to the shift in the seasonal clock</note>, the total reaching 30 [days] 9 [hours] and [648] parts.

- **The Period of Tammuz** [Summer Solstice] begins with **Cancer**, followed by **Leo**, and followed by **Virgo**.
- **The Period of Tishrei** [Autumn Equinox] likewise moves through [Libra], **Scorpio**, and **Sagittarius**.
- **The Period of Tevet** [Winter Solstice] moves through [Capricorn], **Aquarius**, and **Pisces**, neither less nor more.

It is a tradition in our hands that there is no "leap" period or cutting except through the stars, and the star does not return to its place for seven years. And the portions of the temperament pass one over the other...

# Our Rabbi Saadia Gaon, of blessed memory

...and Tishrei in Tevet and Kislev in the soul. He caused the letter *Bet* to reign in the head and *Kof* at the end, and within it [are calculations] <note>The text here contains cryptic letter-combinations and gematria shorthand typical of Sefer Yetzirah commentaries.</note>. And He settled Scorpio in the world, Marheshvan in the year, and the womb <note>original: "בטן" - literally belly or womb</note> in the soul. He caused the letter *Ayin* to reign in the head and *Kof* at the end... and He settled Capricorn in the world, Tevet in the year, and the left hand in the soul. He caused the letter *Tzadi* to reign in the head and *Kof* at the end... and He settled Aquarius in the world, Shevat in the year, and the right foot in the soul. He caused the letter *Kof* to reign in the head and *Kof* at the end... and He settled Pisces in the world, Adar in the year, and the left foot in the soul.

He distributed twelve leaders, each according to his service. The **Brain** is the highest; it is as if hot and moist, and planted within living skins <note>Referring to the meninges, the membranes enveloping the brain.</note>, dwelling between two membranes. Therefore, a person may die because of [injury to] one of these membranes. The **Soul** <note>original: "נשמה" (Neshamah)</note> is hot and pure; it is rested like a wick within a lamp, and its place of dwelling is opposite the foundations of the world. From the lungs to the head, it depends on oil to give it actual life-force. It sits in the "pot" of the brain. 

The **Heart** and the **Lungs** establish the chain of the soul, which is like a burning fire; for the "Lamp of the Lord is the soul of man, searching all the inner rooms of the belly" <note>A quote from Proverbs 20:27.</note>. If not for the cooling of the light of the world <note>Likely referring to the air/breath</note> from the lungs to the head, the flame would immediately burn the brain. And if not for the warmth of the brain, the moisture of the coldness of the lungs—which is like water—would extinguish the soul, which is like fire. By this balance, a man stands in his time and his tranquility, and the happenings of the cold do not overcome the brain. The soul burns so that it may return to the heart and the kidneys. 

**Wisdom** and **Understanding** are in the heart. The lungs fan the heart like a bellows that embraces the one who eats <note>The "eater" here refers to the metabolic heat or the "fire" of the heart.</note>; its coldness cools the heart and its flame. Its internal heat inflames it like the boiling of a dream-broth, while the lungs rest to soothe the heart and the brain. The heart, the cord of the tongue, the opening of the throat, the base, and the lips <unclear>what</unclear> are the thoughts of the heart. 

The **Liver** prepares the food for the heart and sends its vitality to it. The **Red Bile** <note>Yellow bile, often called "Red" in medieval Hebrew texts</note> is between the body and its purity and its digestion, and it cancels out his eating <note>Likely referring to the regulation of appetite or digestion</note>. The **Stomach** <note>original: "המכס" - likely a corruption of "המסס" (omasum/stomach)</note> is the "spitting cauldron," called *caldaria* <term>in the vernacular</term> <note>original: "קלדירה" (caldaria) - Latin/Romance for a boiling pot or cauldron.</note>; within it is the milk <note>Perhaps referring to chyle, the milky fluid of digestion</note> which is the protector of the dream. Therefore, when a boil corrupts within it, by the counsel of the "frying pan" written concerning the milk <note>A metaphorical reference to digestive heat</note>, it is a vessel of food that burns the vessel. Because of this, a man becomes parched... and like a vessel of food within the stomach, it is treated by the counsel of the "multitude of waters" written concerning the milk, directing its vitality. Therefore, the milk passes away from an abundance of food and hidden things. 

The **Gizzard** <note>original: "קרקען" (korkeban)</note> grinds and cooks all around. The Holy One, blessed be He, created the scab of the milk <note>unclear; likely a digestive lining</note> and it clarifies between the food and the waste for his rest; it sends the "living milk" to the intestines. According to nature, they call the rectum *scoria* <term>in the vernacular</term> <note>original: "סקורין בלעז שבתיהו" - possibly related to 'scoria' (dross/waste) or 'sabate' (clog/shoe).</note> to remove the sickness and the waste of the food through the openings, and it sends [the essence] to the liver. 

The liver divides the "dream" into four: the waste goes to the heart and is turned into blood, hot and moist; and the milk <note>chyle</note> is distributed to all his parts for the spirit of life and to all the upper and lower pulses. The [stomach] sends the spirit with the "cloud of the tax" <note>A metaphorical term for digestive vapors</note>, and the "enclosure of the security" in its spirit mixes with the moisture of the lungs and they grow strong. The spirit and the smoke rise together to the chest  Hebrew <note>Stylized shorthand for 'Baruch Hu' or a similar blessing.</note> through small chambers <note>original: "כקביס" - small measures or vessels</note> that descend from the bed to the "burnt offering" of the throat. There are thirty chambers like the foreskin of the throat, and they are attached to the inside of the brain. Know that in the brain, the [fluids] are dragged from the "bed" through the mouth. Also, when you close your mouth, everything flows through the nose. Also, as by way of the moisture of the nostrils, it brings up spirit, scent, and smoke to the brain through the nasal chambers to moisten the brain; otherwise, it would be burned by the flame of the soul. [The Ten] Sefirot <note>original: "ספירות" - The ten divine emanations or "numbers" used by God to create the universe.</note> of Nothingness: Their vision is like a **flash of lightning**, and their limit has no end. His word is within them in "running and returning" <note>An allusion to Ezekiel 1:14, describing a pulsating or oscillating movement of divine energy.</note>, and at His command, they pursue like a whirlwind, and before His throne they prostrate themselves.

**Ten** Sefirot of Nothingness and twenty-two Foundation Letters: three "Mothers," seven "Doubles," and twelve "Simples," <note>The three Mother letters (Aleph, Mem, Shin), seven Double letters (those with two pronunciations), and twelve Simple letters correspond to elements, planets/days, and zodiac signs/months.</note> and a spirit/breath is within each one of them.

Two: Spirit from Spirit; He engraved and hewed within them the four winds of the heavens: East, West, North, and South, and a spirit is in each of them. Three: Water from Spirit; He engraved and hewed within them *Tohu* and *Bohu* <note>original: "תהו ובהו" - Chaos and Void/Desolation.</note>, mud and clay. He made them like a garden bed, He established them like a wall, He covered them like a ceiling, and He poured snow upon them and it became dust, as it is said: "For He says to the snow, 'Become earth.'" *Tohu* is the green line that encompasses the whole world; *Bohu*, these are the damp stones sunken in the abyss from which the waters emerge. 

Four: Fire from Water; He engraved and hewed within it the Throne of Glory, and the *Ophanim* <note>Wheel-angels.</note>, and the *Seraphim*, and the Holy Living Creatures <note>original: "חיות הקדש" - Hayot HaKodesh.</note>, and the Ministering Angels. From the three of them He established His dwelling, as it is said: "He makes His angels spirits, His ministers a flaming fire."

Five: He sealed the Height. He chose three simple letters and fixed them in His great Name **Y-H-W** <note>original: "יה"ו" - A three-letter permutation of the Divine Name.</note> and sealed with them the six directions. He turned upward and sealed it with **Y-H-W**. Six: He sealed the Depth; He turned downward and sealed it with **Y-H-W**. Seven: He sealed the East; He turned forward and sealed it with **H-Y-W**. Eight: He sealed the West; He turned backward and sealed it with **H-W-Y**.

### Chapter Four

Seven Doubles: *B-G-D K-P-R-T* <term>Double Letters: Seven Hebrew letters that can take both a hard and soft sound</term>. Their foundation is Life, Peace, Wisdom, Wealth, Seed <note>offspring</note>, Grace, and Dominion. They are used with two sounds, for they are doubles of permutations: *B-B*, *G-G*, *D-D*, corresponding to soft and hard, the form of the mighty against the weak, and they are permutations. The permutation of Life is Death; the permutation of Peace is Evil; the permutation of Wisdom is Folly; the permutation of Wealth is Poverty; the permutation of Seed is Desolation; the permutation of Grace is Ugliness; the permutation of Dominion is Slavery.

Seven Doubles: *B-G-D K-P-R-T*. Seven and not six; seven and not eight. Aimed at the six sides <note>the directions of the physical world</note> and the six orders, with the Holy Palace aimed exactly in the middle. "Blessed be the glory of the Lord from His place" <note>Ezekiel 3:12</note>; He is the place of the world, but the world is not His place, and He bears them all.

Seven Doubles: *B-G-D K-P-R-T*. How did He combine them? Two stones build two houses; three build six; four build twenty-four; five build one hundred and twenty; six build seven hundred and twenty; seven stones build five thousand and forty houses. <note>These are mathematical factorials: 2!, 3!, 4!, 5!, 6!, 7!. ## Chapter Two

Twenty-two foundation letters: three Mothers, seven Doubles <note>Letters that have two sounds, hard and soft.</note>, and twelve Simples. All of them are engraved with the voice, hewn with the breath, and fixed in the mouth in five places:

2. *Bet, Vav, Mem, Pe* <note>Labials: formed at the lips.</note>
3. *Gimel, Yod, Kaph, Qoph* <note>Palatals: formed against the palate.</note>
4. *Dalet, Tet, Lamed, Nun, Tav* <note>Linguals: formed by the tongue and teeth.</note>

They are tied to the tip of the tongue like a flame. *Aleph, Chet, He, Ayin* are used at the end of the tongue and the throat. *Bet, Vav, Mem, Pe* are between the lips and at the tip of the tongue. *Gimel, Yod, Kaph, Qoph* are cut upon the third of the tongue. *Dalet, Tet, Lamed, Nun, Tav* are used at the tip of the tongue with the voice. *Zayin, Samekh, Tsade, Resh, Shin* are between the teeth with the tongue lying flat and spread.

Twenty-two foundation letters are fixed in a sphere <term>Galgal: A mystical wheel or cycle of letters used for meditative permutations.</term> with two hundred and thirty-one gates. The sphere rotates forward and backward. This is the sign of the matter: if for good, it is above "pleasure" <note>original: "ענג" - Oneg (Pleasure).</note>; if for evil, it is below "plague" <note>original: "נגע" - Nega (Plague). Twenty-two letters: He engraved them and hewed them, weighed them and exchanged them. *Aleph* with all of them, permuting them to form the soul of every creature and the soul of all that is yet to be formed. # The Printers Said

Who is wise enough to understand the beauty of this text? We have waited to print this precious book in order to resolve the many variant versions of it, for it was great in both quantity and quality. From this, no small amount of variation arose between the details of its words, whether in the order of its sections—some appearing earlier or later—or in the language being missing or redundant. Because of this, a correct and knowledgeable investigation <note>original: "lezivnus" — likely a Latinate or Greek loanword used by printers for "examination" or "revision"</note> was required. 

Know that we have lacked nothing in achieving the perfection possible for us, even though we are but students of this craft <note>The printing press</note>, and this is our first time in print. We had few previous copies of the commentators before us. Therefore, we strengthened our arms to engrave with a pen of iron and lead <note>The metal type of the printing press</note> the choicest of its commentators: the commentary of the **Gaon Rabbeinu Saadia** <note>Saadia Gaon (882–942), a foundational philosopher</note>; the commentary of **Rabbi Eleazar of Worms** <note>1176–1238, a famous German mystic</note>; the commentary of the **Ramban** <note>Nachmanides (1194–1270)</note>; and the commentary of the **Ra'avad** <note>Abraham ben David (1125–1198)</note>. Along with the commentary of the **Rosh** <note>Asher ben Jehiel (1250–1327)</note>, [prepared by] J. Lazironi <note>Likely referring to the editor of the Mantua edition, Jacob ben Naphtali Gazolo/Lazirone</note>, may the memory of the righteous be a blessing. 

Though we have adapted to each part of them, we have not listed the merits of each specific section [in the table of contents], which belongs to J. Lazironi, to benefit the studious in what they see and improve. They will find the words of the wise "like goads" <note>A biblical reference to Ecclesiastes 12:11, meaning words that spur one to wisdom</note>. To ease the burden of the different versions, we have applied our hands a second time to print the book's text according to the variations found in it, so that the reader may run through it and gain insight from the source. 

<margin>Poem/Song</margin> We shall laud and praise Him who gave us the strength to bring forth this "good pearl" <note>A metaphor for the Sefer Yetzirah</note> which was [traditionally] hung around the neck of **Abraham our Father**, peace be upon him. May He continue to give us strength and might to produce many books without end, as is our heart's desire, to magnify the Torah and make it glorious. Amen.

# The Book of Formation

-> **Ten Leaders** <-

<margin>Ten leaders</margin> The law of ten: three, seven, and twelve. These are appointed over the **Dragon** <note>original: "Teli" — likely referring to the constellation Draco or the celestial axis</note>, the **Sphere** <note>original: "Galgal" — the cycle of the seasons or the celestial orbits</note>, and the **Heart**. The Dragon in the universe is like a king on his throne; the Sphere in the year is like a king in a province; the Heart in the soul is like a king in war.

<margin>General rule</margin> The sum of the matter: some of these join with others, and some are substitutes for others. These stand over against those, and those over against these. If these did not exist, those would not exist. All of them are attached to the Dragon, the Sphere, and the Heart. Furthermore, God made all things one against the other: good against evil, and evil against good. Good comes from good, and evil from evil. Good makes evil discernible, and evil makes good discernible. Good is hidden away for the righteous, and evil is hidden away for the wicked.

When **Abraham our father** arrived, he looked and saw, searched and understood, carved and hewed, combined and formed, and reflected. When his efforts succeeded, the Lord of All was revealed to him. He took him into His lap, kissed him on his head, called him "My beloved," and made a perpetual covenant with him and his descendants forever. Abraham believed in the Lord, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness. The glory of the Lord was called upon him, as it is written: *“Before I formed you in the womb, I knew you.”* He made a covenant with him between the ten fingers of his hands, which is the **Holy Tongue** <note>Hebrew</note>.

<margin>He tied</margin> He tied the twenty-two letters to his tongue, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, revealed the secret to him. He drew them in water, kindled them in fire, shook them in the wind, burned them in the seven stars, and led them through the twelve signs of the zodiac.

<margin>Air</margin> Air, wind, body, earth, cold and heat, the belly, the heavens, and the head: this is the mystery of **AMSh** <note>Aleph, Mem, Shin — the "Mother" letters representing Air, Water, and Fire</note>.

<margin>AMSh</margin> **Saturn** corresponds to the Sabbath and the mouth. **Jupiter** corresponds to the first day of the week <note>Sunday</note> and the right eye. **Mars** corresponds to the second day <note>Monday</note> and the left eye. **The Sun** corresponds to the third day <note>Tuesday</note> and the right nostril. **Venus** corresponds to the fourth day <note>Wednesday</note> and the left nostril. **Mercury** corresponds to the fifth day <note>Thursday</note> and the right ear.

<column-break/>

## The Secondary Letters

The pairs of letters: **Vav-Het, Tet-Yud, Lamed-Nun, Samekh-Ayin, Pe-Tzadi, Qof-Resh**. These are the twenty-two letters with which **Yah** <note>A name of God</note>, the Beloved of Hosts, the God of Israel, the Living God, El Shaddai, High and Exalted, who dwells forever and whose name is Holy, founded the world.

He has two names: **Yah** and **Beloved of Hosts** <note>original: "Yedid Tzevaot"</note>, which is a sign among our hosts. He is the God of Israel, a Prince before God. **Living God**: three things are called "life"—the Living God, living waters, and the Tree of Life. **El**: He is a "hard" <note>mighty/strong</note> God. **Shaddai**: because up to this point He said "Enough!" <note>original: "Dai" — a traditional wordplay suggesting God set limits to creation</note>. **High**: because He dwells at the heights of the universe and is high above all high ones. **Exalted**: because He carries and bears everything above and below. While all who carry are below and their burden is above, He is above and carries what is below; He carries and bears the entire world. **He dwells forever**: for His kingdom is for all eternity and has no interruption. **Holy is His name**: for He is holy, His ministers are holy, and to Him they say: *"Holy, holy, holy."*

<margin>Twelve</margin> Twelve are below, seven are above them, and three are above the seven. From the three He founded His dwelling place. All of them are hanging and standing as one—a sign for the One who has no second, a lone King in His universe, for He is One and His name is One.

<margin>Three</margin> Three "fathers" and their offspring, seven stars and their hosts, and twelve **diagonal boundaries** <note>term: diagonal boundaries (gevulei alakhson) — the twelve lines connecting the edges of the universe in mystical geometry</note>. The proof of the matter is found in faithful witnesses: the **Universe**, the **Year**, and the **Soul**.

The Universe: its <term>Sefirot</term> <note>divine emanations or numbers</note> are in ten. Its twelve are fire, wind, and water <note>representing the elements</note>; seven stars; and twelve constellations.

The Year: its Sefirot are in ten. Its three are cold, heat, and the temperate season <note>original: "ravayah" — saturation or balance</note>; its seven are the seven days of creation; its twelve are the twelve months.

The Soul: its Sefirot are in ten. Its three are the head, the body, and the belly; its seven are the seven gates <note>the openings in the head: eyes, ears, nostrils, mouth</note>; its twelve...

<summary>This page concludes the primary text of the Sefer Yetzirah, detailing the mathematical and linguistic structure of the cosmos and the covenant of Abraham. It establishes the foundational triad of Universe, Year, and Soul as witnesses to the divine order.</summary>

<meta>This page serves as a printer's afterword or preface to the 1562 Mantua edition of Sefer Yetzirah (The Book of Formation). It provides a list of significant Kabbalistic authorities and the titles of their works to establish the pedigree of the mystical tradition.</meta>

# The Printers Spoke
We, the printers, saw fit to record the names and the memory of the sages who wrote specifically about the **Book of Formation** <note>original: *Sefer Yetzirah*, the earliest extant book on Jewish mysticism</note> which I have transcribed. In truth, we say that the commentaries they composed regarding the **Wisdom of the Kabbalah** <term>Kabbalah: the ancient Jewish tradition of mystical interpretation of the Bible</term>, within which they incorporated portions of this small book... [were gathered] so that it may be known what is in our possession. We saw fit to present it before his eyes in its various streams and many forms. This was done so that the houses might be filled and overflow, to bring [these words] to their ears and restore their delights. Life for this day is entirely in His hand. And from the bread of the earth, one hungers for the Lord.
